en.d: Home page of the Cluster ERP wiki, with what the product is, one row per section, and how to read the pages.
en.b: This wiki documents Cluster ERP as the code implements it. It is the entry point for users, administrators, developers, and operators, and it links to every section. It does not repeat the content of the sections; each section index lists its own pages. What Cluster ERP is ¶ Cluster ERP is a modular enterprise resource planning system. The server is a FastAPI application built by create_app ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1287-1296 ) that stores its data in PostgreSQL through the asyncpg driver ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:841 ). Its business logic lives in 28 backend modules, counted as the 28 classes that subclass ModuleBase in src/cluster_erp/modules/*/module.py . The project's written engineering rules require modules to talk to each other only through the EventBus. Users work in a metadata-driven web app in webapp/ , which the server serves at /app ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1633-1644 ), or in a PySide6 desktop client in src/cluster_erp/desktop/ ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/main.py:139 ). Both clients build their screens from the metadata document that the server publishes at /api/v1/_meta ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1518 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:13 ), and both call the same HTTP API. Sections ¶ Section What it covers Start page Overview What Cluster ERP is, the architecture at a glance, and the repository layout Overview Platform core The backend core: server start-up, module lifecycle, EventBus, contracts, settings, database, ids, money, change history, and shared services Platform core Identity, access, tenancy, privacy, and licensing Sign-in, roles and permissions, attribute policies, field and row access, approvals, tenants, signup, data-subject requests, licensing, and the operator console Identity, access, tenancy, privacy, and licensing Web app platform The metadata-driven browser client in webapp/ and the server routes it relies on Web app platform Desktop client The PySide6 client in src/cluster_erp/desktop/ and how it renders server metadata Desktop client Business modules One page or folder per backend module, from parties to analytics Business modules API reference Conventions, authentication, errors, system and shared routes, and one page per backend module API reference Operations Environments, node installation, configuration, migrations, backups, tenants, and release Operations Contributing The engineering rules, quality gates, tests, the e2e battery, developer scripts, and writing wiki pages Contributing Decision records The binding design rules and the code that enforces each Decision records Reference The glossary and the list of related material outside the wiki Reference Intent assistant The built-in assistant that maps typed requests to API actions Intent assistant How to read this wiki ¶ Each page has one type: a tutorial teaches by doing, a how-to guide completes one task, a reference page lists facts, an explanation describes how and why a part works, a module page gives an overview of one backend module, an API page lists the endpoints of one router group, and an index page lists the pages of a section. Every statement about behaviour cites the code that shows it, as a path and line range such as src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:62 . The text "Not determined from code." marks a question that the code does not answer. A warning that starts with "Discrepancy." records a place where the code and the project's written engineering rules differ; it describes both sides and decides nothing. Every English page name.md has a Turkish twin name.tr.md in the same folder with the same structure, and the language switch moves between them. The last line of each page names the commit and the date that the page was checked against. Related pages ¶ Overview What is Cluster ERP Glossary Verified against commit 7793ff4 on 2026-11-09.

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the Cluster ERP server, its 28 modules, the EventBus, the web app, the desktop client, and the PostgreSQL database fit together.
en.b: This page shows the main parts of Cluster ERP and how they connect: one FastAPI server, 28 modules loaded into it, an in-process EventBus between the modules, two clients, and a PostgreSQL database. It is a map, not a manual. Each part links to the page that documents it. In short ¶ One FastAPI application is built by create_app and serves both the API and the web app ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1287 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1633-1644 ). The module registry discovers the packages under cluster_erp.modules and loads each one into the application ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:19 , src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:58-72 ). Modules talk to each other only through the EventBus and the contracts in core/contracts.py ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:43-49 , src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:1-6 ). Every request that touches business data gets one SQLAlchemy session on PostgreSQL through asyncpg ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:160-200 , src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:95-102 ). The web app and the desktop client draw their screens from module metadata served at GET /api/v1/_meta ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1518-1556 ). How it works ¶ The diagram shows the parts and the direction of the calls between them. flowchart LR browser["Browser: webapp/"] desktop["Desktop client: PySide6"] subgraph server["Server process"] app["create_app: FastAPI"] mw["Middleware stack"] shared["Shared routes: server/routes"] mods["28 modules: ModuleBase"] bus["EventBus"] core["core: models, metadata, change_history"] end db[("PostgreSQL")] storage[("File storage")] browser -->|"HTTP /app and /api/v1"| app desktop -->|"HTTP /api/v1"| app app --> mw mw --> shared mw --> mods mods <-->|"Event and Query contracts"| bus shared --> core mods --> core core --> db shared --> storage In prose, the diagram says the following: A browser loads the web app from /app and calls the API under /api/v1 . The desktop client calls the same API with httpx ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:7 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:86-87 ). Each request passes the middleware stack before it reaches a route. See request pipeline and middleware . Routes belong either to a module (prefix /api/v1/<module> , src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:36-38 ) or to the shared routes in src/cluster_erp/server/routes/ that create_app mounts directly ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1432-1450 ). See shared server routes . Modules exchange data through the EventBus with frozen dataclass contracts. See event bus and contracts reference . Modules and shared routes use the platform core in src/cluster_erp/core/ : the base model, metadata classes, change history, money helpers, search, and storage. Data lives in PostgreSQL. Uploaded files live in a storage backend, local disk or S3, created at start-up ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:65-75 ). See attachments, notes, and storage . Server and start-up ¶ python -m cluster_erp.server.main runs uvicorn with the factory flag ( src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:39-41 ). The lifespan context creates the database handle, the EventBus, the module registry, and the storage backend, then loads the modules and runs start-up passes ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:58-196 ). See server startup and app factory . Modules ¶ Each module subclasses ModuleBase and implements initialize , register_routes , register_events , shutdown , and get_metadata ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:61-74 ). See module lifecycle and the modules section . Metadata and the clients ¶ get_metadata returns a ModuleMeta object that describes screens, forms, lists, and actions ( src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:719 ). The server serializes all modules' metadata into one document with an ETag ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1518-1556 ). See metadata model , th

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: Product scope of Cluster ERP, its three clients, its 28 backend modules, and the global and multi-language intent stated in the project rules.
en.b: Cluster ERP is a modular enterprise resource planning system written in Python. This page describes its scope as the code defines it: the server, the three ways to reach it, and the 28 backend modules with one line each. It does not explain how the parts work together; see the architecture overview for that. In short ¶ The package is named cluster-erp , describes itself as a "Modular Enterprise Resource Planning System", and declares a proprietary license ( pyproject.toml:5-10 , LICENSE ). The server is a FastAPI application built by the factory create_app ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1287 ). Business features live in 28 modules under src/cluster_erp/modules/ . Each one subclasses ModuleBase ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:14 ). There are three clients: the web app in webapp/ , the PySide6 desktop client, and the HTTP API itself ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1633-1644 , pyproject.toml:86-88 ). The project rules aim at all countries and many languages. How it works ¶ The server process starts from python -m cluster_erp.server.main , which runs uvicorn with the create_app factory ( src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:39-41 ). At start-up the module registry loads every enabled module, and each module adds its routes, EventBus handlers, and screen metadata ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:32-56 ). The details are on server startup and app factory and module lifecycle . The three clients ¶ Client What it is Entry point Source Web app A vanilla JavaScript single-page app served by the same server at /app webapp/index.html src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1633-1644 Desktop client A PySide6 application installed through the desktop extra cluster-erp-desktop script, cluster_erp.desktop.main:main pyproject.toml:68-73 , pyproject.toml:88 HTTP API JSON routes under /api/v1/ , one prefix per module ModuleBase.api_prefix src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:36-38 Both clients draw their screens from the module metadata served at GET /api/v1/_meta ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1518-1556 ). The web app section and the desktop section document the clients. The 28 backend modules ¶ The table lists every folder in src/cluster_erp/modules/ (28 folders, counted with ls , excluding __pycache__ ). The description column quotes the module's own description property. The default value of enabled_modules lists the same 28 names ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:535-564 ). Module Description from code Source analytics Analytics: semantic layer, safe query generation, correctness gates src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/module.py:39 app_store App catalogue, entitlements and installs src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/module.py:36 auth Authentication, authorization (RBAC + ABAC), and approval chains src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/module.py:26 bom Bill of Materials, multi-level product structure management src/cluster_erp/modules/bom/module.py:30 calendars Working-time templates, calendars, and exceptions src/cluster_erp/modules/calendars/module.py:27 costing Cost analysis, labor/overhead rates, CBS, margin calculation src/cluster_erp/modules/costing/module.py:26 crm Customer and RFQ management with state machine and inbox src/cluster_erp/modules/crm/module.py:29 currencies Currency management and exchange rate tracking src/cluster_erp/modules/currencies/module.py:29 design_engineering Design lifecycle, versioning, and engineering change notes (ECN) src/cluster_erp/modules/design_engineering/module.py:26 documents Document management with versioning and approval workflows src/cluster_erp/modules/documents/module.py:29 fleet Fleet management: vehicles, machines, custom tracking src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/module.py:150 intranet Intranet: news, policies, directory, leave, requests, delivery src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/module.py:45 inventory Inventory management: warehouses, stock levels, batch and serial tracking src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/module.py:27 logs Activity and error logging src/cluster_erp/modules/logs/module.py:26 mail C

en.d: The shared core_attachments and core_notes tables, their services and routes, the upload policy, and the local, S3, and encrypted storage backends.
en.b: Any record in Cluster ERP can carry files and notes through two shared tables in the core. This page lists the tables, services, and routes in core/attachments.py , core/notes.py , server/routes/attachments.py , and server/routes/notes.py , the upload policy in core/upload_policy.py , and the storage backends in core/storage.py . The versioned document management of the documents module is a separate feature; see documents . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py ( Attachment , AttachmentService ), src/cluster_erp/core/notes.py ( Note , NoteService ), src/cluster_erp/core/upload_policy.py ( check_upload ), src/cluster_erp/core/storage.py ( StorageBackend , create_storage_backend ), src/cluster_erp/server/routes/attachments.py , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/notes.py Count: 8 attachment routes and 6 note routes (counted from the @router. decorators); 3 storage backend classes; 40 default allowed extensions Both tables link to their parent record by entity_type and entity_id , with no foreign key, so any entity can use them. Attachments ¶ core_attachments derives from BaseModel and adds these columns ( src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:51-63 ): Column Type Meaning Source code String(20) , unique Business code from the attachment sequence src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:54 , src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:123 entity_type String(50) Type of the parent record src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:55 entity_id UUID Id of the parent record src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:56 filename String(255) Stored name: a random hex name plus the cleaned extension src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:57 , src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:124-125 original_filename String(255) The name the user uploaded src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:58 content_type String(100) The content type declared by the upload src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:59 file_size BigInteger Size in bytes src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:60 storage_path String(500) Key in the storage backend src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:61 sha256 String(64) SHA-256 of the content src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:62 description Text Optional description src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:63 The storage key is attachments/<entity_type>/<entity_id>/<stored name> , prefixed with tenants/<tenant key>/ on a multi-tenant node ( src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:38-48 ). Downloads carry a Content-Disposition header built by safe_content_disposition , which strips quote, backslash, line-break, and semicolon characters from the ASCII name and percent-encodes the UTF-8 name ( src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:24-35 ). AttachmentService methods ( src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:88-206 ): Method Behaviour Source list_for_entity Live attachments of a record src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:93-104 get One live attachment src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:106-112 create Saves the bytes to storage, then inserts the row src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:114-143 update Changes description or original_filename src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:145-153 delete Sets deleted_at ; the stored file stays src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:155-161 bulk_delete Deactivates many through bulk_soft_delete src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:163-166 get_file_data Loads the bytes from storage src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:168-169 replace_file Deletes the old stored file, saves the new one, and updates the row src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:171-197 count_for_entity Number of live attachments of a record src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:199-206 Attachment routes ¶ The router prefix is /api/v1/attachments ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/attachments.py:27 ). Method and path Permission Purpose Source POST / (multipart: entity_type , entity_id , description , file ) attachment.create Upload a file src/cluster_erp/server/routes/attachments.py:62-85 GET /count/{entity_type}/{entity_id} attachment.read Count a record's files

en.d: The columns every Cluster ERP table inherits from BaseModel, ULID primary keys stored as UUID, and the sequence codes such as PTY-000001 and SO-2026-00001.
en.b: This page lists the columns that every business table inherits from BaseModel in core/models.py , how primary keys are generated in core/ulid.py , and how business codes are generated in core/sequence.py . Soft delete semantics are explained on soft delete and deactivation ; the change history on change history . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: src/cluster_erp/core/models.py ( Base , BaseModel ), src/cluster_erp/core/ulid.py ( new_ulid ), src/cluster_erp/core/sequence.py ( Sequence , next_code , next_value , seed_sequences ) Count: 11 columns on BaseModel (read from the class body); 69 entity prefixes in ENTITY_PREFIXES and 19 entity types in YEARLY_ENTITIES (counted from the dictionary and set literals) BaseModel columns ¶ Base is the SQLAlchemy declarative base ( src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:13-14 ). BaseModel is an abstract subclass that adds the columns below ( src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:17-78 ). Column Type Default Meaning Source id UUID new_ulid() Primary key; a ULID stored as a UUID src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:20-24 tenant_id UUID , nullable, indexed none Not set by any code in core/ , server/ , or modules/ (searched with grep -rn tenant_id ); its use is not determined from code src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:25-29 created_at timestamp with time zone now() on the server Creation time src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:30-34 created_by UUID , nullable none The acting user, stamped by the change-history hook on insert src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:35-38 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:216-224 updated_at timestamp with time zone now() , refreshed on update Last change time src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:39-44 updated_by UUID , nullable none The acting user, stamped by the change-history hook on update src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:45-48 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:225-226 deleted_at timestamp with time zone, nullable none NULL means active; a value means deactivated src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:49-57 deleted_by UUID , nullable none Who deactivated the record src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:58-61 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:249-250 deactivation_reason String(64) , nullable none A code from the deactivation reason catalogue src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:62-68 deactivation_note Text , nullable none Free text, required only when the reason demands it src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:69-72 version Integer 1 Row version for optimistic concurrency checks src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:73-78 version is not managed by SQLAlchemy's version counter: no __mapper_args__ declares one (searched with grep -rn __mapper_args__ ). Services raise it themselves; 140 lines in core/ and modules/ contain version + 1 (counted with grep -rn "version + 1" ), for example src/cluster_erp/modules/bom/boms/services.py:152 . check_version compares a client's version with the row and raises a 409 conflict on mismatch ( src/cluster_erp/core/errors.py:411-430 ). Some infrastructure tables subclass Base directly and do not carry these columns, for example core_change_history and audit_log ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:78-98 , src/cluster_erp/core/audit.py:15-69 ). Primary keys ¶ new_ulid() returns ULID().to_uuid() from the python-ulid package ( src/cluster_erp/core/ulid.py:8-14 , pyproject.toml:45 ). Its docstring states that the result is time-sortable and fits PostgreSQL's native uuid type ( src/cluster_erp/core/ulid.py:9-13 ). The change-history hook assigns the id of a new object before the flush, so the "create" history row carries the entity id ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:273-297 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:327 ). Business codes ¶ Business codes such as PTY-000001 come from the table core_sequences , one row per entity type ( src/cluster_erp/core/sequence.py:112-120 ). Column Type Meaning Source entity_type String(50) , unique The key, for example party src/cluster_erp/core/sequence.py:115 prefix String(10) The code prefix, for example PTY src/cluster_erp/core/sequence.py:116

en.d: The per-process cache version counters in core/cache_versions.py, the web app asset stamp in core/asset_stamp.py, and the HTTP caching of /app, /app/v, and /api/v1/_meta.
en.b: This page lists the caching mechanisms of the platform core: the version counters that let in-process caches notice writes from other workers, the asset stamp that makes web app files cacheable for a year, and the HTTP cache headers that server/app.py sets. The client-side use of the stamp is documented on web app overview . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: src/cluster_erp/core/cache_versions.py , src/cluster_erp/core/asset_stamp.py , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py (static mounts and /api/v1/_meta ) Count: 2 cache families; 2 static mounts; 1 cached metadata document Cache version counters ¶ The table core_cache_versions has one row per cache family with a version counter ( src/cluster_erp/core/cache_versions.py:25 , src/cluster_erp/core/cache_versions.py:39-43 ). Statement-level triggers from migration perf01 raise the counter on every insert, update, delete, or truncate of the family's tables ( src/cluster_erp/core/cache_versions.py:12-16 , migrations/versions/perf01_cache_versions.py ). Family Tables that move it Reader Source auth auth_roles , auth_role_permissions , auth_user_roles , auth_abac_policies , auth_permissions src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/auth_cache.py:69-77 src/cluster_erp/core/cache_versions.py:28-36 entitlement app_store_installs , app_store_licenses src/cluster_erp/server/entitlements.py:68-77 src/cluster_erp/core/cache_versions.py:36 version_statement(family) returns SELECT version FROM core_cache_versions WHERE name = :family and raises ValueError for an unknown family ( src/cluster_erp/core/cache_versions.py:46-51 ). The module docstring states the reason: the earlier stamp read the latest updated_at and the row count of each table on every guarded request, and a count is a full scan; one primary-key lookup costs the same at any table size ( src/cluster_erp/core/cache_versions.py:1-17 ). The lifetime of the authorisation cache is the setting auth_cache_seconds ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:317-320 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1308-1310 ). Asset stamp ¶ asset_stamp(root) returns the first 16 hexadecimal characters of a SHA-256 digest over the relative path, size, and modification time of every file under root , walked in sorted order ( src/cluster_erp/core/asset_stamp.py:30-42 ). The result is memoised for one second ( src/cluster_erp/core/asset_stamp.py:26 , src/cluster_erp/core/asset_stamp.py:45-54 ). PLACEHOLDER is __ASSET_STAMP__ ( src/cluster_erp/core/asset_stamp.py:25 ). webapp/index.html links its files under ./v/__ASSET_STAMP__/ . The application server replaces the placeholder with the computed stamp; on a node, nginx serves the files and the release tag is the stamp ( src/cluster_erp/core/asset_stamp.py:3-10 ). See reverse proxy . h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How core/change_history.py records every create, update, deactivate, activate, and delete of every mapped entity with actor, time, and a field-level diff.
en.b: Cluster ERP writes a history row for every change to every business entity, automatically, in the same transaction as the change. This page explains the capture in core/change_history.py , the value redaction in core/sensitive_fields.py , the legacy audit_log table in core/audit.py with its backfill in core/audit_backfill.py , and the migration evidence rows in core/migration_history.py . The screens that show the history belong to the logs module; see logs . In short ¶ One SQLAlchemy before_flush listener on Session captures every insert, update, and delete of every object whose class derives from Base ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:318-351 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:262-270 ). History rows go to core_change_history in the same transaction as the change ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:12-14 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:349-350 ). The actor and correlation id come from the request context, not from function arguments ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:320-321 ). Credential, special-category, and identifier columns keep their change record but lose their values ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:166-169 , src/cluster_erp/core/sensitive_fields.py:61-82 ). The module is imported by server/app.py so that the listener is registered before any session flushes ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:33-35 ). How it works ¶ The capture ¶ The flowchart shows what the listener does on each flush. flowchart TD start["before_flush"] --> ctx["read actor and correlation id"] ctx --> new["for each object in session.new"] new --> create["ensure id, stamp created_by, snapshot, action create"] ctx --> dirty["for each object in session.dirty"] dirty --> deact{"deleted_at NULL to value?"} deact -->|yes| stamp["stamp deleted_by, reason, note"] deact -->|no| diff["field diff"] stamp --> diff diff --> classify["stamp updated_by, classify action"] ctx --> del["for each object in session.deleted"] del --> snap["snapshot, action delete"] create --> add["session.add history rows"] classify --> add snap --> add add --> queue["queue TenantFieldValuesChanged"] In prose: The listener reads current_actor_id() and current_correlation_id() ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:320-321 ). For each new object it assigns the primary key if it is still empty, stamps created_by , and records a full snapshot with action create ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:324-329 ). For each changed object it first stamps deactivation data when deleted_at goes from NULL to a value, then computes the field diff. If the diff is empty, no row is written. Otherwise it stamps updated_by and classifies the action ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:331-342 ). For each deleted object it records a snapshot with action delete ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:344-347 ). It adds the history rows to the session and queues tenant-field events ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:349-351 ). Actions ¶ Action When Source create A new object is flushed src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:324-329 update A changed object that is not a deactivation or activation src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:213 deactivate deleted_at goes from empty to set, or is_active goes from true to false while deleted_at did not move src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:202-210 activate deleted_at goes from set to empty, or is_active goes from false to true src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:204 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:211-212 delete An object is physically deleted through the ORM src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:344-347 migration A data migration calls record_data_migration src/cluster_erp/core/migration_history.py:20-53 The table ¶ core_change_history has these columns: id , actor_id , correlation_id , entity_type (the class name), tabl

h: Background work started by a request
Why it is built this way
en.d: How Cluster ERP opens PostgreSQL connections, gives each request one SQLAlchemy session, publishes request context, and commits before the response is sent.
en.b: This page explains the database layer of Cluster ERP: the Database class in core/database.py , the request session dependency in server/dependencies.py , the request context in core/request_context.py , and the session helper for EventBus handlers in core/handler_session.py . It also explains when a request's transaction commits. Tenant routing is documented at mechanism level in multi-tenancy . In short ¶ Database wraps one async SQLAlchemy engine on asyncpg and one session factory with expire_on_commit=False ( src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:53-93 ). get_db_session gives each request one AsyncSession , publishes it in context variables, and rolls it back on error ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:160-200 ). The commit runs before the first response byte is sent, through a pre-response hook ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:163-190 , src/cluster_erp/server/middleware.py:25-57 ). The acting user, the correlation id, and the deactivation reason travel in context variables, not in function arguments ( src/cluster_erp/core/request_context.py:16-61 ). An EventBus handler joins the request's session when there is one, else it opens its own ( src/cluster_erp/core/handler_session.py:25-37 ). How it works ¶ The Database class ¶ Database(settings, *, database_url=None, pool_size=None, max_overflow=None) creates the engine with these options ( src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:69-80 ): Option Value Source URL database_url or settings.database_url ( postgresql+asyncpg://... ) src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:70 , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:838-843 echo settings.sql_echo src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:71 pool_size and max_overflow The arguments, else db_pool_size and db_pool_max_overflow src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:72-75 pool_pre_ping True src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:76 pool_recycle 3600 seconds src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:77 pool_timeout db_pool_timeout_seconds src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:78 Server setting plan_cache_mode = force_custom_plan on every connection src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:50 , src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:79 The tenancy layer builds one Database per tenant database with a smaller pool ( src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:62-68 ). Database.session() is an async generator that commits on success and rolls back on error; start-up passes use it ( src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:95-102 ). The request session ¶ get_db_session is the FastAPI dependency for every route that touches data. It does the following: Resolves the request's Database : the process default in single-tenant mode, the tenant's database in multi-tenant mode ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:104-157 ). Opens a session and publishes it, its task, and its database in three context variables ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:182-184 , src/cluster_erp/core/database.py:21-37 ). Opens the connection and injects the audit context ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:186-187 ). This sets five transaction-local PostgreSQL settings in one statement ( app.actor_id , app.ip , app.user_agent , app.session_id , app.correlation_id ), and sets the request context variables ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:34-72 ). Registers _commit_once as a pre-response hook when the middleware has created the hook list ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:188-190 ). Yields the session to the route, then calls _commit_once as a fallback for contexts without the middleware ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:191-192 ). On any exception, marks the hook as done and rolls back ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:193-196 ). Resets the context variables ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:197-200 ). _commit_once commits and then emits the events queued for after the commit ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:171-176 , src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:203-222 ). Commit timing ¶ The sequence diagram shows when the commit happens. sequenceDiagram participant C as Client participant M as Commit

en.b: This page lists the error classes and codes of Cluster ERP and how the server turns exceptions into HTTP responses. It covers core/errors.py , core/exceptions.py , and server/error_handler.py . The full list of codes with their causes, as a client sees them, is on API errors . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: src/cluster_erp/core/errors.py ( AppError , code constants, factories), src/cluster_erp/core/exceptions.py (platform exceptions), src/cluster_erp/server/error_handler.py ( install_error_handlers ) Count: 213 module-level string constants of the form NAME = "NAME" in core/errors.py (counted with grep -c -E '^[A-Z_0-9]+ = "' ), in 23 commented groups; 6 factory functions; 7 exception classes in core/exceptions.py (counted with grep -c "^class" ) The error body ¶ Every handled error returns a JSON body built by _build_body ( src/cluster_erp/server/error_handler.py:33-46 ): { "error" : { "code" : "<CODE>" , "message" : "<developer message>" , "trace_id" : "<YYMMDD-NNN>" , "details" : {} } } details is present only when it is not empty. The code is machine-readable, the client maps it to a localised text, and the message is an English developer string ( src/cluster_erp/core/errors.py:7-16 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How Cluster ERP modules exchange events and queries through the in-process EventBus in core/event_bus.py without importing each other.
en.b: The EventBus in src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py is the only channel through which Cluster ERP modules call each other. This page explains its two patterns, events and queries, how handlers run, and the rules around it. The list of every contract is on the contracts reference . In short ¶ An Event is a frozen, keyword-only dataclass with source_module and timestamp ; a Query is a subclass of Event ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:24-32 ). emit(event) runs every handler subscribed to the exact event type, in priority order, and returns their results as a list ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:83-96 ). query(query) runs the one handler registered for the exact query type and returns its result ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:98-102 ). A second query handler for the same type raises DuplicateQueryHandlerError ; a query without a handler raises QueryHandlerNotFoundError ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:73-81 , src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:98-101 ). The bus is in-process: one instance is created in the server lifespan and handed to every module ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:62 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:140 ). How it works ¶ Events and queries ¶ Pattern Call Handlers Result Error behaviour Source Event (fan-out) await bus.emit(event) Zero or more, registered with subscribe A list with one entry per handler that returned A handler exception is logged and skipped; other handlers still run src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:55-65 , src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:83-96 Query (point to point) await bus.query(query) Exactly one, registered with register_query_handler The handler's return value No handler raises QueryHandlerNotFoundError ; a handler exception propagates to the caller src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:73-81 , src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:98-102 Handlers are looked up by type(event) ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:84 , src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:99 ). A handler subscribed to a base class does not receive events of a subclass. The sequence diagram shows one event and one query. sequenceDiagram participant P as Producer module participant B as EventBus participant H1 as Handler A participant H2 as Handler B participant Q as Query handler P->>B: emit(PartyUpdated) B->>H1: await handler(event) H1-->>B: result or exception (logged) B->>H2: await handler(event) H2-->>B: result B-->>P: list of results P->>B: query(GetPartyById) B->>Q: await handler(query) Q-->>B: result B-->>P: result In prose: emit awaits each subscribed handler one after the other and collects the results; an exception in one handler is logged and does not stop the next. query awaits the single registered handler and returns its value to the caller. Priorities ¶ EventPriority has four values: LOW (0), NORMAL (1), HIGH (2), and CRITICAL (3) ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:17-21 ). subscribe defaults to NORMAL and keeps each handler list sorted from the highest value to the lowest ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:55-64 ). No module passes a non-default priority (searched with grep -rn "EventPriority\.\(HIGH\|LOW\|CRITICAL\)" over src/cluster_erp ). Events used to collect answers ¶ Several contracts are events although the caller wants answers, because more than one module must answer. The design note in src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2043-2056 states the reason: query() allows a single owner, while emit() returns every handler's return value. Examples are DescribeAnalyticsFacts , CollectSubjectData , DescribeDisplaySwitches , and ResolveEntityEmails ( src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2060 , src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2385 , src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2441 , src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:352 ). GET /api/v1/_switches merges the dictionaries returned by DescribeDisplaySwitches handlers ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1558-1572 ). Sessions inside handlers ¶ A handler that runs inside a request joins the request's transaction through core/

h: What modules do in each step
Why it is built this way
en.d: How ModuleBase defines a Cluster ERP backend module and how ModuleRegistry discovers, loads, and shuts down the modules.
en.b: Every business feature of Cluster ERP is a module: a package under src/cluster_erp/modules/ with a module.py whose class Module subclasses ModuleBase . This page explains the contract in core/module_base.py and how core/module_registry.py discovers, loads, and shuts down modules. The modules themselves are documented in the modules section . In short ¶ ModuleBase declares three abstract properties ( name , version , description ) and five abstract methods ( initialize , register_routes , register_events , shutdown , get_metadata ) ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:24-74 ). A module's API prefix is /api/v1/<name> ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:36-38 ). The registry imports cluster_erp.modules.<name>.module , instantiates its Module class, and calls initialize , register_routes , and register_events in that order ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:32-56 ). Modules are loaded in the order of the enabled_modules setting ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:58-72 , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:535-564 ). At shutdown the registry calls shutdown on every loaded module and logs, but does not raise, any error ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:74-80 ). How it works ¶ The contract ¶ Member Kind What the registry or server expects Source name abstract property The module key; also the key in registry.loaded src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:24-26 version abstract property A version string, shown by GET /api/v1/modules src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:28-30 description abstract property A one-line description, shown by GET /api/v1/modules src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:32-34 api_prefix property /api/v1/{name} , used by modules for their routers src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:36-38 request_database() method The current request's database when a request is in flight, else the module's own database handle src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:40-59 initialize(database) abstract async method Called first with the process default Database src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:61-62 register_routes(app) abstract method Adds the module's routers to the FastAPI app src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:64-65 register_events(bus) abstract method Subscribes event handlers and registers query handlers on the EventBus src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:67-68 shutdown() abstract async method Cleanup at process end src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:70-71 get_metadata() abstract method Returns the module's ModuleMeta src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:73-74 Discovery and loading ¶ The state diagram shows the life of one module inside the server process. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Imported: import cluster_erp.modules.name.module Imported --> Instantiated: Module() Instantiated --> Initialized: initialize(database) Initialized --> Routed: register_routes(app) Routed --> Wired: register_events(bus) Wired --> Serving: stored in registry Serving --> Stopped: shutdown() Stopped --> [*] In prose: discover() lists the sub-packages of cluster_erp.modules with pkgutil.iter_modules ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:26-30 ). load_all() takes enabled_modules when it is set, else the discovered list. en.d: How Cluster ERP keeps money as Decimal, stores it as Numeric, sends it as JSON strings, rounds it, and takes currency precision from reference data.
en.b: This page explains how money is handled in Cluster ERP: the project rule, the code in core/currencies.py and in the services that compute amounts, and the tests that guard the rule. It covers currencies and exchange rates only as far as they affect amounts; the currencies module page covers the rest. In short ¶ The project's written engineering rules require Decimal for every money value, Numeric in the database, strings in JSON, and banker's rounding ( ROUND_HALF_EVEN ). A currency's number of decimal places is reference data in core_currencies.decimal_places , not a constant ( src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:86 ). Exchange rates are Numeric(18, 6) columns and are serialised as strings ( src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:110-121 , src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:186-190 ). ROUND_HALF_EVEN is imported in 16 Python files under src/cluster_erp (counted with grep -rln ROUND_HALF_EVEN ); ROUND_HALF_UP appears in none. A test checks that every monetary analytics measure sits on a Numeric column, not a Float column ( tests/test_analytics_contributions.py:120-133 ). How it works ¶ Currency precision from reference data ¶ Currency rows carry code , numeric_code , name , symbol , decimal_places , translations , and is_active ( src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:57-89 ). The rows are seeded from the ISO 4217 set: a curated list with symbols and translations, completed from the pycountry package ( src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:559 , src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:1811-1852 ). See reference data and core i18n . Services that round a money total read the precision from this table. money_scale in the quotations module looks up Currency.decimal_places for the document currency and returns Decimal(1).scaleb(-decimals) ; it falls back to 2 places when the currency is unknown or unset ( src/cluster_erp/modules/quotations/rollup.py:31-46 ). The sales_orders module has its own money_scale ( src/cluster_erp/modules/sales_orders/rollup.py:24 ). Rounding ¶ The files that quantize money import ROUND_HALF_EVEN , for example src/cluster_erp/modules/quotations/rollup.py:21 . The modules with the most occurrences are procurement (MRP engine and routes), costing , projects , nesting , and bom (counted with grep -rn ROUND_HALF_EVEN , grouped by file). Exchange-rate conversion quantizes to six decimal places with quantize(Decimal("0.000001")) and no explicit rounding argument ( src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:423-443 ). The rounding mode then comes from the active decimal context. No code in src/cluster_erp changes the decimal context (searched for getcontext , localcontext , and setcontext ). The default context of Python's decimal module is described in the Python documentation . Quantities are not money and use other modes where the code needs them, for example ROUND_CEILING for the number of stock units needed ( src/cluster_erp/core/stock_conversion.py:65-67 ). JSON transport as strings ¶ ExchangeRateRead and ConvertResult declare field serialisers that turn Decimal values into strings ( src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:173-204 ). A tenant-defined field of type decimal is stored in JSONB as a string, never as a float ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:875-877 ). The test tests/test_tenant_fields.py:59-61 checks that coerce_value returns a string for both "12.50" and 3 . The change history turns Decimal values into strings in its JSON diff ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:108-109 ). Currency codes must exist ¶ assert_known_currency rejects a currency code that is not an active row of core_currencies , with error code CURRENCY_UNKNOWN and HTTP 422 ( src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:27-49 ). Its docstring states the reason: a format check alone would let a direct API call store a code such as ZZZ ( src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:31-36 ). Errors from numeric input ¶ A decimal.InvalidOperation raised while processing a request becomes VALIDATION_ERROR with HTTP 422, and a database DataError (for example a numeric overf

en.d: The mandatory product, model, and version breakdown in core/product_breakdown.py and the stock-size conversion arithmetic in core/stock_conversion.py.
en.b: Every document line that names a product in Cluster ERP must name its model and version too. This page explains the shared form fields and validation in core/product_breakdown.py , and the conversion from part pieces to stock units (bars or sheets) in core/stock_conversion.py . The products, models, and versions themselves are documented on products and services . In short ¶ A product reference is complete only with all three of product_id , product_model_id , and product_version_id , or with none of them ( src/cluster_erp/core/product_breakdown.py:94-118 ). Whether a model belongs to the product and a version belongs to the model is checked by the products_and_services module over the EventBus with ValidateProductBreakdown ( src/cluster_erp/core/product_breakdown.py:120-147 , src/cluster_erp/modules/products_and_services/module.py:131 ). product_breakdown_fields() returns the model and version picker fields for any form, each scoped by the field before it ( src/cluster_erp/core/product_breakdown.py:31-83 ). core/stock_conversion.py computes how many pieces fit into one bar or sheet, and how many stock units an order needs, with Decimal arithmetic ( src/cluster_erp/core/stock_conversion.py:19-67 ). How it works ¶ The breakdown rule ¶ ensure_product_breakdown(bus, product_id, product_model_id, product_version_id, source_module=...) runs these checks: No product: model and version must also be empty, else VALIDATION_ERROR with HTTP 422 ( src/cluster_erp/core/product_breakdown.py:103-110 ). A product without a model or a version: VALIDATION_ERROR with HTTP 422 ( src/cluster_erp/core/product_breakdown.py:112-118 ). All three present: the function queries ValidateProductBreakdown . If the answer is not ok , it raises the returned code, PRODUCT_MODEL_PRODUCT_MISMATCH or PRODUCT_VERSION_MODEL_MISMATCH , with HTTP 422 ( src/cluster_erp/core/product_breakdown.py:120-147 ). The sequence diagram shows the third case. sequenceDiagram participant S as Document service participant C as ensure_product_breakdown participant B as EventBus participant P as products_and_services S->>C: product, model, version ids C->>B: query(ValidateProductBreakdown) B->>P: handler P-->>B: ok, or ok false with code B-->>C: result C-->>S: return, or raise AppError 422 In prose: a service hands the three ids to the core helper. The helper asks the owning module over the EventBus and either returns or raises a 422 error with the returned code. 23 Python files in 11 modules call ensure_product_breakdown (counted with grep -rln ensure_product_breakdown src/cluster_erp/modules ): bom , fleet , inventory , nesting , procurement , production , products_and_services , projects , purchasing_quotations , quotations , and sales_orders . Shared form fields ¶ product_model_source(product_field) and product_version_source(model_field) build ForeignKeySource objects for the routes /models/ and /versions/ of products_and_services , filtered by the sibling field and by active_only ( src/cluster_erp/core/product_breakdown.py:31-48 ). product_breakdown_fields(...) wraps them in two FieldMeta objects, required by default ( src/cluster_erp/core/product_breakdown.py:55-83 ). The {field:...} parameter syntax lets the client fill the filter from the form; see generic form . en.d: The order and purpose of the five middlewares in the Cluster ERP server, the body size limit, security headers, the activity log, and the static web app mounts.
en.b: This page follows an HTTP request through the Cluster ERP server from the socket to the route and back. It covers the five middlewares added in server/app.py , the two middleware classes in server/middleware.py , the request context, the body limit, and the static mounts of the web app. Authentication and tenant routing happen in route dependencies and are documented in the identity and access section . In short ¶ create_app adds five middlewares: CommitBeforeResponseMiddleware , ActivityLogMiddleware , GZipMiddleware , _console_cors , and _security_headers ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1317-1430 ). Counted from the three add_middleware calls and the two @app.middleware("http") decorators. Starlette places each newly added middleware outside the earlier ones, so the request passes them in the reverse order of registration. _security_headers refuses a body larger than max_request_body_bytes with HTTP 413 before reading it, and sets security headers on every response ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1390-1430 ). ActivityLogMiddleware writes one activity-log row per request, and an error-log row for handled errors, in a background task ( src/cluster_erp/server/middleware.py:424-663 ). CommitBeforeResponseMiddleware runs pre-response hooks, which commit the request's session before the first response byte ( src/cluster_erp/server/middleware.py:25-57 ). How it works ¶ Order of the layers ¶ Starlette's add_middleware inserts each middleware at the front of its list, and the stack is built so that the first entry is the outermost one ( Starlette middleware documentation ). @app.middleware("http") registers through the same list. The registration order in create_app is CommitBeforeResponseMiddleware , ActivityLogMiddleware , GZipMiddleware , _console_cors , _security_headers ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1317 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1318 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1323 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1365 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1390 ). A request therefore passes them in this order: flowchart TD client["Client"] --> proxy["uvicorn ProxyHeadersMiddleware, when trust_proxy_headers is on"] proxy --> sec["_security_headers: body limit, security headers"] sec --> cors["_console_cors: CORS for the fleet endpoint only"] cors --> gzip["GZipMiddleware: responses over 1 KB"] gzip --> act["ActivityLogMiddleware: activity and error log"] act --> commit["CommitBeforeResponseMiddleware: pre-response hooks"] commit --> exc["Exception handlers"] exc --> route["Route and dependencies"] The table lists each layer. en.d: How python -m cluster_erp.server.main and server/asgi.py build the FastAPI application with create_app, and what the lifespan does at start-up and shutdown.
en.b: This page explains how the Cluster ERP server process starts: the two entry points server/main.py and server/asgi.py , the factory create_app in server/app.py , and the lifespan context that runs at start-up and shutdown. It is for developers and operators. The middleware order is on request pipeline and middleware , and service units and gunicorn settings are in the operations section . In short ¶ python -m cluster_erp.server.main calls uvicorn.run("cluster_erp.server.app:create_app", factory=True,...) ( src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:39-58 ). cluster_erp.server.asgi:app is a module-level application made by create_app() for a process manager ( src/cluster_erp/server/asgi.py:1-19 ). create_app reads Settings , builds the FastAPI object, installs error handlers and middleware, mounts the shared routes and the web app, and returns the app ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1287-1646 ). The lifespan context creates the database handle, the EventBus , the ModuleRegistry , and the storage backend, then loads every enabled module ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:58-140 ). At shutdown the lifespan closes the PDF renderer, cancels background tasks, shuts down every module, and closes the database ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:196-224 ). How it works ¶ Entry points ¶ There are two entry points. Entry point Used for Behaviour Source python -m cluster_erp.server.main (console script cluster-erp-server ) Development and single-process runs Runs uvicorn with the factory; enables reload when debug is on; uses server_workers processes when greater than 1 and reload is off src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:12-58 , pyproject.toml:87 cluster_erp.server.asgi:app gunicorn with uvicorn workers Creates the app at import time, once per worker src/cluster_erp/server/asgi.py:1-19 main.py ignores server_workers above 1 on Windows and logs a warning ( src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:27-35 ). It passes the proxy-header settings, the access-log switch, and the keep-alive timeout to uvicorn ( src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:50-55 ). See the settings reference for these settings. The factory ¶ create_app(settings=None) runs these steps in order: Creates Settings() when none is passed ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1288-1289 ). Configures logging at DEBUG or INFO ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1291-1294 ). Builds FastAPI with title "Cluster ERP", version 0.1.0 , and the lifespan context. The /api/docs and /api/redoc pages exist only when debug is on ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1296-1303 ). Stores the settings on app.state.settings ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1304 ). Applies three process-wide settings: change-history redaction columns, the authorisation cache lifetime, and the list count cap ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1307-1313 ). Installs the error handlers ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1314 ). See errors and exceptions . Adds five middlewares ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1317-1430 ). See request pipeline and middleware . Includes eight shared routers, and in multi-tenant mode also the signup and vendor routers ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1432-1450 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How Cluster ERP removes records from use without deleting them, records who and why, keeps unique values free, and where rows are still physically removed.
en.b: In Cluster ERP a "delete" from the user's side deactivates a record: the row stays and gets a deactivation time, actor, and reason. This page explains the core mechanism in core/models.py , core/change_history.py , core/bulk_operations.py , and the start-up column sweep, and it lists the places that still remove rows. Reactivation, the reason catalogue, and the retention purge belong to the records module; see records . In short ¶ deleted_at IS NULL means active; a value means deactivated ( src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:49-57 ). A deactivation records deleted_by , deactivation_reason , and deactivation_note on the row ( src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:58-72 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:242-259 ). The reason and note travel as the request headers X-Deact-Reason and X-Deact-Note ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:64-72 ). Bulk deactivation loads the objects and sets deleted_at through the ORM, so the change history and the reason stamp apply to every row ( src/cluster_erp/core/bulk_operations.py:20-55 ). Unique constraints apply only to live rows, through partial indexes with WHERE deleted_at IS NULL , for example src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:61-74 . How it works ¶ The deactivation flow ¶ The sequence diagram shows one deactivation request. sequenceDiagram participant C as Client participant D as get_db_session participant S as Service participant H as before_flush hook participant DB as PostgreSQL C->>D: DELETE with X-Deact-Reason, X-Deact-Note D->>D: set_deactivation_context(reason, note) D->>S: session S->>S: obj.deleted_at = now S->>H: flush H->>H: stamp deleted_by, deactivation_reason, deactivation_note H->>DB: UPDATE row and INSERT core_change_history (action deactivate) In prose: The session dependency reads the two headers, URL-decodes them, and stores them in the request context ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:64-72 ). A service sets deleted_at . Examples: AttachmentService.delete and NoteService.delete ( src/cluster_erp/core/attachments.py:155-161 , src/cluster_erp/core/notes.py:94-100 ). At flush, the change-history hook detects the transition from NULL to a value ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:229-239 ). It stamps deleted_by with the actor, and deactivation_reason and deactivation_note from the context, when they are empty ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:242-259 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:336-337 ). The hook classifies the change as deactivate ; a transition back to NULL is activate ( src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:197-213 ). See change history . Bulk deactivation ¶ bulk_soft_delete(session, model_class, ids, deleted_by=None) selects the live rows among ids , sets deleted_at (and deleted_by when given) on each, flushes, and returns the count ( src/cluster_erp/core/bulk_operations.py:20-55 ). Its docstring states why it does not issue one UPDATE : a Core update bypasses the before_flush hook, so the history and the reason stamp would be lost ( src/cluster_erp/core/bulk_operations.py:26-34 ). 54 files outside core/bulk_operations.py call it (counted with grep -rln bulk_soft_delete ). BulkDeleteRequest and BulkDeleteResponse are the shared request and response schemas ( src/cluster_erp/core/bulk_operations.py:12-17 ). Deactivation columns on every table ¶ At start-up the server runs an idempotent SQL block that adds deactivation_reason VARCHAR(64) and deactivation_note TEXT to every public table that has a deleted_at column but lacks them ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1111-1149 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1152-1166 ). The block takes a transaction-level advisory lock so that two workers starting together do not deadlock ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1111-1115 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1121 ). Live-row uniqueness ¶ A deactivated row must not block its unique value. Models declare unique indexes with postgresql_where=text("deleted_at IS NULL") . 120 lines in src/cluster_erp/modules and src/clus

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How core/tenant_fields.py and server/routes/tenant_fields.py let an administrator switch shipped fields off and add tenant-defined fields stored in an extra JSONB bag.
en.b: Tenant fields let each tenant decide what its forms collect, without code changes: shipped fields can be switched off or made required, and new fields can be added. This page explains the core service in src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py and the routes in src/cluster_erp/server/routes/tenant_fields.py . The metadata classes it builds on are listed on metadata model . In short ¶ An entity opts in by declaring EntityMeta.tenant_fields with one or more storage buckets ( src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:517-550 ). 25 metadata declarations do so (counted with grep -rn "tenant_fields=TenantFieldsMeta" over src/cluster_erp/modules ). Three tables hold the tenant's decisions: core_field_catalog , core_field_definitions , and core_field_settings ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:168-295 ). A tenant field's value lives in the extra JSONB column of the bucket row, as extra[key] ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:16-19 , src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:142-146 ). Clients apply a per-tenant overlay from GET /api/v1/_overlay on top of the fixed metadata ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/tenant_fields.py:446-456 ). The settings screens are generated: the service injects settings entities into the declaring module's metadata ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:3433-3497 ). How it works ¶ The three tables ¶ Table Class What a row means Source core_field_catalog FieldCatalogEntry One concept the tenant collects, defined once: code, labels, type, choices, category, protection class, permission src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:168-201 core_field_definitions FieldDefinition One placement of a concept on an entity bucket: own (stored on the row) or derived (shown read-only from a linked record) src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:208-266 core_field_settings FieldSetting The tenant's decision on one shipped field: enabled, required override, order, list and filter flags src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:269-292 All three derive from BaseModel , so they are deactivated, not deleted, and their unique indexes cover live rows only ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:194-201 , src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:255-266 , src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:287-295 ). Closing a definition sets is_active to false; stored values stay and are shown read-only ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:9-13 ). Specs from metadata ¶ At start-up the server calls build_specs with every module's metadata ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:151 ). The specs record each declaring entity, its buckets, the shipped fields of each bucket, and the foreign-key links between entities ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:300-354 , src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:451-500 ). bucket_for_table maps a table name back to an entity and bucket; the change history uses it ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:506-513 , src/cluster_erp/core/change_history.py:373 ). Values ¶ Owning services call TenantFieldService.validate_extra before they store a row. Every key must be a known, open field of the bucket, and every value is coerced by its definition. A closed field keeps its stored value but takes no new value; an unknown key is refused ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:1942-1955 ). coerce_value handles the eight field types and stores a decimal as a string ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:139-150 , src/cluster_erp/core/tenant_fields.py:854-911 ). Violations raise FIELD_VALUE_INVALID ( src/cluster_erp/core/errors.py:61-66 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: The time-zone-aware working-time engine in core/working_time.py with weekly shifts, date overrides, calendar exceptions, base-calendar inheritance, and DST handling.
en.b: src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py computes working windows, working minutes, and working days for scheduling and planning. It is pure Python with no database access; callers load calendar rows and pass plain structures in. This page explains its two layers. The calendar records that feed it belong to the calendars module; see calendars and scheduling . In short ¶ The low-level layer works on a Shifts map from weekday (0 is Monday) to wall-clock spans ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:32-34 ). Wall-clock times are converted to UTC per local day, with an explicit rule for daylight-saving transitions ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:94-112 ). The calendar layer adds per-date exceptions, open , closed , and inherit controls, and inheritance from a base calendar ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:340-380 ). An unknown or empty time zone falls back to UTC ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:115-122 ). The defaults are Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00, in UTC ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:66-69 ). How it works ¶ Low-level primitives ¶ Function Behaviour Source localize(day, wall, tz) Wall-clock time to an aware datetime; an ambiguous time takes the first occurrence, a skipped time moves forward by the gap src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:94-112 resolve_timezone(name) and is_valid_timezone(name) A ZoneInfo , falling back to UTC; a validity check src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:115-132 shifts_from_rows(rows) Builds Shifts from rows with day_of_week , start_time , end_time src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:135-155 with_overrides(shifts, overrides) Attaches per-date UTC windows to a weekly pattern as DayWindowShifts src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:37-63 working_windows(shifts, tz_name, day) UTC windows of one local day; a date override wins over the weekly pattern src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:158-191 next_working_instant(...) The first working instant at or after a moment, within the search horizon src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:194-210 add_working_minutes(...) Consumes working minutes from a start, skipping gaps; a non-positive duration becomes MIN_BAR_MINUTES src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:213-256 working_minutes_between(...) Working minutes in a UTC interval src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:259-283 day_capacity_minutes(...) and effective_day_capacity_minutes(...) Available minutes of a local day src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:286-329 SEARCH_HORIZON_DAYS is 90 and bounds the slot search; an internal iteration guard stops a pathological shift map ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:76-81 ). Calendar layer ¶ A CalendarLayer holds a weekly template, a time zone, a list of CalendarException objects, and an optional base layer ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:370-379 ). A CalendarException has a recurrence ( none , annual , or weekly ) and a control ( open , closed , or inherit ) ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:344-367 ). windows_for_day(layer, day) resolves one day in this order ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:458-490 ): flowchart TD day["Local day"] --> exc{"Own exception matches?"} exc -->|closed| none["No windows"] exc -->|open with intervals| own["Exception intervals"] exc -->|inherit| base["Resolve on base calendar"] exc -->|no match| hol{"Base ancestor closes the day?"} hol -->|yes| none hol -->|no| tmpl["Own weekly template"] In prose: the layer's own most specific exception decides first; a one-off date beats an annual date, which beats a weekday rule ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:410-433 ). Without an own exception, an explicit closed exception on a base ancestor closes the day; the base's weekly gaps do not propagate ( src/cluster_erp/core/working_time.py:436-455 ). Otherwise the layer's weekly template applies. An open exception without intervals and an inherit exception without a base also fall through to the template ( src/cluster

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How attribute-based policies in modules/auth/policies refine a permission code with rules over user, resource, and environment attributes.
en.b: An attribute-based access control policy ( AuthAbacPolicy , an "ABAC policy") adds conditions to one permission code. A user who holds the code must also satisfy every active policy of that code. Policies are records that an administrator edits in the auth settings; the evaluator lives in modules/auth/guards.py and the records in modules/auth/policies/ . Roles and permission codes themselves are explained in roles and permissions . In short ¶ A policy belongs to one permission_code and stores a condition of the form {"logic": "all" or "any", "rules": [...]} ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/policies/models.py:12-55 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/policies/schemas.py:76-90 ). A rule has a subject attribute path, an operator , and a target that is a literal or another attribute path ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:325-334 ). Ten operators exist: eq , neq , in , not_in , gt , gte , lt , lte , contains , between ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/policies/schemas.py:11-13 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:394-438 ). All active policies of a code must pass; each policy combines its own rules by its logic ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:259-281 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:306-322 ). With no policy, a code is allowed, unless it is listed in the setting abac_strict_permission_codes ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:215-236 , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:339 ). How it works ¶ Attributes ¶ _resolve_attribute splits a path at the first dot into a scope and a field ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:337-369 ): Scope Fields Source user Only the allow-listed names id , username , email , first_name , last_name , employee_id , party_id , is_active , department , clearance , title , location ; any other name resolves to nothing src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:41-61 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:351-356 resource Any key of the attribute dictionary that the caller passes for a loaded entity src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:357-358 env current_time ( HH:MM:SS , UTC) and current_date ( YYYY-MM-DD , UTC) src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:359-367 The names department , clearance , title , and location are not columns of AuthUser ; the comment calls them forward slots for subject attributes from human resources, and they resolve to nothing today ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:41-45 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/models.py:17-91 ). Operators ¶ Operator Meaning Missing or malformed input Source eq , neq String equality or inequality False src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:395-402 in , not_in Membership in a list target False when the target is not a list src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:403-412 gt , gte , lt , lte Ordering of numbers, then ISO times, then ISO dates False when the pair cannot be compared src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:372-391 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:413-424 contains Substring of a string subject False for non-strings src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:425-428 between Inclusive range given as a two-item list False otherwise src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:429-436 any other value none False src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:438 Where policies are evaluated ¶ The flowchart shows the two evaluation points. flowchart TD guard["require_permission"] --> route_eval["check_abac, resource None"] route_eval --> skip["rules on resource.* skipped"] skip --> userenv["user.* and env.* rules decided"] userenv --> handler["route handler loads entity"] handler --> wired{"code in RESOURCE_ENFORCED_CODES?"} wired -->|yes| post["enforce_abac with entity attributes"] wired -->|no| done["no second evaluation"] post --> done In prose: The route guard calls check_abac with resource=None . h: Licence states and the licensing posture
Why it is built this way
en.d: How the app_store module, the licence file, role assignments, and server/entitlements.py decide which apps and module APIs a user may use.
en.b: Cluster ERP sells its business areas as apps. Whether a user can open an app, and whether the API of a backend module answers, depends on four layers: the catalogue, the licence, role assignments, and the deployment's install state. The app_store module in src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/ keeps these records, and server/entitlements.py enforces them on every request to a gated module. This page explains each layer at mechanism level. It does not describe licence file contents or verification details. The module overview is on the app store module page. In short ¶ The catalogue is shipped in modules/app_store/catalog.json and converged into app_store_apps at every start-up; it lists 28 apps, 6 of them system apps ( src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/services.py:50-97 , counted from catalog.json entries with system or permanent set). The licence is a vendor-signed document uploaded by an administrator and re-verified against the public key in license_public_key on every resolution ( src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/license.py:1-14 , src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/services.py:201-236 ). Licence states are none , invalid , active , grace , and read_only ( src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/license.py:9-14 , src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/license.py:33 ). Role assignments use three intents, required , available , and blocked ; an app without assignment rows is open to everyone ( src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/models.py:77-104 , src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/services.py:23-47 ).
