h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How approval chains in modules/auth define ordered role steps, how other modules submit records for approval, and how approvers decide, defer, or cancel.
en.b: An approval chain ( AuthApprovalChain ) is an ordered list of steps for one resource and action, and each step names the role that must decide it. A business module that wants a record approved asks the auth module, over the EventBus, for the chain of its action and submits an approval request ( AuthApprovalRequest ). Approvers see their pending items in My Approvals ( webapp/i18n/en.json key approvals.inbox_title ) and approve, reject, or defer them. This page explains modules/auth/approval_chains/ and modules/auth/approvals/ . Each business module's own approval states are documented on its module page. In short ¶ A chain is identified by resource and action ; only an active, live chain is found ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approval_chains/models.py:13-61 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approval_chains/services.py:61-77 ). A step has step_order , role_code , is_required , condition , and timeout_hours ; step_order is unique per chain among live rows ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approval_chains/models.py:64-106 ). A request has four statuses: pending , approved , rejected , and cancelled ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:279 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:379-400 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:533 ). The decider must hold the current step's role, must not be the requester, and must not have decided an earlier step of the same request; a system administrator role overrides the step role only ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:311-368 ). A final decision emits ApprovalCompleted on the EventBus ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/routes.py:116-127 ). How it works ¶ Request states ¶ The state diagram shows the life of one approval request. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> pending: create_request pending --> pending: approved, next step exists pending --> approved: approved, no next step pending --> rejected: rejected pending --> cancelled: cancel by requester or administrator approved --> [*] rejected --> [*] cancelled --> [*] In prose: create_request locks the chain row, requires the chain to be live, active, and to have at least one live step, and starts the request at the lowest live step_order with status pending ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:229-285 ). decide locks the request row and refuses anything that is not pending ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:287-309 ). It applies three segregation-of-duties checks: the requester cannot decide, a user who already decided a step of this request cannot decide again, and the decider must hold the current step's role_code unless the decider holds admin or system_admin ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:311-368 ). It records an AuthApprovalDecision . A rejection ends the request. An approval moves current_step to the next live step, or ends the request as approved when no step follows ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:370-405 ). cancel sets cancelled ; only the requester or a system administrator may cancel ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:514-537 ). The decision body accepts only approved or rejected ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/schemas.py:16 ). Defer ¶ defer records a personal snooze ( AuthApprovalSnooze ) until a future date. It does not change the request, does not advance a step, and does not hide the item from other approvers. The same eligibility as deciding applies, and a new snooze replaces the caller's previous one ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/models.py:115-156 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:407-489 ). lift_defer ends the caller's own snooze ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/approvals/services.py:491-512 ). In the web app these actions are Defer and Bring back now ( webapp/i18n/en.json keys approvals.defer , approvals.defer_lift ). The inbox ¶ GET /api/v1/auth/approvals/inbox returns the caller's actionable pending requests. Eligibil

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How tenant users sign in, how access and refresh tokens are issued, carried, rotated, and revoked, and which settings control them.
en.b: Cluster ERP signs tenant users in with a user name or company e-mail and a password, then issues a short-lived access token and a rotating refresh token. The web client receives both tokens as HttpOnly cookies; the desktop client and scripts receive them in the response body and send a Bearer header. This page explains the sign-in routes in modules/auth/login/routes.py , the token helpers in modules/auth/jwt_utils.py , the cookie transport in modules/auth/session_cookies.py , password hashing in modules/auth/password.py , revocation through auth_token_blacklist , and the permission memory in modules/auth/auth_cache.py . The operator console has its own sign-in; see operator console . In short ¶ Passwords are hashed with Argon2 through argon2.PasswordHasher , and a hash is upgraded when its parameters are outdated ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/password.py:3-21 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/services.py:298-308 ). Access and refresh tokens are signed with the secret_key setting; each carries a unique jti and a type claim that verify_token checks ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/jwt_utils.py:10-60 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/jwt_utils.py:80-91 ). The web client asks for cookie transport with the X-Token-Transport header; cookie-carried writes must also carry the X-Requested-With header ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/session_cookies.py:31-39 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/session_cookies.py:112-121 ). Every refresh spends the presented refresh token and issues a new pair; the session end is fixed at sign-in and survives rotation ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/login/routes.py:283-354 ). Sign-out, a password change, and an anonymisation stamp last_logout_at , which invalidates every token issued earlier ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/login/routes.py:423-424 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/services.py:273-276 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/privacy_handlers.py:96 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:153-165 ). How it works ¶ Sign-in and refresh flow ¶ The sequence shows a web sign-in, a later request, and a refresh. sequenceDiagram participant C as web client participant L as login route participant U as UserService participant G as get_current_user participant R as refresh route C->>L: POST /api/v1/auth/login with X-Token-Transport L->>L: _check_attempt_budget L->>U: get_by_identifier, authenticate U-->>L: AuthUser or None L-->>C: user and permissions, tokens in HttpOnly cookies C->>G: request with access cookie and X-Requested-With G->>G: verify_token, jti blacklist, last_logout_at C->>R: POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with refresh cookie R->>R: spend old jti, check last_logout_at R-->>C: new access and refresh cookies In prose: The login route first checks the failed-attempt budget for the pair of client address and user name ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/login/routes.py:129-131 ). get_by_identifier resolves the user name. When nothing matches and the identifier holds @ , it tries the company e-mail, then the part before @ as a user name ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/services.py:92-119 ). A locked account is refused before the password is checked ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/login/routes.py:135-147 ). authenticate refuses inactive users, verifies the password, and re-hashes it when needed ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/services.py:298-308 ). On success, the route clears the failure counter, stamps last_login_at at most once a minute, and loads role and permission codes ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/login/routes.py:181-201 ). It issues the tokens. In multi-tenant mode both tokens carry the tenant key resolved for the request ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/login/routes.py:203-228 ). A cookie client gets empty token fields in the body and the tokens in cookies; other clients get the tokens in the body ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/login/routes.py:230-257 ). Every protected request runs get_current_user . It reads the credential, applies the CSRF

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How core/field_access.py hides gated field values, and how core/row_scope.py and core/rls.py limit personal records to their owner and team.
en.b: A permission code decides whether a user may call a route. Two finer layers decide what the user sees in the answer. Field access, in core/field_access.py , removes the values of metadata fields that need a permission code the caller lacks. Row access, in core/row_scope.py with the database backstop in core/rls.py , limits personal records to their owner and the owner's team. The value redaction of change history in core/sensitive_fields.py is a third, separate mechanism; it is documented in change history . In short ¶ A FieldMeta may name a permission ; the field's value then reaches only callers who hold that code ( src/cluster_erp/core/field_access.py:1-13 , src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:115-119 ). redact_restricted blanks gated fields in a response and drop_restricted_input removes them from an incoming payload ( src/cluster_erp/core/field_access.py:48-72 ). build_scope returns one of three scopes: all rows for a holder of <entity>.read_all , the caller's own party plus the transitive team otherwise, and no rows when the caller has no party ( src/cluster_erp/core/row_scope.py:62-83 ). apply_scope adds an IN filter on the owner column; an empty scope yields an empty result, never all rows ( src/cluster_erp/core/row_scope.py:92-109 ). Two tables carry a database row policy that reads a transaction-local setting published from the same scope ( migrations/versions/rls01_crown_jewel_rls_backstop.py:32-48 , src/cluster_erp/core/rls.py:1-23 ). How it works ¶ Field access ¶ restricted_fields walks the form field groups of an EntityMeta , including nested item_fields , and returns each field key with its permission code ( src/cluster_erp/core/field_access.py:24-41 ). denied_fields keeps the keys whose code the caller does not hold ( src/cluster_erp/core/field_access.py:44-45 ). The caller's predicate comes from allowed_from_codes over the caller's permission set, which other modules obtain through actor_allowed or permission_codes_for in modules/auth/guards.py ( src/cluster_erp/core/field_access.py:75-77 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:170-186 ). Users at this commit, found with grep for redact_restricted and drop_restricted_input : Caller Use Source Employee routes Drop gated input on create and update, blank gated output src/cluster_erp/modules/owned_organisations/employees/routes.py:57-112 Party composite route Drop gated employee input src/cluster_erp/server/routes/party_composite.py:118-119 Party roles route Drop gated employee input src/cluster_erp/server/routes/party_roles.py:118 The gated fields declared in code use the code employee.read_sensitive : six declarations in modules/owned_organisations/organisations/metadata.py (for example tax_no , national_id_no , social_security_no , and blood_group at lines 462-500) and six in modules/parties/parties/metadata.py (counted with grep ). Tenant-defined fields have their own permission gate through redact_extra ; see tenant fields . Row scope ¶ row_scope is a pure module. It depends only on uuid and SQLAlchemy Core; the caller supplies the data ( src/cluster_erp/core/row_scope.py:15-21 ). Caller state Resulting Scope Source Holds <entity>.read_all all_access=True , no filter src/cluster_erp/core/row_scope.py:78-79 No party can be resolved Empty party set, sees nothing src/cluster_erp/core/row_scope.py:80-81 Party resolved Own party plus the transitive team src/cluster_erp/core/row_scope.py:82-83 Scope.may_see decides a single record; Scope.restrict returns the list for a query ( src/cluster_erp/core/row_scope.py:46-59 ). deny_all is the explicit empty scope ( src/cluster_erp/core/row_scope.py:86-89 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: The database-per-tenant model in core/tenancy.py, how a request is routed to its tenant database, and how memberships suspend and close tenants.
en.b: Cluster ERP can serve many customer companies from one deployment. Each company, a tenant ( Tenant ), has its own physical PostgreSQL database; a separate control-plane database holds the tenant registry, the commercial memberships, operator accounts, and rate-limit counters. The mode is off by default and turned on with the setting multi_tenant . This page explains core/tenancy.py , the tenant routing in server/dependencies.py , the request context in core/request_context.py , and the membership commands in server/membership.py . Provisioning and offboarding commands are in tenant lifecycle . In short ¶ Isolation is by database: a request resolved to tenant A gets an engine whose connection names A's database, so there is no query filter to forget ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:1-16 ). Control-plane tables use their own declarative base, ControlBase , so tenant schema creation never creates them and the reverse ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:86-93 ). A request is routed by the signature-verified tenant claim of its token, or at sign-in by the X-Tenant-Domain header; anything that does not resolve to an active tenant gets one generic HTTP 401 ( src/cluster_erp/server/dependencies.py:104-157 ). A tenant has four statuses in the database constraint: provisioning , active , suspended , and closed ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:124-129 ). A daily pass suspends tenants whose membership period has ended ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:324-354 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:372-403 ). How it works ¶ Control plane ¶ ControlBase declares six tables, counted with grep __tablename__ in core/tenancy.py : Entity Table Purpose Source Tenant control_tenants Key, name, status, database name, mail domains, region, closing data src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:96-129 Operator control_operators Operator console accounts src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:132-154 OperatorAction control_operator_actions Audit trail of operator actions src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:157-170 RateLimitBucket control_rate_limits Shared fixed-window counters for anonymous routes src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:173-183 ControlRetentionRun control_retention_runs Summary of each control-plane retention pass src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:186-198 Membership control_memberships Plan, status, admin e-mail, payment reference, period end, provisioning state, signup tokens as digests src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:201-285 A tenant key must match a strict identifier pattern because it becomes the database name suffix, tenant_db_prefix plus key ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:42-46 , src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:458-468 ). Mail domains are stored lower-cased and IDNA-encoded by normalize_domain ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:53-70 ). Each tenant has a fixed data-residency region ; its database lives on that region's server ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:107-108 , src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:593-595 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: The vendor operator console of a multi-tenant deployment, its separate accounts and tokens, its second factor, its routes, and its audit trail.
en.b: The operator console is the screen of the people who run a multi-tenant deployment. Operators are not tenant users: their accounts live in the control-plane database, they sign in through their own route, and their tokens are refused by every tenant route. The server side is server/operators.py and server/routes/vendor.py ; the page is webapp/operator.html with webapp/js/operator.js . This page explains accounts, sign-in, the routes, the cross-country fleet view, and the audit trail. In short ¶ The console API exists only in multi-tenant mode, under /api/v1/vendor ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1440-1450 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/vendor.py:68-70 ). Operator accounts live in control_operators ; the first one is created at start-up from vendor_admin_username and vendor_admin_password when none exists ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:132-154 , src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:56-75 ). Sign-in requires the password and, with vendor_require_totp on, an authenticator code ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:114-175 , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:131 ). Operator tokens carry the audience vendor and last a fixed number of hours; tenant tokens and operator tokens are refused at each other's routes ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:1-12 , src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:209-235 ). Every change an operator makes to a customer is written to control_operator_actions ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:238-257 ). How it works ¶ Accounts ¶ Command Effect Source python -m cluster_erp.server.operators add <username> Create an operator src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:78-90 python -m cluster_erp.server.operators list List operators src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:323-366 python -m cluster_erp.server.operators disable <username> Deactivate an operator src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:93-103 python -m cluster_erp.server.operators totp-enroll <username> Issue the authenticator seed src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:178-195 , src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:352-353 The seed is stored sealed; see second factor and secret storage . Sign-in and requests ¶ POST /api/v1/vendor/login takes username , password , and an optional otp_code ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/vendor.py:101-138 ). authenticate returns one of five outcomes: ok , invalid , locked , totp_required , or totp_not_enrolled ; an unknown name and a wrong password give the same answer ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:104-128 ). A wrong code counts as a failed attempt, and repeated failures lock the account for a period ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:110-111 , src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:147-152 ). Every other route depends on require_operator , which reads a Bearer token with the vendor audience and loads the active operator ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/vendor.py:84-96 ). The setting vendor_allowed_ips limits the console API to listed addresses or networks; it applies before sign-in ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/vendor.py:38-70 , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:134 ). When it is empty, the server logs a warning at start-up ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:129-134 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the privacy module registers data-subject requests, collects a person's data from every module, anonymises it, and replays erasures after a restore.
en.b: A data-subject request ( SubjectRequest ) records an application by a person to see, correct, erase, or object to the processing of their personal data. The privacy module keeps the register, the identity check, the deadline, and the outcome. It never reads another module's tables: it fans out two EventBus events, and each module that holds personal data answers for its own tables in its privacy_handlers.py . An erasure is also written to a ledger outside the database so that a restored backup cannot bring the data back unnoticed. The module overview is on the privacy module page. In short ¶ Four request types exist: access , rectification , erasure , objection ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/models.py:13-18 ). Four statuses exist: received , verified , completed , rejected ; every transition is an action ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/models.py:32-36 , src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:196-527 ). The due date is the receipt date plus the setting privacy_response_days ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/models.py:61-62 , src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:157-170 , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:733 ). CollectSubjectData gathers a copy and AnonymiseSubject erases by anonymisation; nine modules subscribe to both ( src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2385-2438 ). A completed erasure is appended to a node-local ledger, sealed with the backup key when one is set, and replayed at every start-up ( src/cluster_erp/core/erasure_ledger.py:1-16 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:255-311 ). How it works ¶ Request lifecycle ¶ The state diagram shows the statuses and the actions that move them. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> received: create received --> verified: verify verified --> verified: export verified --> completed: anonymise, erasure only verified --> completed: complete received --> rejected: reject verified --> rejected: reject completed --> [*] rejected --> [*] In prose: create gives the request a yearly business key, sets due_at , and starts at received ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:157-172 ). verify records the identity method and moves received to verified ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:198-207 ). prepare_export , allowed only while verified , collects the data and stores one JSON file as an attachment on the request ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:247-272 ). export_file returns it ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:274-295 ). anonymise , allowed only for an erasure request that is verified , requires the operator to type the request code, then erases and completes the request ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:297-327 ). complete closes a verified request with a resolution note; reject closes a received or verified request with a reason ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:507-527 ). A completed or rejected request cannot be edited ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:174-186 ). Collecting a copy ¶ collect fetches the subject's e-mail addresses through GetPartyContactValues , emits CollectSubjectData with the party id, the optional user id, and those addresses, and keeps every answer that has sections ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:209-245 ). Each answer has the shape {"module", "sections": [{"key", "label", "rows"}]} and must not contain secrets such as password hashes or tokens ( src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2385-2401 ). Anonymising ¶ _apply_erasure runs all modules in one transaction ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:329-424 ): It emits AnonymiseSubject with the marker from privacy_anonymised_marker , a reason, and three operator decisions: include_employment_records , include_correspondence , and include_documents ( src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/services.py:345-357 , src/cluster_erp/modules/privacy/requests/schemas.py:70-73 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How permission codes are seeded from metadata, granted to roles, assigned to users, and checked by require_permission on every guarded route.
en.b: Cluster ERP authorises requests with role-based access control: a user holds roles, a role holds permission codes, and a route demands one or more codes. This page explains the permission catalogue in modules/auth/permissions , roles in modules/auth/roles , user-role assignment in modules/auth/users , the guard in modules/auth/guards.py , the family splits in server/permission_families.py , and the REQUIRED_PERMISSION pattern on EventBus contracts. Attribute policies that refine a permission are in ABAC policies ; field and row limits are in field and row access . In short ¶ A permission code has the form <resource>.<action> . At every start-up, codes for create , read , update , and delete are seeded for each entity and settings tab in module metadata, plus a fixed list of extra codes ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/permissions/services.py:44-136 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:634-858 ). One system role with code admin is ensured at every start-up and re-granted every live permission ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/roles/services.py:213-276 ). A route declares its demand with require_permission("<code>") ; the guard authenticates the caller, checks that the caller holds every code, then evaluates attribute policies ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/guards.py:205-240 ). Granting is capped: a caller may only add a role or a permission whose codes the caller already holds, unless the caller holds a system administrator role ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/services.py:169-221 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/roles/services.py:122-163 ). A user's permission set is the union over live user-role links and live grants of live permissions ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/services.py:310-332 ). How it works ¶ Data model ¶ Entity Table Key fields Source AuthPermission auth_permissions code (unique among live rows), resource , action , module , translations src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/permissions/models.py:15-55 AuthRole auth_roles code (unique among live rows), name , translations , is_system , is_active src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/roles/models.py:17-65 AuthRolePermission auth_role_permissions role_id , permission_id (unique pair among live rows) src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/roles/models.py:68-97 AuthUser auth_users username , email (each unique among live rows), password_hash , is_active , employee_id src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/models.py:17-91 AuthUserRole auth_user_roles user_id , role_id (unique pair among live rows) src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/models.py:94-123 Grants and assignments are never deleted. Removing a role from a user or a permission from a role sets deleted_at ; adding it again revives the same row ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/users/services.py:161-181 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/roles/services.py:115-134 ). Seeding the catalogue ¶ _seed_permissions_from_metadata collects, for each loaded module, the entity keys of its metadata and the tab keys of its settings sections ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:639-652 ). It adds a list of extra codes for lifecycle actions such as approve , install , or read_all ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:654-848 ). seed_from_metadata creates any missing code and re-files an existing code under the module that declares its entity today ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/permissions/services.py:44-136 ). After that, ensure_system_admin grants every live permission to the admin role, reviving revoked grants, and consolidates a legacy system_admin role into it ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/roles/services.py:174-276 ). copy_family_grants then runs (see the section Family splits). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: The operator console second factor in core/totp.py and how core/secret_box.py and core/crypto_at_rest.py protect secrets, files, and backups at rest.
en.b: Cluster ERP has three small cryptographic helpers in src/cluster_erp/core/ . core/totp.py computes time-based one-time passwords for the operator console. core/secret_box.py seals small control-plane secrets that must be read back, such as the operators' authenticator seeds. core/crypto_at_rest.py encrypts stored files and database dumps. This page states what each one protects and which setting supplies its key. It never shows key values; see the settings reference for the variable names. In short ¶ The second factor is a standard time-based one-time password with six digits and 30-second steps, verified with a tolerance of one step on each side ( src/cluster_erp/core/totp.py:1-4 , src/cluster_erp/core/totp.py:16-17 , src/cluster_erp/core/totp.py:42-55 ). In the code at this commit, verify_totp is called only by the operator sign-in in server/operators.py ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:129-168 ). Operator seeds are stored sealed with the enc: prefix; the key comes from control_encryption_key , or from secret_key when that setting is empty ( src/cluster_erp/core/secret_box.py:1-9 , src/cluster_erp/core/secret_box.py:33-37 ). Files and backups use authenticated encryption with a 256-bit key given as 64 hexadecimal characters ( src/cluster_erp/core/crypto_at_rest.py:1-16 , src/cluster_erp/core/crypto_at_rest.py:34-40 ). In multi-tenant mode the settings validator refuses to start without storage_encryption_key , backup_encryption_key , and mail_encryption_key ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:805-821 ). How it works ¶ The operator second factor ¶ generate_secret creates a random 160-bit seed in base32 ( src/cluster_erp/core/totp.py:20-22 ). otpauth_uri builds the enrolment link an authenticator app reads ( src/cluster_erp/core/totp.py:58-63 ). verify_totp keeps only digits, requires six of them, and compares in constant time against the current step and its neighbours ( src/cluster_erp/core/totp.py:42-55 ). The operator account flow is in server/operators.py : enroll_totp issues or replaces a seed, stores it sealed, stamps totp_enrolled_at , and returns the seed and link once ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:178-195 ). The command python -m cluster_erp.server.operators totp-enroll runs it ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:352-353 ). authenticate checks the password first and the code second. A wrong code counts as a failed attempt. When vendor_require_totp is on, an operator without a seed cannot sign in ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:114-175 , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:131 ). A seed stored before sealing existed is sealed at its next successful use ( src/cluster_erp/server/operators.py:165-167 ). The full operator sign-in is described in operator console . Sealed control-plane secrets ¶ secret_box uses Fernet from the cryptography package. The Fernet key is the SHA-256 digest of the configured material ( src/cluster_erp/core/secret_box.py:27-37 ). seal returns enc: plus the token, and open_secret returns the plain value of a sealed or legacy unsealed entry ( src/cluster_erp/core/secret_box.py:40-61 ). A changed key makes open_secret raise ValueError ( src/cluster_erp/core/secret_box.py:58-61 ). The column control_operators.totp_secret is wide enough for the sealed form ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:147-148 ). The mail module seals its own provider secrets with a separate helper keyed by mail_encryption_key ( src/cluster_erp/modules/mail/crypto.py:1-10 ). The mail module page covers it. Files and backups at rest ¶ crypto_at_rest defines two containers ( src/cluster_erp/core/crypto_at_rest.py:1-16 ): Container Use Key setting Source Blob One stored attachment, encrypted in memory with a fresh random nonce storage_encryption_key src/cluster_erp/core/crypto_at_rest.py:50-66 , src/cluster_erp/core/storage.py:138-166 Stream A database dump of any size, encrypted in chunks that cannot be dropped, repeated, or reordered backup_encryption_key src/cluster_erp/core/crypto_at_rest.py:70-140 , src/clus

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: The self-service signup that creates a tenant and its membership in multi-tenant mode, with domain verification, the privacy notice, and provisioning.
en.b: Signup is the anonymous, public entry through which a company buys a membership and gets its own tenant. It exists only in multi-tenant mode. The routes are in server/routes/signup.py and the flow in server/signup.py ; both work on the control plane, never on a tenant database. This page explains validation, the privacy notice, domain verification, payment, provisioning, and the anonymous status poll. The tenant model itself is in multi-tenancy ; the web form is described in mail and profile screens . In short ¶ The routes are mounted only when multi_tenant is on; otherwise GET /api/v1/signup/ answers {"signup": "closed"} ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1440-1457 ). The setting signup_enabled closes the door on a multi-tenant node: the probe answers closed and a create is refused with SIGNUP_CLOSED ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/signup.py:129-133 , src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:226-234 ). A signup needs the current privacy notice version, read from signup_notice_dir and signup_notice_version ; without a configured notice, signups are refused ( src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:206-253 ). The founder's e-mail must be on the claimed mail domain, and with signup_verify_email on, provisioning waits until a link mailed to that address is confirmed ( src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:256-280 , src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:336-372 ). The anonymous surface accepts only capability tokens in request bodies; the control plane stores their SHA-256 digests ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/signup.py:8-15 , src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:73-84 , src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:233-239 ). How it works ¶ Steps ¶ The sequence shows a signup with e-mail verification on. sequenceDiagram participant V as visitor browser participant R as signup routes participant S as start_signup participant T as TenantRegistry participant P as provision V->>R: GET /api/v1/signup/ R-->>V: open or closed, regions, notice V->>R: POST /api/v1/signup/ R->>S: SignupRequest S->>T: domain_owner, create_tenant, Membership S-->>V: signup_token, state queued V->>R: POST /api/v1/signup/verify with verify_token R->>P: _provision_in_background V->>R: POST /api/v1/signup/status with signup_token R-->>V: state, tenant_domain when ready In prose: GET /api/v1/signup/ returns whether the door is open, the regions, the default region, the node country, the country-to-node map, and the notice ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/signup.py:114-143 ). POST /api/v1/signup/ applies a per-client hourly limit of signup_rate_limit_per_hour , counted in control_rate_limits ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/signup.py:63-85 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/signup.py:146-149 ). start_signup checks the door, validates the request, requires the current notice, refuses a domain that any live tenant already owns, and asks the payment port to check out ( src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:291-310 ). It derives a tenant key from the domain, checks the region, registers the tenant with status provisioning , and stores a Membership with status active , provisioning state queued , the notice version, and the acceptance time ( src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:312-353 ). With verification on, only an Argon2 hash of the founder's password waits on the control plane, and a verification mail goes out ( src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:344-364 ). With verification off, provisioning starts at once ( src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:366-372 ). POST /api/v1/signup/verify stamps verified_at and starts provisioning with the stored identity; an expired link answers HTTP 410 ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/signup.py:171-189 , src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:472-516 ). _provision_in_background sets the state to running , then ready , and clears the waiting hash; on failure it sets failed and logs details only for the operator ( src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:534-568 ). POST /api/v1/signup/status returns the state for a signup token and, only when ready, the s

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How ActionMeta entries reach users through the labelled Actions chip and the bottom action sheet, and how action-sheet.js runs them.
en.b: Every business step beyond create, edit, and deactivate is a metadata action ( ActionMeta ): approving, sending, converting, recalculating, opening a document. The web app never renders these as inline buttons. It offers them behind a labelled Actions chip ( toolbar.actions ) and lists them on a sheet that rises from the bottom of the screen. This page explains where actions appear, how webapp/js/action-sheet.js runs them, and how status changes travel through actions. The class itself is listed on metadata model . In short ¶ ActionMeta.scope is global , single_record , or parent ( src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:418-434 ). Module metadata declares 210 actions: 188 single_record , 21 global , and 1 parent (counted with grep -rn over src/cluster_erp/modules for ActionMeta( and each scope= value). A single_record action is offered only when every condition holds for the row ( webapp/js/action-sheet.js:20-34 ). An action runs in one of three ways: a GET endpoint opens the returned file in the viewer, an action without body fields asks for confirmation and posts, and an action with body fields opens a form ( webapp/js/action-sheet.js:118-223 ). A successful non- GET action emits the data-changed signal through GenApi.action ( webapp/js/gen-api.js:164-174 ). How it works ¶ Where actions appear ¶ Place Actions offered Source List navigation bar chip Actions All actions that are not single_record and not parent webapp/js/gen-list.js:407 , webapp/js/gen-list.js:551-562 List selection bar Actions single_record actions that apply to the one selected row; disabled for zero or several rows webapp/js/gen-list.js:614-640 Record card navigation bar Actions single_record actions that apply to the open record webapp/js/gen-form.js:2387-2393 , webapp/js/gen-form.js:2335-2337 Settings screen rows single_record actions on selected rows and other actions as global entries webapp/js/gen-settings.js:165-177 , webapp/js/gen-settings.js:225 Detail sub-lists Actions of the child entity, filtered the same way webapp/js/gen-detail.js:30 Search results Every action as a target that opens the screen where it lives webapp/js/search-index.js:78-127 The project's written engineering rules require a labelled entry chip for actions because an icon-only entry was not discovered. The list code states the same reason ( webapp/js/gen-list.js:557-559 ). The action sheet flow ¶ The flowchart follows one action from the chip to the server. flowchart TD chip["Actions chip"] --> sheet["openActionSheet"] sheet -->|"pick"| run["runEntityAction"] run --> method{"endpoint method"} method -->|"GET"| blob["apiFetchBlob"] blob --> viewer["openViewer"] method -->|"other"| body{"body_fields or body_field_groups"} body -->|"none"| confirm["confirmAlert"] confirm -->|"confirmed"| post["GenApi.action"] body -->|"present"| form["pushView with createGenForm"] form -->|"Save and valid"| post post --> signal["emitDataChanged"] post --> toast["showToast"] The same flow as steps: openActionSheet({title, subtitle, actions, onPick}) builds a modal sheet. Each row shows the action label and, when present, its description ( webapp/js/action-sheet.js:55-85 ). Escape, a tap outside the sheet, and Cancel close it; focus is trapped inside while it is open ( webapp/js/action-sheet.js:87-106 ). runEntityAction(moduleName, entityMeta, action, target, opts) reads the endpoint method ( webapp/js/action-sheet.js:118-128 ). A GET action fetches the response as a blob and opens it in the document viewer. It neither confirms nor emits a signal, and it does not call onDone ( webapp/js/action-sheet.js:129-148 ). See record documents, viewer, and share . An action without body_fields and body_field_groups shows a confirm dialog. The message is the action's description when declared, e

en.d: Reference for assistant.js, chat-task.js, and widget-ai.js, covering the chat screen and home widget of the intent assistant, and task cards.
en.b: The web app has a chat screen for the intent assistant and a home widget that shares the same conversation. The client only renders: every message goes to POST /api/v1/chat/message , and the server decides the reply. This page lists what the client sends, how it renders each reply part, and how task cards collect a record step by step. The engine is described on intent assistant . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: webapp/js/assistant.js ( renderAssistant , ensureAssistant , askAssistant , getConversation , subscribeConversation , resetAssistant ), webapp/js/chat-task.js ( ChatTask , createTaskCard ), webapp/js/widget-ai.js ( renderAiWidget ) Count: 4 reply parts handled by renderReply ( webapp/js/assistant.js:194-199 ) Opening the assistant ¶ Entry Source The assistant app, manifest id ai-assistant with screen: "assistant" src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/catalog.json:131-139 , webapp/js/home.js:2425-2426 The assistant button on the home status line ( chat.title ) webapp/js/home.js:152-155 The home widget with key ai webapp/js/home.js:292-302 Request ¶ sendToEngine(payload) posts {text, allowed_modules, ...payload} to /chat/message . allowed_modules is the installed-app scope from app-scope.js ; the comment states that the engine answers only within these modules and the caller's permissions ( webapp/js/assistant.js:201-217 ). See module apps and app scope . While a task card is active, typed text does not go to the engine. A cancel word cancels the card; anything else is answered with chat.task.use_card ( webapp/js/assistant.js:252-264 ). Reply parts ¶ Part Rendering Source content An assistant bubble webapp/js/assistant.js:195 navigate_to A bubble with chat.cannot_navigate webapp/js/assistant.js:196 actions A row of buttons; a navigate action also answers with chat.cannot_navigate webapp/js/assistant.js:139-166 , webapp/js/assistant.js:197 task_card A task card in the conversation webapp/js/assistant.js:167-192 , webapp/js/assistant.js:198 An error answer is shown as an assistant bubble with the translated error text ( webapp/js/assistant.js:211-215 ). Conversation ¶ The conversation lives in memory for the session and keeps at most 200 messages ( webapp/js/assistant.js:17 , webapp/js/assistant.js:84-90 ). The chat screen and the widget share it through getConversation and subscribeConversation ( webapp/js/assistant.js:420-437 ). The widget shows the last 40 entries and offers starter chips from each installed module's assistant_starters metadata ( webapp/js/widget-ai.js:18-28 ). tests/test_metadata_driven_rules.py:77 checks that starters are module metadata in both languages. The screen also shows file chips for attached files and a voice recorder with a timer ( webapp/js/assistant.js:275-320 ). The header comment calls the recorder cosmetic ( webapp/js/assistant.js:1-6 ); a files-only message shows the chips and sends nothing to the engine ( webapp/js/assistant.js:262 ). resetAssistant() discards the conversation, the active card, and pending files on logout and when the app is closed from the switcher ( webapp/js/assistant.js:457-467 , webapp/js/main.js:167 , webapp/js/home.js:2545 ). Task cards ¶ A task card is the client side of a server TaskCardOut : an entity type and label, a module, an API path, and a list of fields ( webapp/js/chat-task.js:1-5 , webapp/js/chat-task.js:13-38 ). Step Behaviour Source One field per step Back, skip (for optional fields), and next webapp/js/chat-task.js:47-80 Conditions A field whose condition does not hold is skipped webapp/js/chat-task.js:99-103 Foreign-key search Options come from GET /<module><endpoint> of the field's source webapp/js/chat-task.js:300-315 Summary An editable summary of every answer webapp/js/chat-task.js:81-87 , webapp/js/chat-task.js:122-135 Submit POST of the collected data to the card's API path webapp/js/chat-task.js:466-480 When the module of an active card leaves the installed-app scope, the card is cancelled ( webapp/js/assistant.js:220-230 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the web app starts in main.js, proves the session, loads the app catalogue and metadata, and calls the API through api.js and gen-api.js.
en.b: This page explains what happens between the first byte of index.html and a usable home screen, and how every later request reaches the API. It covers main.js , api.js , app-session.js , gen-api.js , meta.js , and data-bus.js in webapp/js/ . Token handling on the server is described at mechanism level on authentication and sessions . In short ¶ boot() applies stored preferences, loads the language, wires the sign-in form, and then either proves the session with GET /auth/me or shows the sign-in screen ( webapp/js/main.js:211-252 ). The session lives in HttpOnly cookies. Script code keeps only the signed-in user and the permission list as a display hint ( webapp/js/api.js:1-6 , webapp/js/api.js:26-28 ). Before the home screen appears, the app catalogue, the metadata document, and the user UI state are requested in parallel ( webapp/js/home.js:439-474 ). All metadata-driven calls go through GenApi , which builds every path from metadata endpoint declarations ( webapp/js/gen-api.js:37-61 ). document.documentElement.dataset.appReady is set to 1 when boot ends, also after a failure ( webapp/js/main.js:274-280 ). How it works ¶ Boot sequence ¶ The sequence diagram shows the path from page load to the home screen for a returning user. sequenceDiagram participant B as Browser participant S as Server participant M as main.js participant H as home.js B->>S: GET /app/ S-->>B: index.html with stamp filled in B->>M: import main.js M->>M: initPrefs, initA11y, initI18n M->>S: GET /api/v1/auth/me S-->>M: user and permissions M->>H: loadAppCatalog H->>S: GET /_meta, /_switches, /_overlay H->>S: GET /auth/ui-state H->>S: GET /app_store/registry H->>H: initHome, hydrateFromServer, restoreSession M->>B: data-app-ready = 1 In words: The server returns index.html with the asset stamp filled in ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1616-1625 at commit 7793ff4). The page loads js/main.js as a module ( webapp/index.html:406 ). boot() calls initPrefs() for theme and density and initA11y() for accessibility settings, both before first paint ( webapp/js/main.js:212-213 ). initI18n() reads i18n/languages.json , picks a language, and loads its dictionary. apply() translates the static markup ( webapp/js/main.js:218-221 ). See internationalisation and languages . Boot installs the offline banner, the sign-in form, the signup entry, the logout handler, the home duplication button, the custom select upgrade, and the table header alignment ( webapp/js/main.js:222-231 ). If a stored user exists, fetchMe() calls GET /auth/me . Success shows the home screen; failure clears the local session and shows the sign-in form ( webapp/js/main.js:233-251 ). showHome() awaits loadAppCatalog() before it reveals the home screen, so a half-initialised screen never flashes ( webapp/js/main.js:31-41 ). loadAppCatalog() starts loadMeta() and loadUiState() , then requests GET /app_store/registry . It retries once and shows home.catalog_error if both attempts fail ( webapp/js/home.js:439-474 ). initHome() applies the board profile for the device class, reconciles the saved layout, mounts the dock, the floating button, and the status line, adopts the server copy of the layout, and reopens the apps that were open before a reload ( webapp/js/home.js:4479-4562 ). Session and sign-in ¶ login() posts the user name, the password, and the remember-me flag to POST /auth/login and asks for the cookie transport. The server answers with HttpOnly cookies and the user payload. The client stores the user and the permission list in local storage ( webapp/js/api.js:185-205 ). On a multi-tenant deployment, the domain part of a company e-mail address selects the tenant ( webapp/js/api.js:179-184 ). Tenant routing is described on multi-tenancy . isAuthenticated() only checks that a stored user exists. The comment states that this hint is the only thing script code can see of the session ( webapp/js/api.js:24-28 ). The server proves the s

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the data-changed signal in data-bus.js travels from GenApi mutations to lists, stashed screens, the home screen, and bundles.
en.b: When a record is created, updated, deactivated, reactivated, or changed by an action, every screen that shows it must refresh without the user moving away and back. The web app solves this with one signal, cluster:data-changed , defined in webapp/js/data-bus.js . This page explains who emits it, who listens, how screens kept in the background catch up, and how cached data is dropped. The desktop counterpart is the signal bus described in the desktop section . In short ¶ GenApi is the single emitter for metadata-driven mutations: every mutating method calls _changed , which drops the module's cached lists and calls emitDataChanged ( webapp/js/gen-api.js:44-51 ). emitDataChanged increments a session counter and dispatches cluster:data-changed with {module, entityType, id, kind, seq} ( webapp/js/data-bus.js:11-22 ). watchData(el, cb) calls back only while the element is on screen and unsubscribes when the element is destroyed ( webapp/js/data-bus.js:33-44 ). A screen kept alive in the background compares the counter when it returns and redraws when data changed meanwhile ( webapp/js/home.js:2283-2326 ). How it works ¶ Signal path ¶ The flowchart shows the path from a mutation to the screens that refresh. flowchart LR call["GenApi create, update, remove, bulkDelete, reactivate, action"] --> changed["_changed"] changed --> inval["invalidateModule"] changed --> emit["emitDataChanged"] emit --> event["cluster:data-changed"] event --> list["makeGenList watchData"] event --> meta["meta.js overlay refresh"] event --> bundle["gated bundle watchData"] emit --> seq["dataSeq counter"] seq --> resume["unstashInto on resume"] seq --> homeseq["refreshHomeIfStale"] In words: A mutation through GenApi ( create , update , remove , bulkDelete , reactivate , or a non- GET action ) calls _changed(kind, id) ( webapp/js/gen-api.js:98-174 ). _changed calls invalidateModule(module) , which deletes every cached option list and label of that module ( webapp/js/gen-api.js:300-311 ). The comment states that all of the module's entries are dropped rather than guessing which list changed. _changed then calls emitDataChanged with the module, entity type, id, and kind ( webapp/js/gen-api.js:48-51 ). The kind is one of create , update , deactivate , activate , or action . A list that is on screen reloads when the change is in its own module and its last load is older than the change ( webapp/js/gen-list.js:368-372 , webapp/js/gen-list.js:411 ). meta.js re-applies the tenant field overlay when the entity type is tenant_field_definition or tenant_field_setting ( webapp/js/meta.js:252-256 ). Gated bundles receive emitDataChanged , watchData , and dataSeq through the platform context, so they can announce their own mutations and listen to others ( webapp/js/custom-widgets.js:85-90 ). The intranet bundle listens with watchData ( gated_apps/intranet/app.js:1175 ); the analytics, production, and projects bundles use dataSeq to invalidate their caches ( gated_apps/analytics/app.js:3944 , gated_apps/production/app.js:1065 , gated_apps/projects/app.js:696 ). Screens in the background ¶ A screen that is not on screen does not refresh at once: watchData skips the callback while the element is detached. If the element's root is a document fragment, the screen is kept alive and the listener stays; otherwise the listener removes itself ( webapp/js/data-bus.js:33-44 ). When an app is moved to the background, stashActive records dataSeq() ( webapp/js/home.js:2287-2289 ). When it returns, unstashInto redraws the top view if the counter changed, if a paint was dropped while it was away, or if a late paint landed on the empty content area. It does not redraw while a form is open, so typed input is not lost ( webapp/js/home.js:2293-2326 ). The home screen records the counter at each render and redraws when the user returns to it after a change (

h: A class change at run time
Why it is built this way
en.d: How device-class.js classifies a screen as pc, tablet, or phone, and how that sets the home grid, dock, floating button, and layout key.
en.b: The web app gives one answer to the question of what kind of screen it runs on, and every surface reads that answer. webapp/js/device-class.js defines three device classes and the thresholds between them. This page explains the decision, what each class changes, and how a class change is handled while the app runs. The home screen and dock are on home screen, dock, and launcher . In short ¶ There are three classes: pc , tablet , and phone ( webapp/js/device-class.js:22-26 ). pc means the pointer can hover and is fine, at any window width. Otherwise a window up to 640 px wide is phone and a wider one is tablet ( webapp/js/device-class.js:16-33 ). The dock mounts only on pc with a window at least 900 px wide ( webapp/js/device-class.js:17-19 , webapp/js/device-class.js:35-36 ). Each class has its own home grid and its own saved layout in the user account ( webapp/js/device-class.js:22-26 ). How it works ¶ The decision ¶ The flowchart shows how the class and the dock are decided. flowchart TD start["deviceClass"] --> fine{"matchMedia hover hover and pointer fine"} fine -->|"yes"| pc["pc: 8 x 5 board"] fine -->|"no"| width{"innerWidth up to 640"} width -->|"yes"| phone["phone: 4 x 5 board"] width -->|"no"| tablet["tablet: 6 x 5 board"] pc --> wide{"innerWidth at least 900 and not framed"} wide -->|"yes"| dock["dock mounts"] wide -->|"no"| float["floating button only"] phone --> float tablet --> float In words: hasFinePointer() tests the media query (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) ( webapp/js/device-class.js:16 , webapp/js/device-class.js:28 ). If it matches, the class is pc ( webapp/js/device-class.js:31 ). Otherwise the class is phone when window.innerWidth is at most PHONE_MAX_WIDTH (640), else tablet ( webapp/js/device-class.js:20 , webapp/js/device-class.js:32 ). isPcPointer() adds the width test PC_MIN_WIDTH (900). The dock mounts only when it is true and the page is not a duplicated tile ( webapp/js/device-class.js:19 , webapp/js/device-class.js:36 , webapp/js/app-wheel.js:87-93 ). What each class sets ¶ Class Board columns by rows Server layout key Local cache key Dock possible Source pc 8 by 5 springboard cluster_springboard yes, from 900 px webapp/js/device-class.js:23 tablet 6 by 5 springboard_tablet cluster_springboard_tablet no webapp/js/device-class.js:24 phone 4 by 5 springboard_phone cluster_springboard_phone no webapp/js/device-class.js:25 applyBoardProfile(cls) copies the columns, rows, and keys into the home screen and publishes them to CSS as --board-cols , --board-rows , and data-board-class ( webapp/js/home.js:65-79 ). Other effects of the class: The floating button is hidden only when the user docked it and isPcPointer() is true. On phones, tablets, and narrow PC windows it always stays, so an open app always has a way home ( webapp/js/home.js:1040-1047 ). Compact row density applies only on fine-pointer devices ( webapp/js/prefs.js:79-83 ). On touch, a tile must be held for 450 ms before it can be dragged; a finger that moves earlier scrolls ( webapp/js/home.js:77-82 , webapp/js/touch-gate.js:1-22 ). A class change at run time ¶ onDeviceClassChange(cb) listens to resize and to the media query, waits 120 ms for the events to settle, and calls back only when the class really changed ( webapp/js/device-class.js:38-64 ). The home screen then applies the new profile, reconciles, renders, and reads the layout for the new class from the server ( webapp/js/home.js:4481-4492 ). First use of a class ¶ When the server holds no layout for the current class and the browser has no cached one, the home screen starts from the PC layout, reflows it onto the smaller board, and saves it as the class's own layout ( webapp/js/home.js:4590-4612 ). The PC layout itself is never changed by another class ( webapp/js/device-class.js:6-14 ). Why it is bui

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How custom screens of licensed apps ship as gated_apps bundles, reach the browser through the app store asset route, and register widgets.
en.b: Most screens of the web app come from metadata, but some apps need custom screens: dashboards, boards, builders, and home widgets. That code does not ship with the public web app. Each such app has one JavaScript bundle in gated_apps/<app>/app.js at the repository root, served only to a user whose company may run the app. This page explains how a bundle is declared, fetched, loaded, and given access to platform functions. Licensing and entitlement are described on app store, licensing, and entitlements . In short ¶ There are 9 bundles: analytics , bom , calendars , intranet , inventory , nesting , procurement , production , and projects (counted with ls gated_apps/*/app.js ). Their manifests carry gated_entry: true ( src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/catalog.json ). The bundles live outside the /app static mount and are served by GET /api/v1/app_store/assets/{app_key}/{filename} ( src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/routes.py:94-155 ). The client fetches a bundle as a blob, imports it from an object URL, and calls its widgets(ctx) export ( webapp/js/custom-widgets.js:134-157 ). A bundle has no imports. Every platform function it uses arrives in ctx , the PLATFORM_CTX object with 42 distinct members ( webapp/js/custom-widgets.js:50-121 , counted from the object's keys; icon is listed twice). How it works ¶ Declaration ¶ loadAppCatalog() reads the registry and maps every module of every app with gated_entry to that app's key with setGatedApps ( webapp/js/home.js:452-457 , webapp/js/custom-widgets.js:44-48 ). The custom-widget registry starts empty; every custom widget comes from a bundle ( webapp/js/custom-widgets.js:40-42 ). The fleet app declares gated_entry: false and has no bundle ( src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/catalog.json:511-557 ). Loading ¶ The sequence diagram shows the first use of a bundle. sequenceDiagram participant V as module-app.js or gen-detail.js participant R as custom-widgets.js participant S as app_store routes V->>R: ensureModuleWidgets(module) R->>S: GET /app_store/assets/key/app.js S-->>R: bundle or 403 R->>R: Blob, createObjectURL, import R->>R: mod.widgets(PLATFORM_CTX) R->>R: REGISTRY[module.key] = factory V->>R: getCustomWidget(module, key) R-->>V: render function In words: A module app, a custom detail tab, or a module home widget calls ensureModuleWidgets(moduleName) before it builds its tabs or paints ( webapp/js/module-app.js:79-81 , webapp/js/gen-detail.js:372-379 , webapp/js/home.js:255-258 ). If the module belongs to a gated app, the client fetches /app_store/assets/<app_key>/app.js with the session cookie as a blob ( webapp/js/custom-widgets.js:134-141 ). The text is wrapped in a JavaScript blob, imported from an object URL, and the URL is revoked afterwards ( webapp/js/custom-widgets.js:142-152 ). The bundle's default export provides widgets(ctx) , which returns a map from widget name to factory. Each factory is stored under <module>.<name> ( webapp/js/custom-widgets.js:145-149 , gated_apps/inventory/app.js:1-6 ). getCustomWidget(module, key) calls the factory with the module name and r

en.d: Reference for gen-detail.js, entity.js, and avatar.js, which render a record as one scrolling card with section rows, role facets, linked records, and a photo.
en.b: makeGenDetail in webapp/js/gen-detail.js renders a record from EntityMeta.detail_view . The web app shows a detail view as one scrolling page: the form tabs merge into one record card, every other tab becomes a row that opens its own screen, and role facets and linked records follow. This page lists the tab types, the facet rules, and the helpers in entity.js and avatar.js . The record card itself is described on generic form . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: webapp/js/gen-detail.js ( makeGenDetail ), webapp/js/entity.js ( makeEntityList , adminSections ), webapp/js/avatar.js ( recordAvatarBlock , createAvatarPicker , loadPhotoInto ) Count: 9 tab types in DetailTabMeta.tab_type ( src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:255-270 ), all 9 handled by renderSection or the form card ( webapp/js/gen-detail.js:345-366 ) Page structure ¶ makeGenDetail(moduleName, entityKey, entityId) loads the record with GenApi.get and paints ( webapp/js/gen-detail.js:33-58 ): Tabs whose condition does not match the loaded record are dropped. The condition uses the same rule as form groups: a pipe-separated set, inverted by negate ( webapp/js/gen-detail.js:66-78 ). Every form tab without an entity contributes its field_groups to one record card. A form tab with no groups means all groups ( webapp/js/gen-detail.js:80-101 ). Every other tab becomes a chevron row. A tap pushes a screen rendered by renderSection ( webapp/js/gen-detail.js:103-127 ). Role facets are loaded and appended ( webapp/js/gen-detail.js:129-132 ). A record that carries entity_type and entity_id shows a Linked record row ( gen.linked_record ) that opens the owner record. The project's written engineering rules forbid hard-coded values in the metadata-driven web app. webapp/js/gen-detail.js:619-838 renders the three access tab types with fixed permission codes ( role.update at line 621, user.update at line 712) and fixed sub-paths ( /permissions/ , /roles/ , /users/ ) under the owning module. h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How home.js, tiles.js, app-wheel.js, and touch-gate.js build the home screen, dock, floating button, app switcher, and home duplication.
en.b: After sign-in the web app shows a home screen: pages of app tiles, folders, and widgets on a cell grid, a status line, and the controls that move between apps. This page explains the home screen in webapp/js/home.js , the PC dock in webapp/js/app-wheel.js , the floating button and the app switcher, the duplicate-home button in webapp/js/tiles.js , and the touch rules in webapp/js/touch-gate.js . Widgets are on home widgets ; the grid size per device is on device classes . In short ¶ The home screen is a horizontal pager. Every page is a grid of COLS by ROWS cells, and every item has explicit cell coordinates ( webapp/js/home.js:49-79 ). A new account starts with an empty home screen except the permanent Apps library tile ( webapp/js/home.js:696-707 ). On a PC with room for it, a dock shows the user's pinned apps and the running apps; pins are stored in the user account ( webapp/js/app-wheel.js:1-26 , webapp/js/home.js:977-1022 ). A floating button returns to the home screen on a single tap and opens the app switcher on a double tap ( webapp/js/home.js:2993-3014 ). The + button ( tiles.duplicate ) splits the window into up to four independent home screens ( webapp/js/tiles.js:1-11 ). How it works ¶ Pages and items ¶ state.pages is a list of pages; each page is a list of items of type app , folder , or widget , with col and row ( webapp/js/home.js:502-504 ). Saved coordinates are kept when they still fit. Anything out of bounds or overlapping is moved to the first free cell, and empty pages are removed ( webapp/js/home.js:575-595 , webapp/js/home.js:621-710 ). A full page overflows onto the next page, which is created when needed ( webapp/js/home.js:1-11 , webapp/js/home.js:2015-2027 ). reconcile() keeps a tile only while its app is installed. A tile of an app that lost its licence stays in the layout and is hidden at render time, so it returns to the same place on renewal ( webapp/js/home.js:621-635 ). Folders with fewer than two apps dissolve into loose tiles ( webapp/js/home.js:672-689 ). Gestures on the home screen ¶ Gesture Effect Source Tap a tile Opens the app, or resumes it if it is running webapp/js/home.js:2214-2221 , webapp/js/home.js:2469-2500 Drag a tile (mouse) or hold 450 ms then drag (touch) Moves the tile; on touch, movement before the hold scrolls the pager webapp/js/home.js:80-82 , webapp/js/home.js:1640-1762 Hold a dragged tile at the right or left edge for 550 ms Moves to the next or previous page, creating a page at the end webapp/js/home.js:1763-1783 Pause a dragged app over another app for 600 ms Makes a folder on drop webapp/js/home.js:1785-1806 , webapp/js/home.js:1870-1886 Right-click or long-press empty space Opens the widget gallery webapp/js/home.js:4407-4414 Swipe down on the home screen Opens search webapp/js/home.js:4446-4453 Swipe from the left quarter of an open app Leaves the app to the home screen webapp/js/home.js:2768-2852 Long-pressing an app tile asks whether to remove it from the home screen; the app stays in the Apps library. A permanent app cannot be removed ( webapp/js/home.js:782-791 ). Status line and banners ¶ The status line shows the time, the short date, and the current language code, refreshed every second ( webapp/js/home.js:104-140 ). Its buttons open search, the assistant app, and Settings › Notifications ( webapp/js/home.js:142-165 ). The language chip opens a menu of every language in the manifest ( webapp/js/home.js:167-215 ). A licence in grace or read-only state adds a banner above the home screen ( webapp/js/home.js:476-500 ). Apps library ¶ The Apps library is a menu app: it opens as a transient screen and is not added to the running apps ( webapp/js/home.js:2448-2465 ). It lists every app the user may see with search and lets the user add or remove home tiles ( webapp/js/home.js:2600-2766 ). Its catalogue manifest marks it permanent and dock_fixed ( src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/catalog.json:49-60 ). Dock on PC ¶ initAppWheel mounts the dock only when the pointer

en.t: Add a language to the web app
en.d: Add a new interface language to the web app with one dictionary file and one line in languages.json, and know which texts still need translation elsewhere.
en.b: This guide adds a new interface language to the web app in webapp/i18n/ . The language list is data, so the web app code does not change. The guide also lists the texts that do not come from the web dictionary and therefore stay in English until they are translated at their source. Background is on internationalisation and languages . Note Execution status: not executed by the writer; steps derived from webapp/js/i18n.js , webapp/i18n/languages.json , webapp/js/meta.js , and src/cluster_erp/core/asset_stamp.py . Prerequisites ¶ The language has a two-letter code that browsers report, for example de . pick() compares the first two letters of the browser language with the manifest codes ( webapp/js/i18n.js:46-52 ). You can edit files in webapp/i18n/ and deploy the web app. Steps ¶ Copy webapp/i18n/en.json to webapp/i18n/<code>.json . The file name must be the language code, because setLang loads ../i18n/<code>.json ( webapp/js/i18n.js:74-78 ). Translate every value and keep every key. en.json has 2,853 keys; a missing key shows the key itself on screen ( webapp/js/i18n.js:101-106 ). Keep each {name} placeholder unchanged inside the translated text. t() fills placeholders by name ( webapp/js/i18n.js:107-108 ). For texts with plural forms, provide the plural categories your language uses as sub-keys ( one , two , few , many , other ). tp() picks the category with Intl.PluralRules and falls back to other ( webapp/js/i18n.js:112-127 ). Translate error texts under error.<code> . When a key is missing, the server's English message is shown instead ( webapp/js/gen-api.js:16-27 ). Add one entry to webapp/i18n/languages.json with the code and the language's own name. Entries without a string code and name are ignored ( webapp/js/i18n.js:32-44 ). Illustrative manifest built from the existing entries in webapp/i18n/languages.json:1-4 , with a placeholder for the new language: json [ { "code": "tr", "name": "Türkçe" }, { "code": "en", "name": "English" }, { "code": "<code>", "name": "<native name>" } ] Deploy. The asset stamp is a digest over every file in webapp/ , so the new files get new URLs and browsers load them on the next page load ( src/cluster_erp/core/asset_stamp.py:30-42 ). See cache and asset stamp . Verify the result ¶ Settings › Language lists the new entry by its native name ( webapp/js/home.js:3670-3712 ). The language button on the sign-in screen cycles through it ( webapp/js/main.js:152-159 ). After choosing it, the root element's lang attribute is the new code and static texts change at once ( webapp/js/i18n.js:79-82 ). Dates on widgets follow the new locale through Intl.DateTimeFormat ( webapp/js/prefs.js:156-170 ). Troubleshooting ¶ Symptom Cause in code Fix The language is not offered The manifest entry lacks a string code or name , or the manifest is not valid JSON ( webapp/js/i18n.js:32-44 ) Correct the entry Choosing the language changes nothing setLang throws when <code>.json cannot be loaded ( webapp/js/i18n.js:76-77 ) Check the file name and that the file is valid JSON Keys appear on screen The key is missing from the new file ( webapp/js/i18n.js:106 ) Add the key Labels from modules stay in English Metadata labels are dictionaries in Python module metadata; resolveLabel falls back to English ( webapp/js/meta.js:284-288 ) Add the language to the module metadata labels Reference rows stay in English langLabel reads label_<code> columns and falls back to label_en ( webapp/js/meta.js:418-421 ) Provide the column data for the language Warning Discrepancy. The project's written engineering rules state that a new language needs only a new JSON file and no code change. The web dictionary and manifest follow this. Module metadata labels are LabelDict values in Python files such as src/cluster_erp/modules/currencies/metadata.py:302-304 , and the web app shows English for a language they do not contain ( webapp/js/meta.js:287 ). This page documents the code. Terms introduced ¶ Ter

en.b: This guide adds a new entity screen to an existing module app. You declare the entity in the module's metadata and add one sidebar section; the web app then shows a tab with a list, a create form, and a record card without any change in webapp/ . Background is on metadata rendering . Writing the backend routes for the entity is covered by write a backend module . Note Execution status: not executed by the writer; steps derived from src/cluster_erp/modules/currencies/module.py , src/cluster_erp/modules/currencies/metadata.py , webapp/js/module-app.js , webapp/js/gen-list.js , and src/cluster_erp/server/app.py . Prerequisites ¶ The module exists and is loaded by the module registry; see module lifecycle . The entity has HTTP routes for list, get, create, update, and delete under the module's prefix /api/v1/<module> ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:37-38 ). The module has an app in the app catalogue with screen: "module" , so it opens as a module app ( webapp/js/home.js:2429 ). The catalogue is src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/catalog.json . Steps ¶ Declare an EntityMeta for the entity in the module's metadata.py . Give labels in English and Turkish, the entity_type , and the endpoint paths relative to the module prefix. Source: src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:553-649 . From src/cluster_erp/modules/currencies/metadata.py:302-313 : python PAYMENT_TERM_META = EntityMeta( label={"en": "Payment Term", "tr": "Ödeme Koşulu"}, label_plural={"en": "Payment Terms", "tr": "Ödeme Koşulları"}, entity_type="payment_term", is_settings_entity=True, endpoints={ "list": EndpointMeta(method="GET", path="/payment-terms/"), "create": EndpointMeta(method="POST", path="/payment-terms/"), "get": EndpointMeta(method="GET", path="/payment-terms/{id}"), "update": EndpointMeta(method="PUT", path="/payment-terms/{id}"), "delete": EndpointMeta(method="DELETE", path="/payment-terms/{id}"), }, Add a list_view with columns and filters. Source: webapp/js/gen-list.js:582-597 , webapp/js/home.js:1241-1243 . Add a form with field groups. Use field_type="decimal" for money so the value travels as a string. Source: webapp/js/gen-form.js:503-506 , money and Decimal . From src/cluster_erp/modules/currencies/metadata.py:365-373 : python FieldMeta( key="code", label={"en": "Code", "tr": "Kod"}, field_type="string", required=True, max_length=20, weight="hero", immutable_on_edit=True, ), If the record needs a card with several sections, add a detail_view with tabs. Without one, a row opens a read-only record card built from the form. Source: webapp/js/gen-list.js:816-844 . Register the entity in ModuleMeta.entities and add a sidebar section with view_type="list" that names the entity key. Source: webapp/js/module-app.js:115-116 . From src/cluster_erp/modules/currencies/module.py:132-141 : python SidebarSectionMeta( key="payment_term_list", label={ "en": "Payment Terms", "tr": "Ödeme Koşulları", }, view_type="list", icon="payments", entity="payment_term", ), If the screen needs a specific permission beyond the entity's own codes, set required_permission on the section. Source: webapp/js/module-app.js:106-108 . Restart the server. The metadata document is built once per process, and permission codes for each entity are seeded from metadata at start-up. Source: src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1530-1543 and src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:634-858 at commit 7793ff4. h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How i18n.js loads the language manifest and dictionaries, resolves keys and plurals, switches language at run time, and how metadata labels follow the language.
en.b: Every text the web app shows comes either from a language file in webapp/i18n/ or from a label dictionary in server metadata. This page explains the language manifest, how webapp/js/i18n.js picks and loads a language, how keys, parameters, and plurals resolve, and what happens on a language switch. Adding a language is a task on add a language to the web app . In short ¶ The available languages are data: webapp/i18n/languages.json lists tr (Türkçe) and en (English) ( webapp/i18n/languages.json:1-4 ). en.json and tr.json each hold 2,853 keys under 68 top-level groups, and both files have the same key set (counted by flattening both files with a JSON parser and comparing the key sets). t(key, params) resolves a dotted key and fills {name} placeholders; a missing key returns the key itself ( webapp/js/i18n.js:101-109 ). tp(key, n) picks the plural form from Intl.PluralRules ( webapp/js/i18n.js:112-127 ). Metadata labels resolve through resolveLabel , which falls back to English ( webapp/js/meta.js:284-288 ). How it works ¶ Choosing the language ¶ initI18n() loads the manifest, then calls setLang(pick()) ( webapp/js/i18n.js:54-72 ). pick() uses, in order ( webapp/js/i18n.js:46-52 ): the code stored in local storage under cluster_lang , if it is in the manifest; the first two letters of the browser language, if they are in the manifest; tr ( DEFAULT_LANG ), if it is in the manifest; the first manifest entry. If the manifest cannot be loaded, the list falls back to tr alone so the app still boots ( webapp/js/i18n.js:14-16 , webapp/js/i18n.js:32-44 ). If the dictionary cannot be loaded, the app continues with the markup's own text ( webapp/js/i18n.js:56-62 ). Switching language ¶ setLang(code) loads i18n/<code>.json , stores the code, sets lang on the root element, translates the visible markup with apply() , and dispatches cluster:lang-changed ( webapp/js/i18n.js:74-87 ). Three places change the language: Place Behaviour Source Sign-in screen language button Cycles through every manifest entry webapp/js/main.js:152-159 , webapp/js/i18n.js:91-95 Home status line language chip A menu of every manifest entry webapp/js/home.js:167-215 Settings › Language ( common.language ) A list with a check mark on the active entry webapp/js/home.js:3670-3712 Listeners of cluster:lang-changed : gen-api.js clears every cached option list and label, because server-resolved names depend on the language ( webapp/js/gen-api.js:366-371 ). home.js marks every running app as stale; a stale app is redrawn when the user returns to it ( webapp/js/home.js:2334-2342 , webapp/js/home.js:2501-2511 ). Duplicated home tiles follow a change made in another tile through the storage event ( webapp/js/i18n.js:63-71 ). Applying text ¶ apply(root) fills four attribute families from the dictionary ( webapp/js/i18n.js:129-144 ): Attribute Target data-i18n Text content data-i18n-ph placeholder data-i18n-aria aria-label data-i18n-title title Screens built in code call t() directly. apiErrorText translates server error codes through keys of the form error.<code> and uses the server's English message when no translation exists ( webapp/js/gen-api.js:11-35 ). Language sent to the server ¶ Every API call carries Accept-Language with the current code, so names the server resolves (units, categories, reference labels) come back in the same language ( webapp/js/api.js:18-22 ). See reference data and core i18n . Metadata labels and reference rows ¶ Labels in metadata are dictionaries such as {"en": "...", "tr": "..."} . resolveLabel returns the current language, then English ( webapp/js/meta.js:283-288 ). Reference rows that carry one column per language use langLabel , which reads label_<lang> , then label_en , then code ( webapp/js/meta.js:416-421 ). App manifest labels follow the same rule ( webapp/js/home.js:520 ). Dates and numbers ¶ Dates in lists use a fixed YYYY-MM-DD pattern in the user's time zone ( webapp/js/prefs.js:150-154 ). Short date and time on widge

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the web app turns the server's metadata document into module tabs, lists, forms, record cards, trees, settings screens, and actions.
en.b: The web app has no screen code per entity. It reads the metadata document that every module publishes, prunes it for the signed-in user and the tenant, and hands each part to a generic engine. This page explains that path from GET /api/v1/_meta to a painted screen. The metadata classes themselves are listed on metadata model . In short ¶ loadMeta() loads /_meta , /_switches , and /_overlay once per session and keeps the result in memory ( webapp/js/meta.js:16-47 ). Three passes run before any screen reads the document: permission pruning, display-switch pruning, and the tenant field overlay ( webapp/js/meta.js:29-38 ). A module app turns each sidebar section into a tab by its view_type ( webapp/js/module-app.js:101-139 ).
