en.d: How module-app.js turns a backend module into an app with tabs, how running apps stay alive, and how app-scope.js publishes modules.
en.b: In the web app a backend module is used as an app: it opens from the home screen, shows its sections as tabs, and keeps running in the background when the user leaves it. This page explains the app catalogue entries the client reads, how webapp/js/module-app.js builds a module app, how running apps keep their screens, and how webapp/js/app-scope.js publishes which modules are installed. The home screen itself is on home screen, dock, and launcher . In short ¶ The client knows its apps only from GET /app_store/registry , which returns each app's manifest and its entitlement state for the signed-in user ( webapp/js/home.js:409-419 , src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/routes.py:18-40 ). The catalogue file holds 28 app manifests; their screen values are module (20), list (2), and one each of settings , library , store , assistant , mail , and appmgr (counted by parsing src/cluster_erp/modules/app_store/catalog.json ). screenRenderer(a) maps the screen value to a render function; module becomes makeModuleScreen ( webapp/js/home.js:2415-2441 ). makeModuleScreen turns each sidebar section into a tab of a bottom tab bar ( webapp/js/module-app.js:69-235 ). Leaving an app keeps its live screen in memory; only the switcher's close resets it ( webapp/js/home.js:2252-2326 , webapp/js/home.js:2535-2557 ). How it works ¶ App manifests ¶ Each registry entry carries a manifest from the catalogue. The client reads these manifest fields: Field Use in the client Source id , label , glyph , color , bg Tile, dock icon, and title webapp/js/home.js:520 , webapp/js/home.js:1063-1070 screen Which renderer opens the app webapp/js/home.js:2415-2441 module , modules The backend module the app shows, and every module it covers webapp/js/home.js:794-800 , webapp/js/home.js:2429 entity , endpoint The entity of a list app webapp/js/home.js:2431-2437 tableList Full-column tables in the app's lists webapp/js/home.js:2429-2437 menu The app opens as a transient menu, not a running app webapp/js/home.js:2452-2465 , webapp/js/home.js:2469-2473 permanent The tile cannot be removed from the home screen webapp/js/home.js:742-744 dock_fixed The app is pinned at the start of the dock and cannot be unpinned webapp/js/home.js:990-997 folder The app joins a system folder when added to the home screen webapp/js/home.js:762-780 gated_entry The app's custom code ships as a gated bundle webapp/js/home.js:452-457 The state map from the registry hides an app on every surface unless it is installed, licensed, and seat-assigned to one of the user's roles ( webapp/js/home.js:425-430 ). The layers behind these flags are described on app store, licensing, and entitlements . Building a module app ¶ makeModuleScreen(moduleName, {table, accent}) returns a render function that waits for metadata and for the module's gated bundle, then reads the module's sidebar ( webapp/js/module-app.js:69-101 ): Sections with hidden_from_bar are skipped. en.d: Layout of the webapp folder, how the server serves it under /app with a content stamp, and the metadata-driven rule that shapes every screen.
en.b: The web app is a single-page browser client kept in the webapp/ folder at the repository root. The API server serves it from the same origin under /app , so the browser calls /api/v1 without cross-origin requests. This page describes the folder layout, how files are served and cached, and the rule that screens come from server metadata. Start-up and the API layer are on boot, session, and API calls . In short ¶ The web app is plain ES modules with no build step: index.html loads one module script, js/main.js ( webapp/index.html:406 ). webapp/js/ holds 51 JavaScript files plus the vendor/ folder (counted with ls webapp/js : 52 entries). The server mounts the folder twice: /app with revalidation on every load, and /app/v/<stamp>/ as immutable files ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1633-1644 at commit 7793ff4). Every list, form, card, action, and module tab is built from GET /api/v1/_meta ( webapp/js/meta.js:16-47 ). The project's written engineering rules make the web app fully metadata-driven. en.d: How ui-state.js and the auth ui_state routes keep a user's home layout, dock, density, and search history on the server, and which preferences stay in the browser.
en.b: A user's arrangement of the web app belongs to the user account, not to one browser. The client module webapp/js/ui-state.js reads and writes named values through two routes of the auth module, and the server stores them per user in the table auth_user_ui_state . This page explains the data model, the routes, the write coalescing, the conflict rule for the home layout, and which preferences are not stored on the server. In short ¶ One row holds one key and one JSON value for one user; the key is unique among live rows of that user ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/models.py:13-35 ). GET /api/v1/auth/ui-state returns every key of the signed-in user; PUT /api/v1/auth/ui-state/{key} stores one value ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/routes.py:21-39 ). Both routes take the user id from the session, never from the request, and require authentication only ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/routes.py:15-18 ). A stored value may be at most 262,144 bytes as JSON ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/schemas.py:8-29 ). The client batches writes for 600 ms and flushes pending writes when the page is hidden or closed ( webapp/js/ui-state.js:41-73 ). How it works ¶ Server side ¶ Part Content Source Model UserUiState Table auth_user_ui_state ; user_id (foreign key to auth_users.id ), key (up to 60 characters), value (JSONB), plus the base columns src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/models.py:13-35 Unique index uq_auth_user_ui_state_user_id_key_live on user_id and key where deleted_at IS NULL src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/models.py:24-29 Schema UiStateWrite value of any JSON shape, rejected when not serialisable or larger than _MAX_UI_STATE_BYTES src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/schemas.py:10-29 Service UiStateService.all_for Returns {key: value} for live rows of one user src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/services.py:19-28 Service UiStateService.put Inserts a row or updates the live row's value src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/services.py:30-44 Route registration Included in the auth module router under /api/v1/auth src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/module.py:55 , src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/module.py:68 , src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:37-38 The base columns and soft delete come from the shared base model; see base model and ids . An update of a value is recorded by the automatic change history like any other mapped entity; see change history . Client side ¶ loadUiState() reads all keys once per session and shares one request among early callers. A failed read returns null and leaves the local copy in use ( webapp/js/ui-state.js:18-39 ). saveUiState(key, value) updates the in-memory copy, queues the value, and restarts a 600 ms timer; the flush sends one PUT per key with keepalive so that a write survives a page reload ( webapp/js/ui-state.js:41-73 ). visibilitychange to hidden and pagehide flush the queue at once ( webapp/js/ui-state.js:58-65 ). Logout drops the cache and the queue ( webapp/js/ui-state.js:75-85 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the desktop client calls the server through ApiClient, runs calls in QThread workers with ApiMixin, maps errors, and builds entity calls with GenericApi.
en.b: This page explains how the desktop client reaches the server API. It covers core/api_client.py ( ApiClient and its error classes), core/api_worker.py ( ApiWorker , ApiMixin , format_api_error ), core/generic_api.py ( GenericApi ), and core/core_api.py (notes, attachments, and e-mail wrappers), all under src/cluster_erp/desktop/ . The change signals that mutations emit are described on signal bus and watch_entity . In short ¶ One ApiClient wraps one httpx.Client with a 30-second timeout, a base address, and an Accept-Language header ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:80-96 ). Screens run calls in ApiWorker , a QThread , through ApiMixin.call_api . Results and errors come back as Qt signals ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_worker.py:28-65 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_worker.py:187-259 ). A mutation called with an entity descriptor emits a change signal after the server answers ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:223-294 ). HTTP errors become typed exceptions, and format_api_error turns them into a message in the user's language ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:55-77 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_worker.py:108-176 ). GenericApi builds every entity path from the endpoint declarations in the metadata ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/generic_api.py:24-31 ). How it works ¶ The API client ¶ ApiClient.__init__ creates the httpx.Client with the base address, a 30-second timeout, redirects followed, and Accept-Language set to en ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:81-91 ). main() then sets the language of the translator, and every language change updates the header ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/main.py:169-172 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:110-112 ). set_base_url replaces the httpx.Client and keeps its headers ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:98-108 ). login posts the user name and the password to /auth/login . On success it keeps the access token, the refresh token, the user, and the permission list in memory and attaches the access token to every later request ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:134-163 ). The tokens are not written to the settings store: the only settings keys the client writes are listed on languages, themes, and accessibility . logout clears all four in memory ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:165-171 ). Token handling on the server is described on authentication and sessions . _request sends one request. When the answer is 401, it calls _try_refresh_token once and repeats the request once if the refresh worked ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:335-349 ). A failed refresh clears the tokens and emits session_expired on the signal bus ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:173-211 ). A 204 answer returns None ; any other success returns the parsed JSON ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:350-353 ). download follows the same refresh rule and returns the bytes, the content type, and the file name ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:296-324 ). The lock in ApiClient is held only to read the current httpx.Client and around a token refresh, not for the whole round trip. The comment states that a slow background request would otherwise freeze calls from the GUI thread ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:336-341 ). Error classes ¶ _parse_error_response maps the status code to an exception class and reads the server's error body. A body with an error object fills message , code , trace_id , and details ; another body fills only the message from detail ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:64-77 ). A transport failure raises ApiError with status 0 and code CONNECTION_ERROR ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:359-364 ). This reference describes ChatWidget , TaskCard , and the task model in src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/ : how a typed message becomes an answer, a navigation, or a guided record creation. The intent engine that the panel uses is documented on intent assistant . The web client's chat screens are on assistant and chat screens . Count: three Python files with code (2,827, 1,040, and 316 lines) and two background images in assets/ , counted by listing the folder. Placement and signals ¶ MainWindow places the panel as the third column of its splitter. The chat button of the sidebar (key sidebar.chat ) and the panel's own close button toggle its width between zero and the last width, 380 pixels by default ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/main_window.py:103-122 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/main_window.py:217-229 ). Signal Arguments Received by Source close_requested none MainWindow._toggle_chat src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:796 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/main_window.py:111 navigation_requested module, section MainWindow._on_navigate src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:797 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/main_window.py:112 Intent engine ¶ The panel creates an IntentEngine from cluster_erp.ai.intent_engine and loads it 100 ms after construction ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:47 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:818-819 ). IntentEngine.load reads the en and tr intent corpora from files and fits one vectoriser per language ( src/cluster_erp/ai/intent_engine.py:364-394 ). Recognition therefore runs inside the desktop process. The panel does not call the server's chat routes; a search of the folder for /chat paths returns no match. Message flow ¶ _on_send adds the user's message and any picked files to the conversation, then decides in this order ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:1379-1493 ): While a task card is active, a cancel word cancels it, and any other text asks the user to use the card ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:1393-1418 ). Small talk is answered from fixed phrase lists in ten categories: help, name, company, identity, permissions, time, mood, thanks, farewell, and greeting ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:1115-1135 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:1472-1476 ). A message with several requests is split, and the parts are processed one after the other ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:1238-1300 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:1479-1493 ). _process_intent shows a typing indicator and starts recognition ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:1495-1499 ). _do_recognize_inner asks the engine for the five best matches ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:1534-1535 ). With no match it answers with the text of chat.no_intent_found . When the best confidence is below 0.60, it lists the three best candidates and asks the user to rephrase ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/chat/chat_widget.py:1552-1576 ). en.d: How the desktop MetadataStore loads and prunes server metadata, hides modules by app scope, registers labels, and how FkCache loads and caches option lists.
en.b: The desktop client draws its screens from the metadata that the server publishes. This page explains how core/metadata_store.py loads and adjusts that metadata, how core/fk_cache.py loads and caches the option lists of foreign-key fields, and what core/entity_types.py declares, all under src/cluster_erp/desktop/ . The server-side contract is described on metadata model . How the web client does the same is on metadata rendering . In short ¶ MetadataStore.load reads GET /_meta and then applies display switches, permission-gated fields, the tenant field overlay, and the app scope, in that order ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:19-32 ). A failure of any step after /_meta leaves the metadata as shipped and hides nothing ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:39-82 ). register_labels copies every metadata label into the translator under meta.<module>... keys ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:119-192 ). FkCache pages through an option list 200 rows at a time, keeps it for 300 seconds, keeps at most 50 lists, and drops a module's lists on any change signal of that module ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/fk_cache.py:13-14 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/fk_cache.py:51-77 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/fk_cache.py:164-214 ). How it works ¶ Loading metadata ¶ load() runs once at start-up, before the main window exists. main() retries it up to three times ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/main.py:194-222 ). The steps are: GET /_meta fills the raw document. A failure returns False ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:20-27 ). _apply_switches reads GET /_switches and calls prune_switched_off . A field or column whose switch is off is removed from forms, list views, sub-tables, and action bodies. An unknown switch counts as on ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:52-60 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:443-473 ). prune_gated_fields removes every field that names a permission the user does not hold, in form groups and in action forms ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:231-265 ). _apply_field_overlay reads GET /_overlay and calls apply_field_overlay ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:39-46 ). _load_app_scope reads GET /app_store/registry and computes the hidden modules ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:67-82 ). Tenant field overlay ¶ apply_field_overlay changes the metadata in place for each entity in the overlay ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:268-440 ): A shipped field that the tenant switched off leaves its group. It moves, read-only and not required, into one group with the key closed_fields that is shown only on existing records ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:308-328 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:429-440 ). A shipped field with a required override becomes required ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:325-326 ). A tenant-defined field joins its target group with storage set to extra . A field with a condition gets its own conditional group right after the target group. A field gated by a permission is added only for holders ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:329-394 ). A tenant field marked for the list gets a column keyed extra.<key> , inserted after the stretching column ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:395-410 ). Action forms that collect a field bucket follow the same switches and receive the tenant fields of that bucket, except derived fields ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:392-394 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metadata_store.py:411-428 ). The server side of tenant fields is described on tenant fields . App scope ¶ hidden_modules(registry) returns the modules that are covered only by apps the user cannot use. An app is usable when its manifest is system or permanent , or when its state is installed, entitled, and seated. A module that no app covers is never hidden ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/metad

en.d: What the PySide6 desktop client in src/cluster_erp/desktop is, how it starts, signs in, loads metadata, and which packaging and Qt version rules apply.
en.b: The desktop client is a Qt application in src/cluster_erp/desktop/ that talks to a Cluster ERP server over its HTTP API. This page explains its folder layout, the start-up and sign-in sequence in desktop/main.py , the desktop install extra, and the PySide6 version note. Each part of the client has its own page in the desktop section . How to start it is on run the desktop client . In short ¶ The entry point is main() in src/cluster_erp/desktop/main.py:110-130 . pyproject.toml:88 also installs it as the console script cluster-erp-desktop . Start-up creates the settings store, the theme engine, accessibility, the translator, the API client, and the signal bus, then shows the sign-in dialog ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/main.py:162-190 ). After sign-in the client loads the server metadata, with up to three attempts, and exits if all fail ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/main.py:194-222 ). Screens are built from metadata by the generic widgets. Ten section keys map to hand-written screens ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/main_window.py:501-528 ). PySide6 is an optional dependency in the desktop extra, so a server install carries no GUI toolkit ( pyproject.toml:68-74 ). How it works ¶ Folder layout ¶ The package has five folders. The counts below were made by listing src/cluster_erp/desktop/ at the verified commit: 86 Python files, of which 69 are not empty, with 34,331 lines of Python in total. Folder Holds Page core/ API client, worker threads, generic API, signal bus, metadata store, foreign-key cache, tab manager, pane controller, settings store, accessibility, time-zone helpers, preview files API client and workers i18n/ translator.py , en.json , tr.json Languages, themes, and accessibility themes/ theme_engine.py , style.qss Languages, themes, and accessibility widgets/ Main window, sidebar, status bar, panes, dialogs, and the common/ , generic/ , and chat/ widget folders Generic widgets modules/ Hand-written screens in bom , calendars , inventory , logs , procurement , production , and an empty purchasing_quotations package Module screens Warning Discrepancy. The project's written engineering rules list desktop module folders parties , owned_organisations , and products_and_services , each with its own api.py wrapper ( PartiesApi , ProductsApi , OrganisationsApi ). The folder src/cluster_erp/desktop/modules/ contains bom , calendars , inventory , logs , procurement , production , and purchasing_quotations . No file named api.py and no class with those three names exists under src/cluster_erp/desktop/ . en.d: Install the desktop extra, start the PySide6 client, and sign in to a running Cluster ERP server from a workstation.
en.b: This guide installs the PySide6 desktop client on a workstation and signs in to a Cluster ERP server. It covers the desktop install extra, the start command, the sign-in dialog, and the most common start-up failures. Background is on the desktop client overview . Starting the server itself is described on server start-up and app factory . Note Execution status: not executed by the writer; steps derived from pyproject.toml , src/cluster_erp/desktop/main.py , src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/login_dialog.py , and src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/preferences_dialog.py . Prerequisites ¶ Python 3.12 or later ( pyproject.toml:9 ). A reachable Cluster ERP server. The client reads its address from the setting api_url and uses a local default when the setting is empty ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/main.py:167 ). A user account on that server. The client signs in with a user name and a password ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:134-140 ). Steps ¶ Install the package with the desktop extra from the repository root. The comment in pyproject.toml:68-71 names this form for a workstation; the extra adds PySide6 ( pyproject.toml:72-74 ). powershell pip install -e .[desktop] If you choose a PySide6 version yourself, use 6.8.3. The comment in pyproject.toml:70-71 names 6.8.3 as known-good on Windows and 6.11.0 as failing with a DLL error. CI checks the client against 6.8.3 ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:50 ). Start the client. main() runs when the module is executed ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/main.py:243-244 ). The same function is installed as the console script cluster-erp-desktop ( pyproject.toml:88 ). powershell python -m cluster_erp.desktop.main In the sign-in dialog, check the Server field ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/i18n/en.json key auth.server ). It is an editable list of the last ten addresses that signed in successfully, and it starts with the client's current address ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/login_dialog.py:108-124 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/login_dialog.py:274-283 ). Type the API base address of your server, for example https://erp.example.com/api/v1 . Optionally pick the interface language and open Accessibility (key accessibility.title ) from the bottom row of the dialog ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/login_dialog.py:214-240 ). Enter the user name and the password, then select Sign In (key auth.login_button ). The client sends the request in a worker thread ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/login_dialog.py:287-309 ). On success it stores the server address in the settings server_urls and api_url and closes the dialog ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/login_dialog.py:311-314 ). If you later need another server, change Server URL (key settings.api_url ) in Preferences (key settings.title ) and restart the client. The dialog saves the value and asks for a restart when it changed ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/preferences_dialog.py:117-133 ). Verify the result ¶ The main window opens with a sidebar, a welcome tab, and a status bar ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/main_window.py:69-137 ). The status bar shows Connected (key app.connected ) when GET /health on the server root answers 200 ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/status_bar.py:56-88 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py:326-333 ). It checks every 15 seconds ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/status_bar.py:49-51 ). The sidebar lists only sections that the server metadata declares, that the user may read, and whose apps the user may use ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/sidebar.py:159-240 ). See metadata store and foreign-key cache . The dialog shows the text of app.connection_error with a transport message The request failed before any HTTP answer; status 0 is used for transport errors ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/api_client.py

en.d: How the desktop main window, sidebar, split panes, tab manager, and pane controller open, track, close, and persist screens.
en.b: The desktop main window is a sidebar, a pane area that can be split, and a chat panel side by side. Each pane holds tabs, and each tab holds one screen. This page explains widgets/main_window.py , widgets/sidebar.py , widgets/pane_container.py , widgets/pane_widget.py , core/tab_manager.py , and core/pane_controller.py under src/cluster_erp/desktop/ . The screens inside the tabs are described on generic widgets and module screens . In short ¶ MainWindow puts Sidebar , PaneContainer , and ChatWidget in one horizontal splitter, with StatusBarWidget below ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/main_window.py:69-137 ). A sidebar click opens a section tab. If the same section is already open in any pane, that tab is activated instead ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/main_window.py:314-343 ). TabManager keeps one TabDescriptor per tab, refuses duplicates of the same module, section, and record, and asks before closing a tab with unsaved changes ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/tab_manager.py:17-24 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/tab_manager.py:87-161 ). PaneContainer splits panes in nested QSplitter widgets and saves the layout, with the open section tabs, in the local setting panes/layout ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/pane_container.py:28 , src/cluster_erp/desktop/widgets/pane_container.py:261-272 ). PaneController offers the same pane and tab operations through string ids and plain dictionaries ( src/cluster_erp/desktop/core/pane_controller.py:23-30 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How each module declares its analysable data in analytics_facts.py and how the analytics module collects, validates, and permission-filters those fact sets over the EventBus.
en.b: This page explains how data reaches the analytics module. Nine modules each keep a file analytics_facts.py that declares one or more fact sets. The analytics module emits DescribeAnalyticsFacts on the EventBus, collects the answers in src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/registry.py , validates them, and builds the catalogue every analysis reads. No module imports the analytics module, and the analytics module imports no module ( src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2055-2057 ). In short ¶ A fact set ( AnalyticsFactSet ) names its module, a key, a label, its grain, the physical source table, its dimensions and measures, a read permission, and a live filter ( src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2126-2154 ). Each contributing module subscribes a handler to DescribeAnalyticsFacts that returns its fact sets ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/module.py:338-346 ). registry.collect emits the event, type-checks and validates every answer, refuses duplicates, and returns a FactCatalogue ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/registry.py:242-283 ). A caller sees only fact sets whose read_permission they hold ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/registry.py:100-109 ). How it works ¶ Collection path ¶ sequenceDiagram participant S as AnalyticsService participant R as registry.collect participant B as EventBus participant M as module analytics_facts.py S->>R: catalogue(permission_codes, locale) R->>B: emit DescribeAnalyticsFacts B->>M: describe_analytics_facts(event) M-->>B: AnalyticsFactSet or list B-->>R: results of all handlers R->>R: type check, validate_fact, duplicate key check R-->>S: FactCatalogue S->>S: visible_to(permission_codes) In prose: AnalyticsService.catalogue calls registry.collect with the caller's locale ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/service.py:55-62 ). collect emits DescribeAnalyticsFacts(source_module="analytics", locale=...) . The locale only selects labels; keys stay language independent ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/registry.py:253 , src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2060-2073 ). The EventBus calls every subscribed handler and returns their results. A handler that raises is logged and contributes nothing ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:83-96 ). collect accepts one fact set or a list per handler. Anything else fails with ANALYTICS_INVALID_CONTRIBUTION ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/registry.py:254-266 ). validate_fact checks each set; a second set with the same key fails instead of overwriting ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/registry.py:267-277 ). visible_to keeps the sets whose read_permission is among the caller's permission codes ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/registry.py:100-109 ). en.d: Reference for analytics period series on a calendar spine, baseline forecasts and scaled errors, ABC and SBC classification, and saved analysis models.
en.b: This page describes four files of the analytics module in src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/ : series.py (period series with visible gaps), forecasting.py (baseline forecasts and error metrics), classification.py (ABC and SBC classes), and saved_models.py (named, re-runnable analyses). Forecasting and classification use Decimal arithmetic throughout ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/forecasting.py:1-4 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/classification.py:1-4 ). Scope and source ¶ Defined in: period_series , values_of , grouped_period_totals , stratified_counts ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:79-478 ); forecast_baseline , scaling_denominator , accuracy , rolling_origin , compare_baselines ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/forecasting.py:88-373 ); classify_abc , classify_sbc ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/classification.py:56 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/classification.py:246 ); SavedModelService ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/saved_models.py:88 ). Routes: GET /analysis/series/{fact_key} , GET /analysis/baselines/{fact_key} , GET /analysis/abc/{fact_key} , GET /analysis/sbc/{fact_key} , and the /analysis/models routes ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/routes.py:168-310 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/routes.py:946-1069 ). Period series ¶ period_series returns one value per period for every period in the window, by generating the periods and joining the aggregate onto them ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:1-36 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:79-95 ). Parameter Values Source grain the grains declared on the date dimension src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:57-75 aggregation sum , avg , min , max ; a missing value column counts rows src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:76 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:93-94 gap_policy gap (default, a period without rows is null with has_rows false) or zero (the caller chooses zero, and the answer records it) src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:53 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:18-36 filters equality-only selections on declared categorical dimensions src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:93-95 The docstring explains the rule: a month without rows must not look like a month with zero demand, because that hides stockouts and misclassifies lumpy items ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/series.py:7-30 ). Baseline forecasts and errors ¶ Item Values Source Baselines mean , naive , seasonal_naive , drift src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/forecasting.py:55 Metrics computed mase , rmsse , mae , rmse src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/forecasting.py:59 Metrics refused with an explanation mape , smape , mdape , gmrae src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/forecasting.py:60 Rules ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/forecasting.py:24-45 ): Accuracy is only computed out of sample, with a rolling origin; no in-sample accuracy figure is produced ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/forecasting.py:247 ). MASE and RMSSE scale by the in-sample error of the naive forecast over the training span only; a zero denominator is refused ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/forecasting.py:163-197 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How analytics turns semantic keys into safe SQL, which correctness gates refuse wrong totals, and how preparation recipes run and measure each step.
en.b: This page explains the query path of the analytics module. src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/registry.py holds the validated catalogue, src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/query_builder.py builds safe aggregate queries with correctness gates, and src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/recipe_engine.py with recipe_schemas.py runs declarative preparation recipes. How the catalogue is filled by other modules is on analytics facts . In short ¶ A user asks with semantic keys only: a fact, measures, dimensions, filters, order, and a page ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/schemas.py:1-11 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/schemas.py:47-61 ). Table and column names come only from module declarations; values are bound parameters. There is no string concatenation into SQL ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/query_builder.py:5-10 ). Four gates refuse a number that would be wrong: non-additive sums, semi-additive sums over an unpinned axis, mixed currencies, and dates without a grain ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/query_builder.py:11-23 ). A recipe is a stored list of steps from a closed vocabulary; the engine records rows in and rows out for each step ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/recipe_engine.py:1-21 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/recipe_schemas.py:1-33 ). How it works ¶ The recipe and query pipeline ¶ flowchart TD A["POST /analysis/run with AnalysisSpec"] --> C["AnalyticsService.catalogue: collect and visible_to"] P["POST /analysis/prepare with RecipeDefinition"] --> C C --> F["FactCatalogue.get fact"] F --> S{"summaries.plan fits"} S -->|yes| QS["query_builder._build_from_summary"] S -->|no| QB["query_builder.build"] QB --> G["gates: additivity, currency, grain"] QS --> G G --> X["execute, cap at MAX_ROWS"] X --> R["AnalysisResult with source summary or live"] F --> RE["RecipeEngine.run"] RE --> ST["apply steps, count rows in and out"] ST --> EX["check expectations"] EX --> RR["RecipeRunResult with observations"] In prose: Both entry points first build the caller's catalogue: registry.collect asks every module, and visible_to keeps only fact sets whose read_permission the caller holds ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/service.py:55-62 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/registry.py:100-109 ). For a run, summaries.plan decides whether the pre-aggregated cells can answer; otherwise the query runs on the fact table ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/service.py:139-148 ). See reports, summaries, and cross . query_builder.build builds one relation with all declared columns, adds grouped dimensions, measures, filters, the live filter, order, and a page of at most MAX_ROWS 10000 plus one row to detect truncation ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/query_builder.py:71-96 , src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/query_builder.py:375-470 ). The result states whether it came from summary or live , and why the live path was taken ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/service.py:157-168 ). For a recipe, the engine starts from every declared column keyed by its semantic name, applies the live filter, runs each enabled step, and measures the row count before and after ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/recipe_engine.py:195-262 ). Correctness gates ¶ Gate Refuses Error code Source Additivity sum or avg of a non_additive measure ANALYTICS_NON_ADDITIVE src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/query_builder.py:242-272 Semi-additive axis sum of a semi_additive measure unless its non_additive_on dimension is pinned with eq ANALYTICS_SEMI_ADDITIVE_AXIS src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/query_builder.py:274-288 Currency an aggregate of a monetary measure without a currency breakdown or a single-currency eq filter; count and count_distinct are exempt ANALYTICS_MIXED_CURRENCY src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/query_builder.py:290-335 Grain a date dimension without an explicit,

Every method turns its precondition into a gate and refuses to answer when the precondition fails ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/statistics.py:1-14 ). en.d: Module page for costing, which rolls a BOM version up into material, labour, nesting, scrap, and overhead costs, a suggested price, and an approval flow.
en.b: The costing module in src/cluster_erp/modules/costing/ costs a BOM version. A costing analysis reads the BOM explosion, applies labour and overhead rates, adds an optional nesting cost, and stores a cost breakdown, a total, a suggested price for a target margin, and a low-margin flag. An analysis then goes through submission, approval, or rejection, and an approved analysis linked to a quotation reports its price back. Labour rates and overhead rates are the module's own reference records. en.d: Module page for design_engineering, which holds designs with review and approval and the engineering change notes that create new design versions.
en.b: The design_engineering module in src/cluster_erp/modules/design_engineering/ holds designs and engineering change notes (ECN). A design belongs to a project, can name the part it describes, links its drawing, 3D model, and DXF documents, and goes through review and approval. An approved design is locked; a change goes through an ECN, which creates the next design version and supersedes the old one. Approving a design with a part makes the bom module create a BOM card. A wrong reading is marked incorrect and the chain after it is recomputed ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/meters/services.py:9-12 ). The meter row is locked for the duration of the post, so two posts cannot read the same predecessor ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/meters/services.py:244-254 ). After a post, the asset's last_odometer_km is synchronised by reading date and the maintenance reminders are recomputed ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/meters/services.py:308-311 ). en.d: How fleet computes total cost of ownership and the renewal ranking, keeps tires and campaigns, ingests telematics counters, and feeds analytics.
en.b: This page explains four parts of the fleet module that read across its ledgers. src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/ computes total cost of ownership (TCO), ranks assets for renewal, and keeps tires, campaigns, and emission factors. src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/telematics.py ingests counter batches, src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/analytics_facts.py publishes fleet facts to the analytics module, and src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/validation.py holds shared input checks. In short ¶ TCO sums what the ledgers recorded over a window of months and divides by the kilometres the odometer moved ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:1-8 ). The renewal ranking lists active and in-maintenance assets by cost per kilometre, highest first ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:63-91 ). The telematics feed turns device counters into ordinary reading documents with source telematics ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/telematics.py:1-16 ). Four fact sets go to analytics through the DescribeAnalyticsFacts contract ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/analytics_facts.py:300-310 , src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/module.py:338-346 ). How it works ¶ Total cost of ownership ¶ GET /tco/assets/{asset_id} and GET /tco/renewal take months between 1 and 120, default 12, and need fleet_asset.read ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/routes.py:48-66 ). For each asset the service adds: Cost part Rows counted Source Maintenance total_cost of completed work orders completed in the window src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:113-124 Fuel total_cost of verified fuel entries filled in the window src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:125-136 Penalties amount of penalties not objected , occurred in the window src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:152-164 Compliance amount of completed compliance items completed in the window src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:165-177 Kilometres used are the difference between the first and the latest life-to-date value of the odometer meter in the window. Cost per kilometre is the total divided by that difference, quantized to two decimals; with no kilometres it is empty. CO2 is the fuel quantity per fuel type times the emission factor of that type ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:179-226 , src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:293-325 , src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:327-360 ). The renewal board computes all aggregates in a fixed number of grouped queries, not one query set per asset ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:94-98 ). Tires, campaigns, and emission factors ¶ A tire ( FleetTire ) is identified by serial number and is in_storage , in_use , or scrapped ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/models.py:125 , src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/models.py:705-737 ). Mount needs a stored tire, an asset, and a free position. Unmount adds the odometer distance since mounting to accumulated_km . Scrap needs a stored tire ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:439-521 , src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/metadata.py:77-113 ). A campaign ( FleetCampaign ) lists assets that need the same work, for example a recall. A campaign item can open one work order or be marked done; a closed campaign takes no new assets ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/services.py:617-760 , src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/tco/metadata.py:287-427 ). An emission factor ( FleetEmissionFactor ) gives kilograms of CO2 per unit of one fuel type, unique among live rows. The table starts empty and the organisation fills it; the code comment states that the module computes a report and never a certification ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/models.py:773-789 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the intranet scopes personal records, trims content by access grants, builds audience segments, resolves the acting person, and retains analytics.
en.b: This page explains the cross-cutting rules of the intranet module. src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py scopes personal records and resolves the content viewer, src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/context.py resolves the acting person, src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/retention_handlers.py ages out analytics events, and src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/validation.py normalises form input. Access grants and audience segments live in src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/content/services.py . In short ¶ Access and audience are two separate axes. Access grants decide who may see content; segments decide who is targeted ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/models.py:8-11 ). Personal records (leave, requests, deliveries, the inbox) use three tiers: read_all sees everything, others see their own records and their team's, and a caller without a party sees nothing ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:1-21 ). The acting person is the party of the signed-in user's employee link ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/context.py:1-30 ). Read analytics of a post are shown only in aggregate, with unique counts below a minimum group size suppressed ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/content/services.py:1327-1355 ). How it works ¶ Acting person ¶ resolve_party_for_user reads employee_id from the signed-in user and asks GetPartyForEmployee for the party. A login without an employee link resolves to no party ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/context.py:20-30 ). For personal writes, effective_party_guarded uses the caller's own party; naming another party needs the privileged permission the route passes, for example intranet_leave_request.read_all ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:147-170 ). A named party must also be an active employee ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:124-144 ). Row scope for personal records ¶ resolve_scope returns a scope from the core row-scope helpers ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:189-220 ): Caller Sees Source holds <entity>.read_all every record src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:209-210 has a party own records and the team, read live through GetTeamPartyIds src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:173-186 , src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:211-218 has no party nothing src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:213-216 The resolved scope is also published to the database row-level security backstop ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:202-219 ). The mechanism is described on field and row access and multi-tenancy . Official deliveries add one rule: a confidential delivery is visible only to its recipient and to read_all holders ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/delivery/services.py:40-64 ). Access grants for content ¶ An access grant ( IntranetAclGrant ) attaches to a space or a post and names a realm: everyone , role , party , or segment , with can_view , can_edit , and can_publish flags ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/models.py:78-79 , src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/models.py:379-408 ). Listing joins the grant table as an SQL predicate. A post with no view grants on itself or its space is visible to every reader; otherwise the reader must match a grant by party, role, or segment ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/content/services.py:585-626 ). resolve_acl_viewer collects the reader's party, role ids, and segment ids; holders of intranet_content.read_all skip the trimming ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/access.py:78-121 ). Publish grants narrow the editorial permission: with no publish grant on the space or post, the permission alone decides; with grants, the actor must match one ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/content/services.py:628-660 ). Grants are set by an upsert per subject, realm, and id, and removed by setting deleted_at ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/content/services.py:544-583 ). The routes are GET , POST /acl/ and DELETE /acl/{grant_id} ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/content/routes.py:515-546 ). Audience segments ¶ flo

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the intranet inbox stores notifications, fans them out to channels including e-mail, and how official document delivery records a receipt.
en.b: This page explains three parts of the intranet module that carry messages to employees. The notifications sub-module in src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notifications/ is the in-app inbox. src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notify.py is the helper that raises a notification and hands the e-mail channel to the mail module. The delivery sub-module in src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/delivery/ hands official documents to employees and records the receipt. In short ¶ A notification is stored once and fanned out as one dispatch row per channel: in-app is delivered at once, e-mail goes through the system mailbox, push and SMS are recorded as skipped ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notifications/services.py:1-9 ). Read state lives on the server as seen_at and read_at ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notifications/services.py:193-231 ). Notifications carry an English fallback title plus an i18n key with parameters, so the client renders them in the reader's language ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notifications/services.py:53-58 ). An official delivery moves from pending to delivered to acknowledged or refused , and the acknowledgement records who, when, and from which client address ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/delivery/services.py:26-30 , src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/delivery/services.py:221-243 ). How it works ¶ Notification path ¶ flowchart TD A["intranet action: leave decision, request outcome, delivery, event change"] --> N["notify_party"] B["IntranetNotify event from the bus"] --> H["Module._handle_notify"] H --> S["NotificationService.create"] N --> S S --> R["IntranetNotification row"] S --> D1["dispatch in_app: delivered"] S --> D2["dispatch email: queued"] S --> D3["dispatch push or sms: skipped"] D2 --> F["fan_out_email"] F --> E1["ResolveEntityEmails"] E1 --> E2["SendTransactionalEmail"] E2 --> M["mark_email_dispatch: sent or skipped"] In prose: An intranet service calls notify_party on its own session, so the notification commits with the action that caused it. The helper opens the row-level backstop for exactly the recipient for this insert ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notify.py:1-6 , src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notify.py:68-113 ). Another module can publish IntranetNotify on the EventBus. The handler writes into the caller's tenant database and commits ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/module.py:305-345 , src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:2194-2208 ). NotificationService.create inserts the notification and one dispatch per requested channel ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notifications/services.py:37-99 ). For the e-mail channel, fan_out_email asks the parties module for the person's addresses through ResolveEntityEmails , takes the primary one, and asks the mail module to send through SendTransactionalEmail ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notify.py:20-65 ). The e-mail dispatch is marked sent when the system mailbox accepted the message, otherwise skipped with the reason, for example no address or no handler. sent means an attempt, not a delivery receipt ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/notifications/services.py:111-135 ). The dispatch states are queued , sent , delivered , bounced , failed , and skipped ; the channels are in_app , email , push , and sms ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/models.py:82-90 ). How the mail module sends is on mail module . en.d: Module page for inventory, the warehouses, storage locations, stock levels per product breakdown, goods movements, reservations, batches, and serial numbers.
en.b: The inventory module in src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/ keeps the stock of the company. It holds warehouses and storage locations, one stock level row per product, model, version, place, batch, owning project, and custodian, and the goods movements that change those rows. It also manages stock reservations, usage decisions on received goods, project stock loans, batches, and serial numbers. Purchasing, production, nesting, and sales post their stock changes to this module through the EventBus. en.d: Module page for nesting, which prepares sheet-metal nesting jobs, takes layouts from an external tool, costs them, and turns leftovers into remnants.
en.b: The nesting module in src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/ plans how parts are cut from metal sheets. A nesting job describes the sheet and the parts; the job is exported to an external nesting tool, and the tool's layout is imported back, checked, and stored. The module then draws the layout as SVG or DXF, costs the material, reserves and consumes sheet stock through the inventory module, records reusable remnants, and reports utilisation KPIs. The layout itself is not computed inside the module; see nesting engine . h: Why it is built this way
en.d: What the nesting/engine package does in code, geometry types, transforms, and SVG and DXF output, and where layouts really come from.
en.b: The package src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/ holds the geometry code of the nesting module: shared geometry types, polygon transforms, a DXF reader, a DXF writer, and an SVG writer. At this commit it contains no placement algorithm; layouts come from an external nesting tool through the import route. This page explains what the package does, how the module uses it, and what is stored but not used. The import itself is on integration and KPI . In short ¶ The package has five files: types.py , transforms.py , dxf_reader.py , dxf_writer.py , and svg_writer.py (folder listing of src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/ ). No function in the package places parts on a sheet. The job summary states that results only come from an external tool and shows the tool's name instead of the stored algorithm ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/nesting_jobs/services.py:827-834 ). The import check uses the transforms to rebuild each placed outline and to reject parts outside the sheet or overlapping ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/integration/services.py:48-106 ). The drawing routes rebuild placements from the stored layout and render them as SVG or DXF ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/nesting_jobs/routes.py:33-118 , src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/nesting_jobs/routes.py:307-396 ). How it works ¶ Geometry types ¶ types.py defines frozen and plain dataclasses that carry geometry between the module and the writers ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/types.py:12-142 ): Type Holds Source SheetGeom Sheet width and height, edge margin, kerf, part gap; usable size and area src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/types.py:12-36 PartGeom Part id, label, outline, quantity, allowed rotations, priority, mirror flag src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/types.py:39-61 Placement Placed instance: part id, instance number, x, y, rotation, mirror flag, outline, sheet index src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/types.py:64-84 RemnantRect A leftover rectangle on a sheet src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/types.py:87 SheetResult , NestResult Per-sheet and whole-run result containers src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/types.py:109-142 Transforms ¶ transforms.py wraps Shapely affine operations: rotate about the centroid, translate, mirror, move the outline so that its bounding box starts at the origin, area, bounding box, buffer, and conversion between polygons and coordinate lists ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/transforms.py:9-88 ). rotate_and_normalize rotates and then moves the outline back to the origin ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/transforms.py:84-88 ). make_rect builds a rectangle for a part that has no outline ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/engine/transforms.py:68-69 ). Rebuilding a stored layout ¶ The diagram shows how a drawing is produced from a stored job. flowchart LR J["NestingJob.layout_placements"] --> R["_reconstruct_placements"] P["NestingPart.geometry_polygon or part size"] --> R R --> T["mirror_polygon, rotate_and_normalize, translate_polygon"] T --> S["render_svg or render_multi_sheet_svg"] T --> D["write_multi_sheet_dxf"] In prose: _reconstruct_placements builds a SheetGeom from the job and, for each stored placement, takes the part's true outline when it has one, else a rectangle of the part's length and width ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/nesting_jobs/routes.py:45-82 ). It mirrors the outline if the placement is mirrored, rotates and normalises it, and moves it to the placement's x and y ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/nesting_jobs/routes.py:84-90 ). GET /nesting-jobs/{id}/svg returns the stored layout_svg when there is one; otherwise it renders all sheets, or one sheet when sheet_index is given ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/nesting_jobs/routes.py:307-361 ). GET /nesting-jobs/{id}/dxf writes a multi-sheet DXF ( src/cluster_erp/modules/nesting/nesting_jobs/routes.py:364-396 ). Writers ¶ The DXF writer puts the sheet

en.d: How one party card carries the customer, supplier, employee, and owned-organisation roles as facets, kept in step over the EventBus.
en.b: In Cluster ERP a customer, a supplier, an employee, and an owned organisation are not separate cards. Each is a role record in its own module that points at one party ( Party ) of the parties module, and the web app opens the party card for all of them. This page explains the identity redirect, the role sections on the party card, the role flags, guided creation, and role enabling. The party fields themselves are listed on the parties sub-module . In short ¶ A role record carries a party_id : the CRM customer, the procurement supplier, the employee, the assignment, and the owned organisation ( src/cluster_erp/modules/crm/customers/models.py:23 , src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/suppliers/models.py:42 , src/cluster_erp/modules/owned_organisations/employees/models.py:43 , src/cluster_erp/modules/owned_organisations/organisations/models.py:41 ). IdentityMeta on a role entity tells the web app to open the party card instead of a separate role card ( src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:304-313 ). FacetMeta entries on the party metadata show each role's data as sections of the party card ( src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:357-377 , src/cluster_erp/modules/parties/parties/metadata.py:550-763 ). The flags is_customer , is_supplier , and is_employee on the party follow the role records through the PartyRoleSet event and a start-up reconciliation ( src/cluster_erp/modules/parties/module.py:168-195 , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1002-1055 ). Creating a party with roles, and adding a role later, run in the server layer, which calls several module services in one request transaction ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/party_composite.py:1-10 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/party_roles.py:1-15 ). How it works ¶ The model ¶ The diagram shows which role records point at a party and which module owns each. flowchart LR Party["Party (parties)"] Customer["Customer (crm)"] -->|party_id| Party Supplier["Supplier (procurement)"] -->|party_id| Party Employee["Employee (owned_organisations)"] -->|party_id| Party Assignment["Assignment (owned_organisations)"] -->|party_id| Party Org["OwnedOrganisation (owned_organisations)"] -->|party_id| Party Assignment -->|organisation_id| Org Assignment -->|employee_id| Employee In prose: five role records point at the party with a party_id column. An assignment also points at the employee record and at the owned organisation where the person works ( src/cluster_erp/modules/owned_organisations/employees/models.py:69-102 ). None of these columns is a database foreign key across modules; the employee model states that the manager and party ids are bare UUIDs so that the module boundary stays clean ( src/cluster_erp/modules/owned_organisations/employees/models.py:59-61 ). Identity redirect ¶ IdentityMeta(field, module, entity) names the local column that holds the party id. When it is set, the web app opens the party card instead of the role card ( src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:304-313 ). Five entities declare it: customer ( src/cluster_erp/modules/crm/customers/metadata.py:30 ), supplier ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/suppliers/metadata.py:27 ), organisation , employee , and assignment ( src/cluster_erp/modules/owned_organisations/organisations/metadata.py:53 , src/cluster_erp/modules/owned_organisations/organisations/metadata.py:355 , src/cluster_erp/modules/owned_organisations/organisations/metadata.py:590 ). The intranet directory also declares it ( src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/directory/metadata.py:30 ). Role sections on the party card ¶ FacetMeta describes a role that a party can play. The web app loads the role records with a plain list query filtered by link_field equal to the party id, and renders the declared sections ( src/cluster_erp/core/metadata.py:357-377 ). The party metadata declares five facets: Facet Sections Gate Source crm / customer Commercial form; Customer Parts table; RFQ, quotation, and order history

en.d: Module page for procurement, with suppliers, purchase requests, purchasing RFQs, purchase orders, contracts, info records, critical materials, substitution, and MRP.
en.b: The procurement module in src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/ covers buying. It holds the supplier facet of a party, purchase requests, purchasing RFQs with vendor quotations and scoring, purchase orders with goods receipt, purchase contracts, and purchasing info records. It also runs material requirements planning (MRP) and keeps critical materials and substitution groups. This page is the overview; each sub-module has its own reference page, and MRP has an explanation page. en.b: This page describes two sub-modules of src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/ . critical_materials/ marks materials that must not run short, with lead-time bounds and an alert threshold. substitution_groups/ groups product breakdowns that can stand in for each other, with a preference order and a conversion factor. Both are read by the MRP run, described on material requirements planning . en.d: How the MRP run in procurement collects demand and supply, explodes BOMs, nets, sizes lots, raises exceptions, and turns proposals into requests or orders.
en.b: Material requirements planning (MRP) lives in src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/ . A planning run ( MrpRun ) compares demand with stock and open supply for each product, explodes bills of materials, and stores one result row ( MrpRunItem ) per product with a proposal and an exception message. This page explains how a run works and how its results are used. Field lists are on the procurement module page and in the source; the BOM explosion is described on the BOM module . In short ¶ A run has seven phases: init, demand, supply, low-level coding, netting, exceptions, and result assembly ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:1-19 ). Only one run can be running at a time; a database advisory lock guards the check ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/services.py:157-176 ). All data from other modules arrives through EventBus queries such as GetOpenSalesOrderDemand , GetBulkStockLevels , and GetBomExplosion ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:871 , src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:1325 , src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:1720 ). Stock and production events mark the run stale and flag products in a planning file for the next net-change run ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/module.py:863-1003 ). Run items become purchase requests or production orders by explicit actions ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/services.py:331 , src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/routes.py:359-375 ). How it works ¶ A run starts with POST /mrp/runs (synchronous) or POST /mrp/runs/background (returns at once with status running ) and the parameters of MrpRunCreate ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/routes.py:105-121 , src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/schemas.py:28-70 ). The diagram shows the phases. flowchart TD P0["_phase0_init: MrpRun status running"] --> PM["planning_mode: delete_and_recreate or normal"] PM --> P1["_phase1_demand: sales, production, PIR, safety stock"] P1 --> P2["_phase2_supply: stock, open POs, production supply, vendors"] P2 --> P3["_phase3_llc: low-level codes from active BOMs"] P3 --> P4["_phase4_net_requirements: netting, lot sizing, dates"] P4 --> P5["_phase5_exceptions: action messages"] P5 --> P7["_phase7_assemble: MrpRunItem rows, totals"] P7 --> E["MrpRunCompleted and CriticalMaterialAlert"] P7 --> PR["purchase requests when output_type is purchase_requisition"] In prose: Init. The engine creates the run with status running and snapshots the parameters ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:769-823 ). With delete_and_recreate , the items of the previous completed run are bulk-deleted and one summary change-history row is written; with normal , the BOM cache of the previous run is preloaded ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:555-562 , src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:697-767 ). Demand. Demand comes from open sales orders, open production order components, planned independent requirements (PIRs), safety stock deficits, and reorder points. A run with scope project first derives its product list from the project's demand ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:824-977 , src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:1059 ). Supply. Stock levels, open purchase orders, production supply, production versions, vendors, and substitutes are read in bulk ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:1311-1626 ). Low-level coding. Each manufactured product gets the active BOM version, and the BOM is exploded to assign low-level codes; the scope grows with BOM children ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:1627-1920 ). Netting. Requirements are netted per time bucket with dependent demand from BOMs, phantoms, substitution, lot sizing, scrap, lead-time offset, and vendor selection ( src/cluster_erp/modules/procurement/mrp/engine.py:1921-

en.d: How the production scheduling board reads work orders, resolves each work center's working calendar, detects conflicts and capacity, and moves or auto-schedules work orders.
en.b: The scheduling board lives in src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/ . It shows work orders as bars on work-center rows over time, computed against each work center's effective working calendar, and it moves, resizes, or auto-schedules them. The web app ( scheduling_board ) and the desktop ( scheduling_board.py ) draw the same data. Work order fields are on work orders ; calendar math is on working time . In short ¶ GET /api/v1/production/scheduling/board returns one read model: work centers with shifts and holidays, scheduled bars, the unscheduled pool, conflicts, capacity cells, and dependencies ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/routes.py:41-86 , src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:170-313 ). Each work center's calendar is resolved through the owner chain work center, then the party of its organisation or of the headquarters, then the company group calendar ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:72-94 ). A work order's end is always derived from its duration laid over working hours; a caller cannot set it ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:314-388 ). The time math comes from the shared engine core.working_time , re-exported by scheduling/calendar.py ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/calendar.py:1-30 ). How it works ¶ The diagram shows the data path of a board read. flowchart TD R["GET /scheduling/board with date range and filters"] --> WC["_load_work_centers"] WC --> SH["_load_shifts: calendar_candidates per work center"] SH --> EC["GetEffectiveWorkingCalendars in one query"] EC --> HO["_load_holidays: GetCalendarWindows per calendar"] HO --> CA["_load_capabilities"] CA --> WO["_load_work_orders: bars and unscheduled pool"] WO --> OV["_flag_overlaps with capacity_units"] OV --> CP["_compute_capacity: cells and utilization"] CP --> DP["_compute_dependencies: finish-to-start"] DP --> RS["BoardResponse"] In prose: The route takes date_from , date_to , and optional work center, production order, project, and scope filters; it needs work_order.read ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/routes.py:41-86 ). The service loads the work centers and resolves each one's effective calendar with one GetEffectiveWorkingCalendars query over the owner chains ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:891-946 ). Holidays and exceptions per date come from GetCalendarWindows ; the effective time zone comes from the calendar, the organisation, or GetCompanyDefaultTimezone ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:780-874 , src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:982-1016 ). Work orders in the window become bars; pending ones without a schedule form the unscheduled pool ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:1038-1204 ). Overlaps are flagged per work center, allowing up to capacity_units parallel bars; capacity cells and over-capacity days are computed; finish-to-start dependencies and predecessor violations are added ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:1205-1384 ). Writes: PUT /scheduling/work-orders/{work_order_id}/schedule moves, resizes, reassigns, or unschedules one pending work order. It checks the record version, snaps an explicit start forward to the next working instant, and derives the end ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/routes.py:87-109 , src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:314-388 ). POST /scheduling/work-orders/{work_order_id}/auto-schedule snaps a work order to the nearest valid free slot after its predecessors; no slot gives a 422 ( src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/routes.py:110-135 , src/cluster_erp/modules/production/scheduling/services.py:389-426 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the projects board and calendar read model builds one payload from projects, their children, production schedules, and the group calendar.
en.b: The project board is a read-only read model in src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py , served by src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board_routes.py . One call returns every project placed along the lifecycle columns, with its schedule, meetings, actions, fixtures, items, and the production reality from the production module. The web app draws it as a kanban ( project_board ) and as a month calendar ( project_calendar ), and as two home widgets. Project fields are on projects, items, and fixtures . In short ¶ One endpoint, GET /api/v1/projects/project-board/ , assembles the whole board; the board edits nothing ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:1-11 , src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board_routes.py:17-47 ). The columns are the project lifecycle PROJECT_STATUS_FLOW ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:100 ). Production orders and scheduled work orders come from GetProjectProductionSchedule ; open days come from GetOwnerWorkingDays for the group calendar ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:162-201 ). scope=mine narrows the board to projects where the caller's party is manager or action owner ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:57-82 ). How it works ¶ The diagram shows the data path of one board call. flowchart TD R["GET /project-board/ with date_from, date_to, scope"] --> M{"scope is mine"} M -->|yes| E["GetPartyForEmployee"] M -->|no| B["ProjectBoardService.board"] E --> B B --> P["Project rows, newest first"] P --> F["_only_member_projects when mine"] F --> C["_load_children: schedules, kickoffs, meetings, actions, fixtures, items"] C --> PR["_load_production: GetProjectProductionSchedule"] PR --> OD["_load_open_days: GetOwnerWorkingDays group calendar"] OD --> K["_card per project"] K --> J["payload: range, columns, projects, calendar, scope"] In prose: The route reads date_from , date_to , and scope . With scope=mine , it resolves the caller's employee to a party with GetPartyForEmployee ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board_routes.py:20-44 ). The service sets the date range; the default is 7 days back and 56 days ahead ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:43-45 , src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:70-72 ). It loads all live projects, newest first, and with mine keeps only the projects the party belongs to. A caller without a party gets an empty board ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:73-82 , src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:109-128 ). It loads the children of all projects in one pass per table: schedules by version descending, kick-offs, meetings by week, actions by due time, fixtures, and items by line ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:129-161 ). It asks the production module for the orders and work orders of the projects, and the calendars module for the open days of the group calendar ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:162-201 ). It builds one card per project with a summary: item count, open and overdue actions, open fixtures, meetings held, orders, work orders done, stale orders, and the schedule status. The active schedule is used, or the newest one when none is active ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:202-325 ). It returns the range, the columns, the cards, the open days, and the scope ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:88-107 ). The web widgets read this one payload. The board bundle states that tapping a card opens the project's own detail card and that nothing on the board edits data ( gated_apps/projects/app.js:7-17 ). Why it is built this way ¶ The module docstring gives two reasons: the client renders a single payload, and data of other modules is fetched over the EventBus because direct module imports are forbidden ( src/cluster_erp/modules/projects/board.py:1-11 ). The membership rule for mine follows the intranet audience builder's rule, as the docstring states

en.d: Module page for records, the record lifecycle with the deactivation reason catalogue, generic reactivation and passive lists, and the retention window and purge.
en.b: The records module in src/cluster_erp/modules/records/ owns the lifecycle of records under the rule that nothing is deleted outright. en.b: The sales_orders module in src/cluster_erp/modules/sales_orders/ turns a customer purchase order into a sales order and follows it to delivery. en.d: Landing page of the ai section, which documents the product's built-in intent assistant that maps typed requests to API actions.
en.b: This section documents the intent assistant of Cluster ERP, a built-in feature that turns a typed request such as "list the parties" into a call of the matching API endpoint. The engine lives in src/cluster_erp/ai/ : a tokenizer, a TF-IDF vectorizer, and an intent matcher trained at start from two example corpora, English and Turkish ( src/cluster_erp/ai/intent_engine.py:353-418 ). The web app reaches it through POST /api/v1/chat/message in src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py , and the desktop client runs the same engine locally. The assistant runs inside the product; it calls no external service. Pages ¶ How the intent assistant works : the request path, the matching score, the permission scope, and the corpora. Related pages ¶ Wiki home Assistant and chat screens Desktop chat widget Shared server routes Verified against commit 7793ff4 on 2026-11-09.

en.d: How the built-in intent assistant tokenises a request, scores it against the English and Turkish intent corpora, filters by permission, and answers through the chat route.
en.b: This page explains the intent assistant of Cluster ERP. The engine in src/cluster_erp/ai/ ( intent_engine.py , tokenizer.py , vectorizer.py , and the corpora intent_corpus_en.json and intent_corpus_tr.json ) matches a typed request to an API intent. The chat route src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py wraps the engine for the web app: it handles small talk, checks permissions, calls the matched endpoint, and returns replies. The screens are described on assistant and chat screens and desktop chat widget . In short ¶ The engine is a local text classifier: tokenisation with Turkish stemming, word and character features, TF-IDF vectors, and cosine similarity against example sentences ( src/cluster_erp/ai/tokenizer.py:400-438 , src/cluster_erp/ai/vectorizer.py:7-52 ). An intent names a module, an HTTP method, an API path, and a description ( src/cluster_erp/ai/intent_engine.py:14-24 ). The route offers only intents whose endpoint the caller holds the permission for, within the modules the client declares installed ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1158-1177 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1253-1265 ). Reads run the matched list endpoint in-process with the caller's own token; create intents return a task card; update and delete intents point to the record instead of acting ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1055-1066 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1436-1466 ). How it works ¶ Request path ¶ flowchart TD A["POST /api/v1/chat/message: text, action_context, allowed_modules"] --> P["require_permission dashboard.read"] P --> AC{"action_context set"} AC -->|yes| HA["_handle_action follow-up"] AC -->|no| ST{"small talk"} ST -->|yes| SR["fixed greeting or help reply"] ST -->|no| SP["_try_split_intents"] SP --> RE["IntentEngine.recognize top 5"] RE --> F["_intent_allowed: module scope and permission code"] F -->|none left| FB["_scope_fallback"] F --> C{"confidence below 0.60"} C -->|yes| SUG["did you mean, top 3"] C -->|no| K{"intent kind"} K -->|list or get| G["_api_get in-process with caller token"] K -->|create| T["task card from metadata"] K -->|update or delete| N["navigate to the record"] In prose: The route needs dashboard.read and loads the caller's permission codes ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1191-1200 ). The language is Turkish when the text has Turkish letters or common Turkish command words, otherwise English ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:999-1040 ). A follow-up from an action button goes to _handle_action . Greetings and help requests get a fixed reply ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1209-1218 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:537-647 ). A text with several requests is split and each part is processed in turn ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1223-1239 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:664-717 ). IntentEngine.recognize returns up to five candidates. The engine is created and loaded once per process ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:24-35 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1253 ). Candidates whose endpoint the caller may not reach are removed before anything is shown. With no candidate left, the reply is the same as for an unknown request ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1255-1265 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1179-1185 ). Below a confidence of 0.60 the route lists the top three as suggestions ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1270-1279 ). For a list or get intent the route builds filters, temporal order, and a search term from the text, calls the endpoint in-process through an ASGI transport with the caller's Authorization header, and formats the rows with the list columns from metadata ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1282-1433 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:1055-1066 ). en.d: Credentials, cookies, tenant selection, language, deactivation, and audit headers that Cluster ERP API clients send and receive, at mechanism level.
en.b: This page lists the credentials and HTTP headers that the Cluster ERP API reads and writes, at the level a client developer needs to call it. It covers tenant users, the operator console, and the token-based supplier portal and signup routes. The design of sessions and tokens is explained in Authentication and sessions ; this page does not repeat it and does not describe internal checks beyond their results.
