en.d: Methods, status codes, pagination, search and filters, ids, money, soft delete, bulk operations, action endpoints, and concurrency in the Cluster ERP API.
en.b: This page states the conventions that the Cluster ERP routes share: methods and status codes, list pagination, search and filters, identifiers, money values, deactivation instead of deletion, bulk operations, action endpoints, and optimistic concurrency. Counts on this page cover the 1,364 routes in src/cluster_erp/modules/ and src/cluster_erp/server/routes/ , from the same scan as the module pages. The seven routes declared in src/cluster_erp/server/app.py are on System endpoints . Methods ¶ Method Routes Use Example GET 510 list, read, and read models src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:66 POST 531 create, actions, bulk operations, and computations src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:108 PUT 158 update a record src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:132 PATCH 8 partial update in sales_orders and in tenant fields, and one MRP item action src/cluster_erp/modules/sales_orders/orders/routes.py ( update_order ) DELETE 157 deactivate a record or remove a dependent row src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:146 Collection routes end with a slash in 263 route paths, for example /api/v1/inventory/warehouses/ ( src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:66 ). The module pages show the exact path of every route. Status codes ¶ Status Routes that declare it Meaning in this API Example 201 201 a record was created src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:108 202 5 work was accepted and continues, for example a signup or a background MRP run src/cluster_erp/server/routes/signup.py:146 204 145 success without a body, mostly deactivation src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:146 not declared 1,013 the framework default for a successful response; the module pages show it as 200 (default) see the FastAPI reference Some handlers return their own Response object and set the status there, for example sign-out ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/login/routes.py:373-432 ). Error statuses are listed on Errors . Pagination ¶ List routes take limit and offset query parameters (111 routes take limit , 105 take offset ). Each route sets its own bounds in Query(...) ; for example the warehouse list uses a default of 50, a minimum of 1, and a maximum of 200 ( src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:66-73 ). A paginated list answers with an envelope. From src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:84-96 : return { "items" : await redact_extra_items ( session , [ WarehouseListRead . model_validate ( w ) for w in items ], "warehouse" , "warehouse" , await actor_allowed ( session ), ), "total" : total , "total_capped" : svc . last_count_capped , "limit" : limit , "offset" : offset , } Field Meaning Source items the page of rows src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:85-91 total the row count, counted up to the cap src/cluster_erp/core/pagination.py:33-69 total_capped true when the count stopped at the cap src/cluster_erp/core/pagination.py:65-68 limit , offset the values the request used src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:94-95 The cap is the setting list_count_cap ; 0 means exact counts ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:324 , src/cluster_erp/core/pagination.py:27-30 ). Not every list route uses this envelope: routes with response_model=list[...] return a bare array. The module pages show the response model of each route. Search and filters ¶ Parameter Routes Meaning Example search 93 free-text search over the entity's search columns src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:66-69 status 46 filter on a status field module pages active_only 35 only active rows module pages is_active 6 filter on the is_active flag src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:70 include_inactive 6 include deactivated rows module pages extra.<key> lists that read tenant fields filter on a tenant-defined field v

en.d: The JSON error body, the exception-to-code mapping, and every error code with its HTTP status, raise sites, and first message.
en.b: This page describes the error body that every failed API request returns and lists every error code found in code. It covers the 213 code constants in src/cluster_erp/core/errors.py , the codes that modules and server files define locally, and the codes that the exception handlers in src/cluster_erp/server/error_handler.py assign. The design of the error model is explained in Errors and exceptions . Error body ¶ Every handler builds the body with _build_body . From src/cluster_erp/server/error_handler.py:33-46 : def _build_body ( code : str , message : str , trace_id : str , details : dict [ str , Any ] | None = None , ) -> dict [ str , Any ]: body : dict [ str , Any ] = { "code" : code , "message" : message , "trace_id" : trace_id , } if details : body [ "details" ] = details return { "error" : body } Illustrative response built from _build_body and the RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND factory not_found ( src/cluster_erp/core/errors.py:357-367 ): { "error" : { "code" : "RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND" , "message" : "Warehouse (<warehouse_id>) not found" , "trace_id" : "<yymmdd>-<seq>" , "details" : { "resource" : "Warehouse" , "id" : "<warehouse_id>" } } } Field Meaning code Machine-readable code. Clients map it to a localised message ( src/cluster_erp/core/errors.py:6-16 ). message Developer-oriented English text ( src/cluster_erp/core/errors.py:10-11 ). trace_id Date prefix yymmdd and a daily sequence from the trace_sequence table; a time-based fallback when the table write fails ( src/cluster_erp/server/error_handler.py:49-70 ). details Present only when not empty ( src/cluster_erp/server/error_handler.py:45-46 ). debug_message , exception_type Added for unhandled and mapped exceptions only when debug is on ( src/cluster_erp/server/error_handler.py:306-308 , src/cluster_erp/server/error_handler.py:346-347 ). Note A request whose Content-Length exceeds max_request_body_bytes is refused with 413 and code REQUEST_TOO_LARGE before the body is read. That body carries code and message but no trace_id ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1396-1411 ). Exception handlers ¶ install_error_handlers registers one handler per exception class ( src/cluster_erp/server/error_handler.py:200-398 ). The table lists what each produces. en.d: Base paths, module prefixes, OpenAPI availability, content types, and the path of one request through the Cluster ERP HTTP API.
en.b: The Cluster ERP server is one FastAPI application that create_app builds in src/cluster_erp/server/app.py . This page explains how its HTTP paths are formed, where the interactive API documentation is available, which content types the routes use, and what happens to one request between the socket and the service. It does not list endpoints; the API reference links one page per route group. In short ¶ Every backend module mounts its routes under /api/v1/<module> , the value of ModuleBase.api_prefix ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:37-38 ). The fleet and intranet modules write the same prefix as a literal ( src/cluster_erp/modules/fleet/module.py:310 , src/cluster_erp/modules/intranet/module.py:172 ). The module registry calls each module's register_routes while it loads the module ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:49-51 ). Shared routes outside the modules live in src/cluster_erp/server/routes/ and are included by create_app ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1432-1450 ). The interactive documentation pages exist only when the debug setting is on ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1296-1303 ). Request and response bodies are JSON, except file uploads (multipart form data) and file downloads. Base paths ¶ The table groups the paths that the server answers. The module and shared route counts are on the API reference page. Path family Owner How the path is formed Source /api/v1/<module>/... 28 backend modules api_prefix plus the router prefix plus the route path src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:37-38 /api/v1/notes , /api/v1/attachments , /api/v1/email , /api/v1/chat shared server routes the router prefix argument src/cluster_erp/server/routes/notes.py:14 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/attachments.py:27 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/email.py:22 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/chat.py:23 /api/v1/parties/composite , /api/v1/parties/{party_id}/roles/... shared server routes a second router on the parties prefix src/cluster_erp/server/routes/party_composite.py:27 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/party_roles.py:31 /api/v1/{module}/_fields/... , /api/v1/_overlay tenant fields a module name inside the path src/cluster_erp/server/routes/tenant_fields.py:42-43 /api/v1/signup/... , /api/v1/vendor/... signup and operator console included only when multi_tenant is on src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1440-1450 /api/v1/modules , /api/v1/_meta , /api/v1/_switches application declared with @app.get src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1507-1572 /health , /ready , /.well-known/security.txt application declared with @app.get src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1459-1504 /app/... , /app/v/... web app static files app.mount when the webapp folder exists src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1633-1644 Module prefixes ¶ Most modules create a module_router with prefix=self.api_prefix , include their sub-module routers into it, and include it into the application with an entitlement dependency. The inventory module is an example ( src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/module.py:52-62 ). Some modules skip the module_router and pass the prefix to app.include_router directly, for example analytics , app_store , logs , mail , privacy , and records ( src/cluster_erp/modules/analytics/module.py:55 , src/cluster_erp/modules/records/module.py:50-52 ). A sub-module router adds its own prefix , for example /warehouses ( src/cluster_erp/modules/inventory/warehouses/routes.py:33 ). Several routers have no prefix and write the resource segment into every route path instead: the crm routers, the calendars router, the parties routers, the sales order routers, the currency router, and the customer subscription router ( src/cluster_erp/modules/crm/customers/routes.py:28 , src/cluster_erp/modules/calendars/routes.py:44 , src/cluster_erp/modules/parties/parties/routes.py:28 , src/cluster_erp/modules/sales_orders/orders/routes.py:33 , src/cluster_erp/server/routes/currencies.py:18 , src/cluster_erp/modules/subscriptions/customer_subscriptions/routes.py:30-34 ). en.d: How the fleet backup runner dumps, encrypts, verifies, and prunes every database of a node, how a dump is restored, and what the optional archive scripts add.
en.b: Cluster ERP has one backup implementation: the runner python -m cluster_erp.server.backup_tenants . Cron, the installer, the operator console, and tenant offboarding all call it. This page explains what it dumps, how a dump becomes a verified backup, how old dumps are pruned, and how a restore works. Backup locations of real nodes are deployment data and are omitted under the security disclosure policy; the page names the setting backup_dir instead. In short ¶ The runner dumps the default database, every live tenant database from the server of its region, and the control-plane database ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:387-405 ). Before each dump it checks that the dump role can read past the row guard; otherwise it stops with a named error ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:105-144 ). A dump counts only after pg_restore --list reads it back; a dump that does not read back is renamed with the suffix .corrupt ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:147-173 , src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:287-304 ). With backup_encryption_key set, the dump stream is encrypted on its way to disk as .dump.enc ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:259-278 ). A restore goes only into a database without tables ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:477-532 ). How it works ¶ Commands ¶ Command Effect Source python -m cluster_erp.server.backup_tenants Back up every target. src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:3 python -m cluster_erp.server.backup_tenants --only <db> Back up one database. src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:4 python -m cluster_erp.server.backup_tenants --restore <db> --file <dump> Restore one dump into one database. src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:5 python -m cluster_erp.server.backup_tenants --list Print every target as name, host, and port separated by tabs. src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:6 , src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:535-543 The exit code is 1 when any database failed, so cron reports the failure ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:570-573 ). The backup and restore path ¶ The diagram shows the path of one database. flowchart TD start["backup_all"] --> check["assert_dump_role_can_read_everything"] check --> dump["pg_dump -Fc"] dump --> enc{"backup_encryption_key set"} enc -- "yes" --> sealed["encrypt_stream to .dump.enc"] enc -- "no" --> plain["write .dump"] sealed --> verify["verify_dump with pg_restore --list"] plain --> verify verify -- "fails" --> corrupt["rename to .corrupt, report"] verify -- "passes" --> prune["_prune by count and age"] rstart["restore_one"] --> rcheck["role check, create database"] rcheck --> empty{"database has tables"} empty -- "yes" --> refuse["refuse"] empty -- "no" --> restore["pg_restore --no-owner"] In prose: backup_all walks the targets in order and counts failures; one failing database does not stop the others ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:408-439 ). _dump_one checks the dump role, then runs pg_dump -Fc against the region's server ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:241-258 ). With an encryption key the output of pg_dump is encrypted chunk by chunk into a .dump.enc file, and no plain copy is written ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:259-278 ). Without a key the dump is written as .dump ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:279-286 ). verify_dump lists the dump with pg_restore --list . An encrypted dump is decrypted straight into pg_restore , and every chunk is authenticated ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:147-173 , src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:187-238 ). A dump that fails verification is renamed with .corrupt , so it never takes a retained slot ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:287-304 ). After a

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: The jobs of the CI workflow, the lock and advisory gate, the gated production deploy job, and the tag and changelog conventions of a release.
en.b: Continuous integration of Cluster ERP is one GitHub Actions workflow, .github/workflows/ci.yml . It runs three gate jobs on every push and pull request and adds a deploy job for version tags. This page explains each job, the order between them, and the conventions for tags and CHANGELOG.md . How a tag then moves through staging is in environments and promotion . In short ¶ Triggers: a push to any branch, a push of a tag that matches v* , and every pull request ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:25-29 ). Three gate jobs run in parallel: lint , lock , and test ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:37-124 ). The deploy job runs only for refs/tags/v* and only after all three gates pass ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:126-129 ). The workflow token has read access to repository contents only ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:31-32 ). Every job installs Python packages from requirements.lock with --require-hashes ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:47 , .github/workflows/ci.yml:106 ). How it works ¶ The job graph: flowchart LR push["push or pull request"] --> lint["lint: ruff + mypy"] push --> lock["lock: lock integrity + advisories"] push --> test["test: migrations + pytest"] lint --> deploy["deploy: tag v* only"] lock --> deploy test --> deploy deploy --> node["install.sh --role production"] In prose: the three gates start together on every event; the deploy job waits for all three and runs only for a version tag; it then calls the installer on the production node. Lint job ¶ Installs the locked packages, the project, the dev extra, and PySide6==6.8.3 , then runs ruff check src tests and mypy src ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:38-52 ). The desktop toolkit is installed because mypy src also checks the Qt client ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:48-49 ). Lock job ¶ uv lock --check fails when uv.lock does not match pyproject.toml ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:59-62 ). The job exports requirements.lock again with the same command and fails on any difference ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:63-68 ). pip-audit checks every pin in requirements.lock in strict mode; a pin with a known advisory fails the job ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:72-74 ). The pins in [tool.uv] are the versions that the full battery and pytest last ran on; the comment describes how to move one ( pyproject.toml:155-166 ). Test job ¶ The job starts a postgres:16 service container and passes database settings and a CI-only secret through the job environment ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:79-99 ). The values are omitted under the security disclosure policy. It then: applies the whole Alembic history to the empty database ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:110-113 ); fails unless there is exactly one Alembic head ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:114-117 ); runs pytest ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:124 ). CLUSTER_SKIP_LIVE_TESTS=1 skips the tests that need a running server, so the waiver is visible ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:17-20 , .github/workflows/ci.yml:99 ). Deploy job ¶ The job uses the GitHub environment production , and the concurrency group production-deploy never cancels a running deploy ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:131-136 ). It requires four secrets and one variable, by name DEPLOY_HOST , DEPLOY_USER , DEPLOY_SSH_KEY , DEPLOY_HOST_KEY , and DEPLOY_DOMAIN , and stops when one is empty ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:139-150 ). The node's host key comes from a secret and is checked strictly ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:153-155 ). The job runs install.sh --tag <tag> --domain <domain> --role production on the node ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:155-156 ), so the promotion gate of the installer applies ( deploy/install.sh:101-107 ). Why it is built this way ¶ The migration step runs on Linux PostgreSQL because it is "the first place a Windows-authored migration meets Linux PostgreSQL" ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:110-112 ). "a drifted lock means somebody edited one without the other" ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:60-61 ). "a pin with a known advisory does not ship" ( .github/

h: Variables read by gunicorn and the scripts
en.d: Every variable of the node environment template deploy/env.example, by name with a placeholder value, mapped to its field in config/settings.py.
en.b: This page lists the variables of the node environment template deploy/env.example and maps each one to its field in src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py . It also lists the variables that the gunicorn configuration and the shell scripts read straight from the environment. Values are never shown: every value cell is the placeholder <value> . Types, defaults, and the readers of every field are in the settings reference . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: deploy/env.example (the template) and src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py ( Settings ). Count: 88 distinct CLUSTER_ERP_ names in the template, counted with grep -oE "CLUSTER_ERP_[A-Z0-9_]+" deploy/env.example | sort -u . Of these, 77 are value lines, 6 are commented value lines, and 5 appear only inside a comment (the S3 variables). Every one of the 88 maps to a Settings field. The Template column gives the line in deploy/env.example and whether the line is commented. The Meaning column is one sentence taken from the code comment of the field. The Source column is the field line in settings.py . A variable name is CLUSTER_ERP_ followed by the field name in upper case, read case-insensitively ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:64-70 ). File format ¶ systemd reads the file with EnvironmentFile= . A line that starts with # or ; is a comment; a # after a value becomes part of the value. A value with spaces, # , or double quotes is wrapped in single quotes ( deploy/env.example:6-10 ). The same file works as a .env file for a local run ( deploy/env.example:11 ). install.sh refuses to start the service while any value line still contains a <...> placeholder; comment lines are ignored by this check ( deploy/install.sh:176-179 ). systemd hands the file to the process only at start, so install.sh restarts instead of reloading when the file is newer than the running service ( deploy/install.sh:228-243 ). Variables of the template ¶ Mode, secrets, and database ¶ Template lines 13 to 38: the run mode, the signing and sealing keys, two optional switches, and the database connection. en.d: The application container image in deploy/docker/Dockerfile and the measurement stack in deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml, which are not a deployment artefact.
en.b: The repository holds a container image of the application tier and a Compose file that runs it next to PostgreSQL 16. Both exist to measure performance budgets on the real Linux process model; a node is installed with deploy/install.sh , not with containers ( deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:1-5 ). This page describes deploy/docker/Dockerfile and deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: deploy/docker/Dockerfile (one build target, runtime ) and deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml (two services, db and app ). Count: two services and one named volume, counted from the Compose file. Image ¶ Part Behaviour Source Base python:3.12-slim-bookworm , build target runtime . deploy/docker/Dockerfile:10 Environment Unbuffered output, no byte-code files, no pip cache, no pip version check. deploy/docker/Dockerfile:12-15 System packages PostgreSQL client tools for the backup runner, libpq5 , and curl . deploy/docker/Dockerfile:17-21 User A system user with a fixed numeric id owns the application folder; the container runs as that user. deploy/docker/Dockerfile:23-24 , deploy/docker/Dockerfile:41 Dependencies requirements.lock with --require-hashes , before the source for layer caching. deploy/docker/Dockerfile:26-28 Content pyproject.toml , README.md , src , migrations , alembic.ini , webapp , the gunicorn configuration, and scripts/backup . deploy/docker/Dockerfile:30-36 Install The project without dependency resolution, plus state and backup folders owned by the user. deploy/docker/Dockerfile:37-39 Health check curl against /ready every 15 seconds. deploy/docker/Dockerfile:43-44 Command gunicorn with deploy/gunicorn.conf.py and cluster_erp.server.asgi:app . deploy/docker/Dockerfile:46 The image contains no compiler and no Qt toolkit, and no database ( deploy/docker/Dockerfile:1-7 ). Measurement stack ¶ Service Behaviour Source db postgres:16 with a fixed max_connections and shared_buffers , a health check, a named data volume, and its port published on the loopback interface only. deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:16-31 app Built from the Dockerfile, started after db is healthy, with worker count, pool size, and keys from the environment, and its port published on the loopback interface only. deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:32-58 Compose refuses to start the services without MEASURE_DB_PASSWORD (for db ) and MEASURE_SECRET_KEY (for app ), through the :? form of the variables ( deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:20 , deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:44 ). MEASURE_WORKERS sets the worker count and defaults to four ( deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:43 ). The storage and backup keys fall back to fixed test values when MEASURE_STORAGE_KEY and MEASURE_BACKUP_KEY are unset ( deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:53-54 ); the values are omitted under the security disclosure policy. The header comments describe the run: build and start db , load a dump of the test database, start app , and run the performance budget suite against it ( deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:7-14 ). Constraints and validation ¶ CLUSTER_ERP_DEBUG is false and CLUSTER_ERP_TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS is false in the stack, so the settings validation of a production start applies ( deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:44 , deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:55 ). The container listens on all interfaces inside the container network ( CLUSTER_ERP_SERVER_HOST ) and is reachable from the host only through the loopback binding ( deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:41 , deploy/docker/compose.measure.yml:57-58 ). h: Why it is built this way
en.d: What the residency_check command verifies about a country node, every finding code it can report, and what it cannot verify.
en.b: A Cluster ERP deployment can declare the country it serves. The command python -m cluster_erp.server.residency_check then looks for anything in the configuration or in the control plane that contradicts that declaration. This page explains the rule behind it, every finding code, and the limits of the check. The settings themselves are listed in the configuration reference . In short ¶ The declaration is CLUSTER_ERP_NODE_COUNTRY , a two-letter ISO 3166-1 code; without it the command prints that no policy is declared and exits with code 0 ( src/cluster_erp/server/residency_check.py:347-355 , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:756-760 ). With a declaration the command prints a summary, then either CLEAN: nothing contradicts the declaration. with exit code 0 or the findings with exit code 1 ( src/cluster_erp/server/residency_check.py:358-373 ). The checks are pure functions over settings and tenant rows; only collect reads the control plane ( src/cluster_erp/server/residency_check.py:28-29 , src/cluster_erp/server/residency_check.py:325-344 ). install.sh runs the check after every install and refuses to report the release as live when it fails ( deploy/install.sh:258-259 ). How it works ¶ main builds Settings , calls collect , and prints the result ( src/cluster_erp/server/residency_check.py:347-373 ). collect runs config_findings and, on a multi-tenant node, adds tenant_findings over the (key, region) pairs of every tenant whose registration is not deleted ( src/cluster_erp/server/residency_check.py:325-344 ). Finding codes ¶ Nineteen codes, counted as the Finding(...) constructors in residency_check.py . h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How Cluster ERP changes its database schema through one Alembic history, who runs it, the boot migration lock, and the rule that shipped migrations are frozen.
en.b: Every business table of Cluster ERP comes from one Alembic history in migrations/ . The same history builds a new tenant database, upgrades an existing one, and is checked in continuous integration. This page explains who runs it, how parallel workers are kept apart, and which parts of the schema are not in that history. The operator commands that run it for many tenants are in tenant lifecycle . In short ¶ migrations/versions/ holds 218 revision files, counted as the *.py files of that folder ( ls migrations/versions/*.py ). alembic.ini carries no database address; migrations/env.py takes it from Settings or from an address that the caller passes in ( migrations/env.py:42-73 ). All runs go through upgrade_database_to_head , which holds a PostgreSQL advisory lock for the duration of the upgrade ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:665-720 ). A multi-tenant worker migrates its default database at start-up; a single-tenant node is migrated by install.sh before the restart ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:99-113 , deploy/install.sh:221-226 ). Continuous integration applies the whole history to an empty PostgreSQL 16 database and requires exactly one head ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:110-117 ). How it works ¶ Where the address comes from ¶ migrations/env.py decides the target database in this order ( migrations/env.py:56-73 ): An address set by a program in cfg.attributes["explicit_url"] . upgrade_database_to_head always sets it, so tenant provisioning and the fleet runner reach the intended database ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:687-692 ). Otherwise Settings().database_url_sync , built from the CLUSTER_ERP_DB_* variables. If Settings cannot be built, the run stops with an error instead of guessing a database. The alembic.ini logging section applies only when no logging is configured yet, so an in-process run does not silence the application log ( migrations/env.py:32-40 ). env.py imports each module's top-level models.py to fill target_metadata ( migrations/env.py:76-86 ). Who runs the history ¶ The diagram shows every caller of the history. flowchart LR ci["CI: alembic upgrade head"] --> alembic["Alembic command.upgrade"] inst["install.sh single-tenant"] --> alembic boot["worker lifespan multi-tenant"] --> uh["upgrade_database_to_head"] prov["provision_tenant"] --> uh upg["upgrade_tenants"] --> uh uh --> lock["migration_lock"] lock --> alembic In prose: Continuous integration runs python -m alembic upgrade head on an empty database ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:113 ). On a single-tenant node, install.sh takes a backup and runs alembic upgrade head ( deploy/install.sh:221-226 ). In multi-tenant mode each worker creates the default database if needed and calls upgrade_database_to_head at start-up ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:110-113 ). provision_tenant replays the history on a new tenant database ( src/cluster_erp/server/provision_tenant.py:132-137 ). upgrade_tenants upgrades every tenant whose revision differs from the head ( src/cluster_erp/server/upgrade_tenants.py:83-100 ). The boot migration lock ¶ upgrade_database_to_head wraps command.upgrade(cfg, "head") in migration_lock . The lock is pg_advisory_lock with the fixed key MIGRATION_LOCK_KEY , taken on the target database and released at the end ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:693-720 ). A second worker waits until the first has finished and then finds the head already applied ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:693-699 ). The test tests/test_boot_migration_lock.py checks that a second holder waits for the first. Why it is built this way ¶ One history keeps a provisioned tenant identical to a migrated deployment ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:666-672 ). The database address is not stored in alembic.ini , because "a tracked credential is a liability" ( migrations/env.py:60-63 ). The lock exists because two workers once replayed a new revision at the same moment and one failed

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How a Cluster ERP release moves from a workstation through continuous integration and a staging node to a production node, and what enforces each gate.
en.b: Cluster ERP has four environments: the development workstation, continuous integration, a staging node, and a production node. A release reaches production only after the same tag ran on staging. This page explains the chain and the code that enforces it in deploy/install.sh , .github/workflows/ci.yml , and src/cluster_erp/server/staging_fixtures.py . Step-by-step installation is in install a Linux node ; the CI jobs are in CI pipeline and release . In short ¶ A node is installed with deploy/install.sh --tag <tag> --domain <domain> --role staging|production ; the role is mandatory ( deploy/install.sh:77-83 ). A production install refuses a tag that has no annotated promotion tag staging-ok/<tag> on the same commit ( deploy/install.sh:101-107 ). A node records its role at the first install and refuses any other role later ( deploy/install.sh:122-128 ). Continuous integration runs lint, lock, and test jobs on every push, and a deploy job on version tags that waits for approval in the production environment ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:25-28 , .github/workflows/ci.yml:126-136 ). The browser battery is not part of continuous integration; it runs against the staging node before the promotion tag is set ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:21-22 ). How it works ¶ The chain has five gates. The diagram shows them in order. flowchart LR dev["Workstation"] --> ci["CI jobs lint, lock, test"] ci --> tag["Version tag v*"] tag --> stg["install.sh --role staging"] stg --> battery["_run_battery.mjs on staging"] battery --> ok["Tag staging-ok/v*"] ok --> prod["install.sh --role production"] tag --> deploy["CI deploy job, approval"] deploy --> prod The same content in prose: A developer works on a workstation. On Windows the server runs as one process whatever server_workers says ( src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:27-35 ). Every push and pull request runs the lint , lock , and test jobs ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:37-124 ). A version tag v* is pushed. The workflow runs the same gates and then the deploy job ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:126-129 ). The operator installs the tag on the staging node with --role staging . A staging install needs no promotion record ( deploy/install.sh:101 , tests/test_install_role_gate.py:145 ). The browser battery runs against the staging node. The runner web-client/_run_battery.mjs runs every _e2e_*.mjs suite in sequence and exits non-zero when one suite fails or prints no result ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:1-20 ). Suites that need a second PostgreSQL server or local processes are left out with --exclude ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:35-38 ). When the battery passes, the operator records the promotion as a second annotated tag staging-ok/<tag> on the same commit and pushes it ( deploy/install.sh:15-21 ). The production install (by hand or by the CI deploy job) resolves both tags on the remote. It stops when the record is missing or points at another commit ( deploy/install.sh:85-107 ). Node role ¶ At the first install the script writes the role into the file named by ROLE_FILE ( deploy/install.sh:58 , deploy/install.sh:122-128 ). A later install with a different role stops with the message that a node never changes role. The staging test accounts are created only on a node whose recorded role is staging ( src/cluster_erp/server/staging_fixtures.py:92-105 ). See demo and staging data . Approval of the deploy job ¶ The deploy job is bound to the GitHub environment production and to a concurrency group that never cancels a running deploy ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:131-136 ). The workflow header states that the environment is configured with required reviewers, so a person approves each deploy in the Actions screen ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:7-12 ). The reviewer setting itself lives in the repository settings: Not determined from code. The job runs install.sh --role production on the node, so the promotion

en.d: Prepare an Ubuntu node with bootstrap-node.sh and install or upgrade a tagged Cluster ERP release on it with install.sh.
en.b: This guide installs a tagged Cluster ERP release on one Linux node, for staging or for production, and upgrades it later with the same command. It follows deploy/bootstrap-node.sh for the operating system and deploy/install.sh for the application. The reasons behind the staging and production split are in environments and promotion . Note Execution status: not executed by the writer; steps derived from deploy/bootstrap-node.sh , deploy/pg-tune.sh , deploy/postgres-roles.sql , and deploy/install.sh . Prerequisites ¶ A fresh Ubuntu 24.04 node with root access; the bootstrap script refuses other systems ( deploy/bootstrap-node.sh:52-55 ). The administrator's OpenSSH public key file ( deploy/bootstrap-node.sh:46-51 ). A PostgreSQL 16 server on the node. install.sh installs only the PostgreSQL client ( deploy/install.sh:114 ), and pg-tune.sh stops when the PostgreSQL 16 configuration directory is missing ( deploy/pg-tune.sh:23-31 ). A release tag that exists on the repository remote, and read access from the node to that remote ( deploy/install.sh:47-54 , deploy/install.sh:85-90 ). For production: the promotion record staging-ok/<tag> on the same commit ( deploy/install.sh:101-107 ). Steps ¶ Prepare the operating system once, as root. Source: deploy/bootstrap-node.sh:8-23 , deploy/bootstrap-node.sh:36-44 . bash bash bootstrap-node.sh --admin <name> --pubkey <public-key-file> --admin-cidr <cidr> --admin-cidr is optional; without it the SSH port stays open to every address and the script prints a note ( deploy/bootstrap-node.sh:139-145 ). The script turns on unattended security updates, sets the clock to UTC with NTP, creates the administrator with sudo and the key, records every privileged session, switches SSH to keys only, and opens only SSH, HTTP, and HTTPS in the firewall ( deploy/bootstrap-node.sh:57-149 ). Before you close the root session, open a new session with the key. Root login and passwords are off after step 1 ( deploy/bootstrap-node.sh:151-154 ). Tune PostgreSQL for the node's memory and processor count, from a copy of the repository. The script writes one configuration file and restarts PostgreSQL. Source: deploy/pg-tune.sh:20 , deploy/pg-tune.sh:48-69 . bash sudo deploy/pg-tune.sh Replace both password placeholders in deploy/postgres-roles.sql , then create the application role and the backup role. Source: deploy/postgres-roles.sql:1-11 . See PostgreSQL roles and tuning . bash psql -U postgres -f deploy/postgres-roles.sql Run the installer with the tag, the public host name, and the role. Source: deploy/install.sh:11-13 . bash sudo deploy/install.sh --tag <tag> --domain erp.example.com --role staging On a node without an environment file the script copies deploy/env.example into place with mode 0640 and stops, because the file still holds <...> placeholders ( deploy/install.sh:171-179 ). Fill in every placeholder value of the environment file. The variables are listed in the configuration reference . If the node has no TLS certificate yet, obtain one with the command that the script prints. Source: deploy/install.sh:204-209 . bash certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/html -d erp.example.com -m <mailbox> --agree-tos -n Run the same install.sh command again. It now runs all eight steps: system packages, service user and directories, code at the tag, virtual environment from requirements.lock with hashes, environment file check, systemd unit with nginx site and cron table, database migration with a backup first, and start or reload with a readiness check ( deploy/install.sh:26-34 , deploy/install.sh:110-261 ). If the node is a production node, first record the passed staging battery on the release commit, then run the installer with --role production . Source: deploy/install.sh:20-21 . bash git tag -a staging-ok/<tag> <tag> -m "<battery log, date>" git push origin staging-ok/<tag> sudo deploy/install.sh --tag <tag> --domain erp.example.com --role

h: Step 2: Create the database roles and the database
en.d: Run Cluster ERP on a workstation for the first time, with a PostgreSQL database, the server, the web app, and optionally the desktop client.
en.b: This tutorial takes a developer from a fresh checkout to a running single-tenant server with the web app in the browser. It uses the commands that the repository itself runs in continuous integration and in the node scripts. It does not cover a Linux node (see install a Linux node ) or the graphical Windows installer (see Windows installer ). Note Execution status: not executed by the writer; steps derived from .github/workflows/ci.yml , deploy/postgres-roles.sql , deploy/env.example , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py , src/cluster_erp/server/main.py , and src/cluster_erp/server/app.py . What you will build ¶ At the end, one server process answers on the address set by CLUSTER_ERP_SERVER_HOST and CLUSTER_ERP_SERVER_PORT , its database is migrated to the newest revision, and the web app opens under /app/ . Optionally the desktop client connects to the same server. Before you start ¶ Python 3.12 or newer ( pyproject.toml:9 ). A PostgreSQL server. Continuous integration tests against PostgreSQL 16 ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:79-81 ). A shell in the repository root: Alembic and the server read alembic.ini and migrations/ from the working directory ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:681-684 ). Step 1: Install the Python packages ¶ Install the tested pins with hash checking, then the project without dependency resolution, then the development tools and the desktop toolkit at the pinned version. python -m pip install --quiet --require-hashes -r requirements.lock python -m pip install --quiet --no-deps -e . && python -m pip install --quiet -e ".[dev]" "PySide6==6.8.3" Source: .github/workflows/ci.yml:47-50 . The desktop extra holds the Qt toolkit; the dev extra holds pinned mypy and ruff , plus pytest ( pyproject.toml:64-84 ). You need the toolkit only for the desktop client. Step 2: Create the database roles and the database ¶ Edit the two password placeholders in deploy/postgres-roles.sql , then run it as the PostgreSQL superuser. psql -U postgres -f deploy/postgres-roles.sql Source: deploy/postgres-roles.sql:1-11 . The script creates the application role with CREATEDB and without BYPASSRLS , and a separate backup role ( deploy/postgres-roles.sql:13-42 ). Then create an empty database owned by the application role, named as you will set CLUSTER_ERP_DB_NAME . The repository has no command line for this step; the Windows setup wizard does it with createdb ( installer/setup_wizard.pyw:598-610 ). Step 3: Write the settings file ¶ Settings reads environment variables with the prefix CLUSTER_ERP_ and a .env file in the working directory ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:64-70 ). Create .env in the repository root with at least these lines: CLUSTER_ERP_DB_HOST = <value> CLUSTER_ERP_DB_NAME = <value> CLUSTER_ERP_DB_USER = <value> CLUSTER_ERP_DB_PASSWORD = <value> CLUSTER_ERP_SECRET_KEY = <value> Illustrative file built from the fields at src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:72-76 and src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:186 . Generate the secret with the command from the template: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))" Source: deploy/env.example:16-17 . Outside debug mode a default, short, or weak secret stops the start-up ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:771-808 ). Every other variable is described in the settings reference . Step 4: Migrate the database ¶ python -m alembic upgrade head Source: .github/workflows/ci.yml:113 . A single-tenant server does not migrate its database at start-up; only a multi-tenant server does ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:99-113 , deploy/install.sh:222-225 ). See database migrations . Step 5: Start the server ¶ python -m cluster_erp.server.main Source: src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:12-62 . With CLUSTER_ERP_DEBUG=true the server reloads when files under src/cluster_erp/server , core , or modules change ( src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:15-24 ). On Windows it always runs one process ( src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:27-35 ).

en.d: The two database roles of deploy/postgres-roles.sql, the backup runner's role check, and the memory and planner settings that deploy/pg-tune.sh writes.
en.b: A Cluster ERP deployment needs two PostgreSQL roles on every database server: the application role and the backup role. This page describes them as deploy/postgres-roles.sql creates them, the check that the backup runner makes before each dump, and the settings that deploy/pg-tune.sh writes for a node. Passwords are never part of this page; the script carries placeholders that the operator replaces. Scope and source ¶ Defined in: deploy/postgres-roles.sql , deploy/pg-tune.sh , and src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py ( assert_dump_role_can_read_everything ). Count: two roles, counted from the two CREATE ROLE statements; fourteen settings, counted from the lines of the generated file in pg-tune.sh . Roles ¶ Role Attributes Used by Source application role LOGIN , CREATEDB , NOSUPERUSER , NOBYPASSRLS The server, which creates its control-plane and tenant databases itself. deploy/postgres-roles.sql:13-27 backup role LOGIN , BYPASSRLS , NOSUPERUSER , NOCREATEDB , member of pg_read_all_data Only the backup runner. deploy/postgres-roles.sql:29-42 Rules stated in the script: Run it on every database server, including every data-residency region ( deploy/postgres-roles.sql:2-3 ). Replace both passwords before running. On a server that logs DDL statements, set the passwords afterwards with \password instead ( deploy/postgres-roles.sql:5-8 ). Re-running is safe: an existing role keeps its password and only the attributes are applied again ( deploy/postgres-roles.sql:10-11 ). The application role must never get BYPASSRLS , because that would switch off the row guard on the private tables ( deploy/postgres-roles.sql:13-15 ). The settings CLUSTER_ERP_BACKUP_DB_USER and CLUSTER_ERP_BACKUP_DB_PASSWORD (or CLUSTER_ERP_BACKUP_DB_PASSWORD_FILE ) point the runner at the backup role ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:67-80 ). See configuration reference . Backup role check ¶ Before each dump, assert_dump_role_can_read_everything asks PostgreSQL whether the dump role is a superuser or has BYPASSRLS , and whether it is a superuser or a member of pg_read_all_data . When either answer is no, the runner stops with an error that names the role and the missing attribute ( src/cluster_erp/server/backup_tenants.py:105-144 ). The final SELECT of postgres-roles.sql shows the same attributes for both roles ( deploy/postgres-roles.sql:44-52 ). Tuning settings ¶ pg-tune.sh reads the node's memory and processor count and writes one file into the conf.d folder of PostgreSQL 16, then restarts PostgreSQL ( deploy/pg-tune.sh:23-25 , deploy/pg-tune.sh:33-69 ). It refuses a node with less than 1 GB of memory ( deploy/pg-tune.sh:35 ). After the restart it prints seven of the applied settings an

h: What install.sh does with the template
en.d: The nginx site template deploy/nginx.conf.example at mechanism level, with TLS, static web app files, the asset stamp, headers, and the signup rate limit.
en.b: A Linux node puts nginx in front of the application. nginx terminates TLS, serves the web app files from the checkout, and forwards everything else to the gunicorn master. This page describes the template deploy/nginx.conf.example and the lines of deploy/install.sh that install it. The application-side cache rules are in cache and asset stamp . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: deploy/nginx.conf.example (two server blocks and a commented http block snippet) and deploy/install.sh:189-209 . Count: two server blocks and seven location blocks, counted as the location lines of the template. The host name in the template is the placeholder erp.example.com ; install.sh replaces it with the --domain value ( deploy/install.sh:195 ). Plain HTTP server ¶ Location Behaviour Source /.well-known/acme-challenge/ Served from the certificate tool's web root, so certificate renewals keep working. deploy/nginx.conf.example:13-16 / Permanent redirect to the same URL over HTTPS. deploy/nginx.conf.example:17-19 HTTPS server ¶ Part Behaviour Source TLS TLS 1.2 and 1.3, AEAD ciphers only, client cipher choice, session tickets off, OCSP stapling with verification. deploy/nginx.conf.example:33-47 Version banner server_tokens off . deploy/nginx.conf.example:49-50 Body size client_max_body_size 64m for uploads and document versions. deploy/nginx.conf.example:58-59 Forwarded headers Host , X-Real-IP , X-Forwarded-For , and X-Forwarded-Proto go to the application. deploy/nginx.conf.example:61-67 location = / Temporary redirect to /app/ . deploy/nginx.conf.example:72-76 Asset stamp Includes the file that sets $cluster_asset_stamp to the release tag. deploy/nginx.conf.example:78-84 Compression gzip for CSS, JavaScript, JSON, SVG, and fonts above 1024 bytes. deploy/nginx.conf.example:86-94 location /app/ Serves webapp/ from the checkout, falls back to index.html , sends Cache-Control: no-cache , and replaces __ASSET_STAMP__ in HTML with the stamp. deploy/nginx.conf.example:96-105 Headers on /app/ HSTS, a content security policy, nosniff , and no-referrer , listed inside the location because a location-level add_header replaces the server-level ones. deploy/nginx.conf.example:52-56 , deploy/nginx.conf.example:106-115 location ~ ^/app/v/... Serves the same files under the stamp, cached as immutable for one year, with the same headers. deploy/nginx.conf.example:117-127 location / Proxies to the application over HTTP/1.1 with a 120-second read timeout. deploy/nginx.conf.example:129-134 location /api/v1/signup Applies the signup rate-limit zone with a burst of five, then proxies. No trailing slash, so the bare path is covered too. deploy/nginx.conf.example:136-148 The http block ¶ The rate-limit zone signup belongs in the http block ( deploy/nginx.conf.example:151-152 ). install.sh writes it to an nginx conf.d file when no zone of that name exists ( deploy/install.sh:201-203 ). A commented access-log format logs the path without the query string ( deploy/nginx.conf.example:154-163 ). What install.sh does with the template ¶ Step Behaviour Source Group access Adds the nginx worker account to the service user's group and sets the checkout to mode 0750 . deploy/install.sh:189-193 Site file Writes the template with the domain substituted and links it into the enabled sites. deploy/install.sh:195-196 Asset stamp Writes set $cluster_asset_stamp "<tag>"; to the stamp file on every install. deploy/install.sh:197-200 Reload Tests and reloads nginx only when a certificate for the domain exists; otherwise prints the certificate command. deploy/install.sh:204-209 Constraints and validation ¶ The application rejects a body larger than max_request_body_bytes with HTTP 413 ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:342-347 ). That limit and client_max_body_size are two separate settings. The application interprets forwarded headers only when trust_proxy_headers is on and the peer is in trusted_proxy_ips ( src/cluster_erp/server/main.py:45-51 , deploy/gunicorn.conf.py:47-49 ). Witho

en.b: Cluster ERP runs periodic work in two places: the cron table deploy/cluster-erp.cron of the service user, and background loops that every server worker starts in src/cluster_erp/server/app.py . This page lists both, the lock that keeps a loop to one worker, and the retention passes in app.py and src/cluster_erp/server/control_retention.py . The admin-configured record retention window is explained on the records module page. Scope and source ¶ Defined in: deploy/cluster-erp.cron , src/cluster_erp/server/app.py ( lifespan , _leader , and the _*_loop functions), src/cluster_erp/server/control_retention.py ( sweep_control_plane ), src/cluster_erp/server/membership.py . en.d: The security.txt document built from settings, the liveness and readiness probes, their answer contract, and the code that relies on them.
en.b: A Cluster ERP server answers three unauthenticated operational routes: /.well-known/security.txt , /health , and /ready . This page describes what each returns, the settings behind them, and the tests and scripts that depend on them. The routes are defined in src/cluster_erp/server/app.py ; the document builder is src/cluster_erp/server/security_txt.py . The full list of system routes is in system endpoints . Scope and source ¶ Defined in: src/cluster_erp/server/app.py ( security_txt , health , ready ) and src/cluster_erp/server/security_txt.py ( security_txt_body ). Count: three routes, counted from the @app.get decorators at src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1459-1476 . Security.txt ¶ GET /.well-known/security.txt answers HTTP 404 when no contact is configured, and otherwise a text/plain document ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1459-1466 ). The route is not in the OpenAPI schema ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1459 ). Field Content Source Contact security_contact ; a value with @ and no scheme becomes a mailto: address. src/cluster_erp/server/security_txt.py:21-25 Expires Now plus security_expires_days , clamped to 1 to 365 days, in UTC. src/cluster_erp/server/security_txt.py:26-30 Preferred-Languages tr, en . src/cluster_erp/server/security_txt.py:31 Policy security_policy_url , only when set. src/cluster_erp/server/security_txt.py:33-34 Canonical public_base_url plus the route path, only when set. src/cluster_erp/server/security_txt.py:35-37 Setting Variable Value Source security_contact CLUSTER_ERP_SECURITY_CONTACT <value> src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:296 security_policy_url CLUSTER_ERP_SECURITY_POLICY_URL <value> src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:297 security_expires_days CLUSTER_ERP_SECURITY_EXPIRES_DAYS <value> src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:298 public_base_url CLUSTER_ERP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL <value> src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:292 The module states that an empty or fictional security.txt is worse than none, which is why the route answers 404 without a contact ( src/cluster_erp/server/security_txt.py:4-7 ). Liveness ¶ GET /health answers {"status": "healthy", "version": <app version>} and touches no backing store, so a database outage never restarts the process through a supervisor ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1469-1474 ). Readiness ¶ GET /ready asks each backing store SELECT 1 under the deadline readiness_timeout_seconds ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1485-1493 , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:649 ). Check Present when Source database always src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1495 control_plane multi-tenant mode src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1496-1498 Outcome Status code Body Source every check passes 200 {"status": "ready", "checks": {...}} src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1499-1503 any check fails 503 {"status": "not_ready", "checks": {...}} src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1499-1503 A failing check is reported as fail and the error goes only to the server log, so the answer never contains a host name or connection string ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1477-1493 ). en.d: Provision a tenant database, upgrade every tenant to a new release, suspend and reactivate a membership, and offboard a tenant on a multi-tenant node.
en.b: On a multi-tenant node every customer company is a tenant with its own database, registered in the control plane. This guide covers the operator commands that create a tenant, upgrade all tenants, change a membership, and end a tenant: server/provision_tenant.py , server/upgrade_tenants.py , server/membership.py , and server/offboard_tenant.py . The tenancy model itself is explained in multi-tenancy ; self-service signup is in signup . Note Execution status: not executed by the writer; steps derived from src/cluster_erp/server/provision_tenant.py , src/cluster_erp/server/upgrade_tenants.py , src/cluster_erp/server/membership.py , src/cluster_erp/server/offboard_tenant.py , and deploy/install.sh . Prerequisites ¶ A node with CLUSTER_ERP_MULTI_TENANT=true and a complete environment file ( src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py:82 ). See configuration reference . A shell in the checkout as the service user, with the environment file loaded, as install.sh runs these commands ( deploy/install.sh:63-66 , deploy/install.sh:215-220 ). For --region : a region code listed in CLUSTER_ERP_REGIONS ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:456-457 ). The states a tenant passes through are listed in TENANT_STATUSES : provisioning , active , suspended , and closed ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:48-50 ). The diagram shows the commands that move a tenant between them. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> provisioning: provision_tenant or signup provisioning --> active: provision completes active --> suspended: membership sweep or suspend suspended --> active: membership extend or activate active --> closed: offboard_tenant suspended --> closed: offboard_tenant closed --> [*]: offboard_tenant --drop In prose: a tenant is registered as provisioning , becomes active when provisioning completes, moves to suspended when its paid period ends or an operator suspends it, returns to active on extension or activation, becomes closed on offboarding, and loses its database and files with the --drop step. Steps ¶ Provision a tenant. Source: src/cluster_erp/server/provision_tenant.py:3-5 , src/cluster_erp/server/provision_tenant.py:163-172 . bash python -m cluster_erp.server.provision_tenant --key <key> --name "<company name>" --domains <domain>,<domain> --region <region> The key must match TENANT_KEY_RE ( src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:46 , src/cluster_erp/core/tenancy.py:460-461 ). The command registers the tenant as provisioning , creates its database on the region's server, replays the Alembic history, runs the real application start-up once against the new database (tables, sequences, permissions, first administrator), and marks the tenant active ( src/cluster_erp/server/provision_tenant.py:85-157 ). Each step is idempotent, so a failed run resumes when you run it again ( src/cluster_erp/server/provision_tenant.py:7-15 ). Self-service signup calls the same function after the domain is verified ( src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:472-478 , src/cluster_erp/server/signup.py:546 ). List what a release would change, before every upgrade. Source: src/cluster_erp/server/upgrade_tenants.py:4 , src/cluster_erp/server/upgrade_tenants.py:15-16 . bash python -m cluster_erp.server.upgrade_tenants --dry-run Take a backup of every database, then upgrade all tenants. install.sh runs the dry run, the backup, and the upgrade in this order on a multi-tenant node ( deploy/install.sh:217-220 ). See backups and restore . bash python -m cluster_erp.server.backup_tenants python -m cluster_erp.server.upgrade_tenants The runner visits the default database and every tenant whose registration is not deleted, suspended tenants included. It migrates a database that is behind the head, then runs the one-shot start-up against every tenant to refresh its permission catalogue and seeds. A failing tenant is reported and skipped ( src/cluster_erp/server/upgrade_tenants.py:62-115 ). If only one active tenant needs its seeds refreshed, run step 1 again with that

en.d: How three pytest files hold the module boundaries, the metadata-driven web rules, and the zero-finding lint and type-check state of Cluster ERP.
en.b: Cluster ERP holds its architecture rules in tests rather than in memory. This page explains the three test files that do it: tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py , tests/test_metadata_driven_rules.py , and tests/test_static_quality.py . It covers what each test reads, what it rejects, and what it does not see. The EventBus itself is explained on event bus . In short ¶ No module may import another module. The single exception is cluster_erp.modules.auth.guards ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:24 , tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:46-57 ). Every module folder has a module.py and at least one HTTP route of its own ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:60-72 ). The generic web engines do not compare against business module names ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:75-87 ). Rules that once lived in generic web code are now declared in module metadata, and tests check the metadata ( tests/test_metadata_driven_rules.py:1-5 ). Ruff and mypy must report zero findings across the package, not only on changed files ( tests/test_static_quality.py:1-11 ). How it works ¶ The boundary test reads source files as text or syntax trees. It does not import the modules. The metadata test imports each module and calls get_metadata . The static test runs Ruff and mypy as subprocesses. The flowchart shows which imports the boundary test allows for a file inside a module folder. flowchart TD file["Python file in src/cluster_erp/modules/X"] --> imp{"imports cluster_erp.modules.Y?"} imp -->|no| ok1["allowed"] imp -->|"Y equals X"| ok2["allowed"] imp -->|"name equals DOOR"| ok3["allowed"] imp -->|"any other Y"| fail["offender: path, line, import"] In prose: an import that does not name cluster_erp.modules.* passes. An import of the file's own module passes. An import of exactly cluster_erp.modules.auth.guards passes. Every other import of a module is listed as an offender with its path and line ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:48-56 ). Module isolation ¶ MODULE_NAMES is every folder under src/cluster_erp/modules/ that does not start with __ ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:25-27 ). _imports walks the syntax tree of each file and collects import and from ... import names with their line numbers ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:31-39 ). test_modules_exist guards against an empty scan: it requires at least 20 module folders ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:42-43 ). Every module is an application ¶ test_every_module_is_an_application_with_its_own_api first lists modules without a module.py . It then counts route decorators such as @router.get( in each module and lists modules with none ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:60-72 ). Generic engines and business names ¶ BUSINESS_MODULES is every module except auth , records , and logs ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:28 ). The test searches gen-list.js , gen-detail.js , gen-form.js , entity.js , and gen-settings.js for a comparison or case against one of those names ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:75-87 ). Metadata-driven rules ¶ tests/test_metadata_driven_rules.py loads every module's metadata through ModuleRegistry().discover() ( tests/test_metadata_driven_rules.py:23-29 ). Its checks are: Test Rule it holds Source test_every_is_active_column_declares_the_active_flag_formatter An is_active list column declares the active_flag formatter tests/test_metadata_driven_rules.py:36-48 test_guided_party_creation_is_declared_in_metadata Party creation offers the roles customer , supplier , and employee from metadata tests/test_metadata_driven_rules.py:51-60 test_record_documents_provider_is_declared_by_capability Exactly one module provides record_documents , and it is documents tests/test_metadata_driven_rules.py:63-74 test_assistant_starters_are_module_metadata_in_both_languages Assistant starters carry English and Turkish labels tests/test_metadata_d

en.d: The project's written engineering rules for Cluster ERP, each restated with the code or test that enforces it, or marked as not enforced by code.
en.b: This page restates the project's written engineering rules for Cluster ERP in plain words. Each rule names the code that implements it and the test or gate that enforces it. When nothing in the repository enforces a rule, the page says so. The reasons behind the largest rules are in the decision records ; this page is the lookup table. Scope and source ¶ The rules come from the project's written engineering rules. The enforcement column was produced by reading the tests in tests/ , the gates in .github/workflows/ci.yml , the configuration in pyproject.toml , and the cited source files at the verified commit. Defined in: the project's written engineering rules. Enforced in: tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py , tests/test_metadata_driven_rules.py , tests/test_static_quality.py , tests/test_e2e_db_isolation.py , other files in tests/ , and .github/workflows/ci.yml . Count: 34 rules in seven groups, counted as the rows of the tables below. Architecture and communication ¶ These rules keep modules independent of each other. The architecture boundaries page explains the tests in detail. Rule What the code does Enforced by Modules never import each other. The only allowed import is the permission door cluster_erp.modules.auth.guards . The boundary test parses every Python file under src/cluster_erp/modules/ and lists imports of another module. tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:24 , tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:46-57 Communication between modules goes through the EventBus , with frozen dataclass contracts. EventBus.emit fans an event out to every subscriber; EventBus.query calls the one handler of a query ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:83-102 ). Contracts are @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) classes, for example PartyRoleSet ( src/cluster_erp/core/contracts.py:47-55 ). The import ban above; a second query handler raises DuplicateQueryHandlerError ( src/cluster_erp/core/event_bus.py:78-79 ) Every module subclasses ModuleBase and follows its lifecycle. ModuleBase declares initialize , register_routes , register_events , shutdown , and get_metadata ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py:61-74 ). The registry calls the first three in that order ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:49-52 ). tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:60-72 requires a module.py and at least one route in every module The application layer may orchestrate several module services. It is not a module. server/routes/party_composite.py creates a party and its role facets in one transaction ( src/cluster_erp/server/routes/party_composite.py:1-10 ). Not enforced by a test. The boundary test scans only src/cluster_erp/modules/ ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:21 ). Each sub-module keeps its business logic in a service that takes an AsyncSession . Routes create the service and validate with Pydantic. Example: UiStateService ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/services.py:12-44 ) and its routes ( src/cluster_erp/modules/auth/ui_state/routes.py:21-39 ). Not determined from code. No test checks the layering. The schema comes from Alembic migrations. A module does not create tables itself. initialize imports the models only, for example src/cluster_erp/modules/records/module.py:36-37 . Alembic imports every module's models.py ( migrations/env.py:76-85 ). CI applies the full history and requires one head ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:113-117 ) A shipped migration is never edited. pyproject.toml calls migrations "frozen historical records" and relaxes only the line-length rule for them ( pyproject.toml:134-136 ). Not determined from code. No test compares migrations with a baseline. Data, keys, and money ¶ These rules fix how values and keys are stored. The platform section documents each mechanism. Rule What the code does Enforced by Money is Decimal , Numeric in the database, a string in JSON, and rounded with ROUND_HALF_EVEN . Read schemas serialise Decimal fields to strings ( src/cluster_erp/core/currencies.py:186-204 ). No file under sr

h: Why it is built this way
en.d: How the browser e2e battery of Cluster ERP runs every _e2e_*.mjs suite against one test instance, and how the shared helpers keep the test database isolated.
en.b: The e2e battery is the browser test run of Cluster ERP. One Node script, web-client/_run_battery.mjs , runs every _e2e_*.mjs suite in turn against one test instance and writes a log. Four shared modules give the suites their target address, their test account, their fixtures, and a clean home-screen layout. This page explains the run and the isolation rules; the suites themselves are listed in the e2e suite catalogue . In short ¶ The runner executes the suites one after another, because they share one server and one database ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:15-16 ). A suite passes only when it prints a line of the form N passed, M failed with M equal to zero; a suite that exits without that line counts as a failure ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:18-20 , web-client/_run_battery.mjs:110-119 ). The target address and the test database name come from one shared module, and the default target is the local test instance, not the development server ( web-client/_shared_e2e_base.mjs:4-17 , web-client/_shared_e2e_base.mjs:40-46 ). Suites that touch the home layout must use the ui-state guard, which saves and restores the test account's layout ( web-client/_ui_state_guard.mjs:1-11 , tests/test_e2e_db_isolation.py:177-200 ). CI does not run the battery; it runs on the staging node before a tag is cut ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:21-22 ). How it works ¶ The run ¶ The flowchart shows one battery run. flowchart TD start["node _run_battery.mjs"] --> list["collect _e2e_*.mjs, apply --filter and --exclude, sort"] list --> h1{"GET /health equals 200?"} h1 -->|no| stop["exit 2: server not answering"] h1 -->|yes| loop["spawn next suite with node"] loop --> wait{"result line printed before timeout?"} wait -->|yes| add["add passed and failed to totals"] wait -->|no| broken["count 1 failure, name the suite"] add --> more{"more suites?"} broken --> more more -->|yes| loop more -->|no| h2{"GET /health equals 200?"} h2 -->|no| inc["exit 2: run inconclusive"] h2 -->|yes| done["exit 0 if no failures, else 1"] In prose: The runner lists the files in web-client/ whose names start with _e2e_ and end with .mjs , applies --filter and --exclude , and sorts them ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:42-46 ). With --list it prints the list and stops ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:48-52 ). It asks the target's /health route. If the answer is not 200, it exits with code 2 before running anything ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:54-70 ). It starts each suite as a separate Node process and collects its output ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:78-99 ). A suite that runs longer than the timeout is killed and recorded as timed out. The default timeout is 900 seconds; --timeout changes it ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:39-41 , web-client/_run_battery.mjs:83-93 ). It reads the result line, adds the counts, and names every suite with failures or without a result line ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:110-119 ). At the end it asks /health again, writes the totals and the failing suites to the log, and exits with 0 when nothing failed, 1 when something failed, and 2 when the server stopped answering ( web-client/_run_battery.mjs:124-137 ). This page lists the settings and the commands. The web JavaScript has no lint gate in CI; Not determined from code whether one is run elsewhere. Scope and source ¶ Defined in: pyproject.toml (sections [tool.mypy] , [[tool.mypy.overrides]] , [tool.ruff] , [tool.ruff.lint] , [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores] ). Count: 9 selected Ruff rule families, 2 ignored rules, and 9 per-file ignore entries, counted from pyproject.toml:123-149 . Tool versions ¶ The dev extra pins both tools. A comment says the zero-finding state is measured against these versions and that raising a pin is a deliberate change with its own re-run ( pyproject.toml:75-78 ). h: Step 4: Write schemas, services, and routes
en.d: A guided walk from an empty folder to a registered Cluster ERP backend module with models, routes, metadata, and EventBus handlers.
en.b: This tutorial takes a developer from an empty folder under src/cluster_erp/modules/ to a module that the server loads, that serves routes, that publishes metadata to the clients, and that talks to other modules over the EventBus. It uses the small records module as the worked example. It does not cover web screens in detail; for those see add a screen with metadata . Note Execution status: not executed by the writer; steps derived from src/cluster_erp/core/module_base.py , src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py , src/cluster_erp/modules/records/ , src/cluster_erp/config/settings.py , migrations/env.py , and tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py . What you will build ¶ At the end you have a package src/cluster_erp/modules/<module_name>/ with a module.py whose class Module subclasses ModuleBase . The server discovers it at start-up, calls its lifecycle methods, mounts its routes under /api/v1/<module_name> , and includes its metadata in /api/v1/_meta . The architecture tests pass. Background on the contract is on module lifecycle . The sequence diagram shows the calls the server makes into a module. sequenceDiagram participant App as server/app.py lifespan participant Reg as ModuleRegistry participant Mod as Module App->>Reg: load_all(app, bus, database, enabled_modules) Reg->>Mod: initialize(database) Reg->>Mod: register_routes(app) Reg->>Mod: register_events(bus) App->>Mod: get_metadata() for /api/v1/_meta App->>Reg: shutdown_all() Reg->>Mod: shutdown() In prose: at start-up the lifespan calls load_all with the list of enabled modules ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:140 ). For each name the registry imports cluster_erp.modules.<name>.module , creates Module() , and calls initialize , register_routes , and register_events in that order ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:39-52 ). The metadata route reads get_metadata of every loaded module through effective_module_meta ( src/cluster_erp/server/app.py:1537-1538 ). At shutdown the registry calls shutdown on every module and logs, but does not raise, an error ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:74-80 ). Before you start ¶ A working checkout and database, as in local development setup . Python 3.12 or later ( pyproject.toml:9 ). The development tools from the dev extra: mypy, pytest, and Ruff ( pyproject.toml:79-84 ). Step 1: Create the package ¶ Create src/cluster_erp/modules/<module_name>/ with an __init__.py . The registry treats every package under cluster_erp.modules as a module candidate ( src/cluster_erp/core/module_registry.py:26-30 ). The folder name becomes the module name that the boundary test checks ( tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:25-27 ). Keep one sub-folder per sub-module, each with models.py , schemas.py , services.py , and routes.py , as in src/cluster_erp/modules/records/deactivation_reasons/ . Add a top-level models.py that imports every sub-module model. Alembic imports exactly that file for each module ( migrations/env.py:76-85 ); src/cluster_erp/modules/records/models.py is an example. Step 2: Define the models ¶ Subclass BaseModel from cluster_erp.core.models . You then get a ULID primary key, the tenant column, the audit columns, the soft-delete columns, and the version counter ( src/cluster_erp/core/models.py:17-78 ). Declare uniqueness only on live rows with a partial index, as DeactivationReason does ( src/cluster_erp/modules/records/deactivation_reasons/models.py:16-25 ). Money columns use Numeric and Decimal ; see money and Decimal . Step 3: Add the migration ¶ The business schema comes only from the Alembic history; a module never creates tables itself. Add a revision under migrations/versions/ . The procedure, the naming, and the checks are on database migrations . CI applies the whole history to an empty database and requires exactly one head ( .github/workflows/ci.yml:113-117 ). en.d: How to add or update a page of the Cluster ERP wiki under the documentation standard, with its Turkish twin, and build the static HTML site.
en.b: This guide adds a new page to the wiki in docs/wiki/ , or updates an existing one, so that it meets the documentation standard ( docs/wiki/_standard/DOC_STANDARD.md ) and builds into the static HTML site. It covers placement, front matter, citations, admonitions, diagrams, the Turkish twin, and the build script docs/wiki/_build/build.py . The full rules are in the standard and the style checklist ( docs/wiki/_standard/STYLE_CHECKLIST.md ); this page is the working sequence. Note Execution status: not executed by the writer; steps derived from docs/wiki/_standard/DOC_STANDARD.md , docs/wiki/_standard/INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md , and docs/wiki/_build/build.py . Prerequisites ¶ Read the documentation standard ( docs/wiki/_standard/DOC_STANDARD.md ) and the information architecture ( docs/wiki/_standard/INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md ). For the build: Python with the packages markdown , pygments , and yaml ( docs/wiki/_build/build.py:22-23 , docs/wiki/_build/build.py:37-41 ). For diagrams: the Mermaid package installed with npm install in docs/wiki/_build/ ( docs/wiki/_build/package.json , docs/wiki/_build/build.py:524-528 ). Steps ¶ Find the row for the page in the information architecture. It gives the folder, the file name, and the page type. If no row fits, add one and name it in your change. Copy the template for the page type from docs/wiki/_standard/templates/ and its .tr.md twin. A decision record uses the explanation template with the headings "Context", "Decision", "Consequences", "Where the code enforces it", and "Related pages". Fill the front matter. title , description , lang , type , section , stage , verified_commit , and verified_date are mandatory; audience is optional. The build parses the block as YAML and stops with an error when it does not parse ( docs/wiki/_build/build.py:181-194 ). ```yaml title: Event bus description: How modules exchange events and queries through the EventBus without importing each other. lang: en type: explanation section: platform stage: 2 audience: developer verified_commit: 7793ff4 verified_date: 2026-11-09 ``` Write one H1 equal to the title, then a summary of two to four sentences. The build removes the first H1 from the body and draws the title in the page header instead ( docs/wiki/_build/build.py:337-338 ). Open every file you describe and cite it inline as path:line or path:start-end , with the symbol name when one exists. Where the code gives no answer, write "Not determined from code." and say what you searched. Write a discrepancy warning when the code and the project's written engineering rules disagree. Use only the three admonitions > **Note:** , > **Warning:** , and > **Tip:** . The build turns them, and their Turkish forms Not , Uyarı , and İpucu , into styled callouts ( docs/wiki/_build/build.py:121-125 , docs/wiki/_build/build.py:278-299 ). Draw diagrams as mermaid fenced blocks and repeat their content in prose. The build keeps these blocks out of the Markdown renderer and hands them to Mermaid in the browser ( docs/wiki/_build/build.py:225-246 ). Link other pages with relative paths to .md files. The build rewrites them to .html and reports every link whose target page does not exist ( docs/wiki/_build/build.py:249-275 ). Turkish pages link to .tr.md files. Add new terms to the "Terms introduced" table, then the "Related pages" list, then the footer line with the same commit and date as the front matter. Write the Turkish twin name.tr.md in the same folder with the same structure: the same headings, tables, rows, admonitions, code blocks, and citations. The build pairs files by stem and offers a language switch ( docs/wiki/_build/build.py:197-200 , docs/wiki/_build/build.py:555-556 ). Build the site from the repository root: bash python docs/wiki/_build/build.py The output goes to docs/wiki/_site ; --out chooses another folder and --site-root adds links back to a product page ( docs/wiki/_build/build.py:613-617 ).
